summary: Serializes and restores debugger pane layouts and dock axis to a key-value store, mapping active items to DebuggerPaneItem variants. Provides helpers to build and deserialize pane hierarchies, wiring subscriptions and creating views for each supported pane.

Manages a running debug session entity, wiring the RunningState and optional serialized layout to render and focus the session UI. Exposes session metadata, stack trace view creation, shutdown, and workspace follow/dedup integrations.

Renders a multibuffer editor showing stack frames’ source excerpts, tracks selection to navigate frames, and highlights active frames. Asynchronously opens buffers based on frames, computes context ranges, and auto-scrolls to selected anchors.

Test utilities to initialize a workspace with debugger and terminal panels and start mock debug sessions. Provides helpers to access active debug session panels and start sessions with custom adapter configuration.

Implements the debugger console UI with a read-only output editor and an input query bar, including ANSI color parsing and highlighting of streamed OutputEvent spans. Integrates completions, focus behavior, history, and reacts to stack frame changes.
Displays and updates a list of loaded sources from a Session, reacting to session events. Uses a ListState to efficiently render entries and track focus.

Interactive memory viewer that renders uniform lists of memory cells, supports address jumps, selection via drag, scrolling, and context menus. Tracks view state (base row, width, selection), integrates with session for reads and data breakpoints.

Renders a scrollable list of modules from a debug session, supporting selection, keyboard navigation, and opening module paths in the workspace. Rebuilds entries on session events and handles asynchronous buffer opening.

Builds and filters stack frame entries (normal, labels, collapsed) from session data, persists filter choice, and manages selection/opened frame state. Debounces refreshes on session events and provides flattened views of frames for other components.

Client for DeepSeek chat completions API, defining models, request/response schemas, tool-call streaming, and a streaming completion function over SSE-like lines. Encapsulates roles, tool definitions, usage accounting, and error handling.

Realtime dual-stage denoising engine using embedded ONNX models and FFT/IFFT to compute magnitude masks and reconstruct signals. Manages model memory tensors and block processing with overlap-add and normalization.

Wraps the denoise engine as a rodio Source with a worker thread, maintaining a fixed-latency pipeline that can be enabled/disabled seamlessly. Buffers sub-blocks, handles startup and mid-audio enabling, and propagates denoised audio chunks.

Buffer-focused diagnostics editor that renders excerpts containing diagnostics, subscribes to project/editor events, and updates highlights/blocks efficiently. Provides deployment from workspace, focus handling, and controls for including warnings.

Transforms grouped diagnostics into rendered markdown blocks with severity styling and inline navigation links, integrating with editor custom block rendering. Supports hover rendering and link handling to jump between related diagnostics.

Initializes diagnostics integration and defines a project-wide diagnostics editor that aggregates excerpts across files, updates on project events with debounce, and toggles warning inclusion and refresh behavior. Wires global settings, toolbar, and rendering state.

Status bar indicator showing error/warning counts and next diagnostic preview, subscribing to project/editor changes with timed updates. Provides click actions to open diagnostics and navigate to next diagnostic.

Toolbar controls for diagnostics editors, exposing toggle warnings, refresh/stop update actions, and querying editor state via a trait object. Adjusts icon states and button enablement based on editor state.

MdBook preprocessor that injects metadata and templates actions/keybindings, validating against registered app actions and keymaps. Outputs transformed book JSON or runs a postprocessing mode, surfacing errors with ANSI output.

Defines the EditPredictionProvider trait and handle, modeling local edits or jump suggestions along with data collection state and usage reporting. Standardizes provider capabilities and lifecycle (refresh/cycle/accept/discard) across implementations.

Status button UI for edit prediction providers (Copilot/Supermaven/Zed), reflecting provider statuses, showing menus, and switching providers/settings. Integrates with workspace notifications and user settings, gating by AI disablement.

Data model for declarations extracted from outlines, including identifiers, ranges, and truncated text/signatures for file or buffer-backed items. Provides helpers to compute signature ranges within item text and construct declarations from outlines.

Scores declarations against the current excerpt using text similarity (jaccard/overlap) and reference proximity, ranking by density and relevance. Filters declarations by file proximity and collects score components for downstream usage.

Builds edit prediction context around the cursor by selecting an excerpt, gathering identifiers/references, and scoring candidate declarations via a syntax index. Offers async gathering with optional SyntaxIndex and produces a structured context with occurrences.

Selects an excerpt around the cursor using TreeSitter node boundaries with fallback to line-based expansion, targeting byte budgets and before/after ratios. Includes parent signatures via SyntaxIndex and tracks total size for prompt planning.

Extracts outline declarations from syntax maps across languages, capturing name, item, and signature ranges and computing parent relationships by nesting. Provides iterators to collect overlapping declarations efficiently.

Finds identifier references in an excerpt and parent signatures using highlight queries, grouping by Identifier and tagging regions (Nearby/Breadcrumb). Deduplicates overlapping captures and normalizes ranges to buffer coordinates.

Project-wide syntax index that tracks declarations per file/buffer and identifiers, parallel-indexing files and reacting to worktree/buffer events. Exposes queries for declarations containing ranges and orchestrates background updates via tasks and channels.

Implements occurrence multiset and similarity metrics (jaccard, weighted variants, overlap), tokenizing identifiers by case/delimiters and hashing entries. Provides utility functions to compare excerpt and declaration texts efficiently.

Criterion benchmarks measuring performance of display map conversions (to_tab_point/to_fold_point) over generated buffers with inlays and folds. Sets up test app context and snapshot pipelines for reproducible runs.

Benchmarks editor render and multi-cursor edit flows on randomized buffers, measuring layout/prepaint/paint and common edit actions. Initializes app context with settings and assets to simulate realistic rendering.

Defines the editor’s action schema (navigation, selection, deletion, folding, completions, diagnostics, etc.) with serde-validated config and gpui Action registration. Serves as the central command interface driving editor behavior.
Manages cursor blinking state with global setting observation, pause/resume timers, and visibility toggling. Coordinates blink epochs to avoid race conditions and ensures updates notify the UI.

Integrates clangd-specific LSP extensions to switch between source/header files, selecting appropriate servers and issuing requests via collab or local channels. Registers related actions when C/C++ is present and opens results in the workspace.

Tests for completion sorting and fuzzy matching rules, asserting precedence among kinds, sort_text, snippets, positions, and exact matches. Validates the CompletionsMenu behavior with constructed Completion items.

Tests edit prediction integration with the editor, including local edit application, jump target behavior, invalidation rules, and provider capability gating. Uses a fake provider to simulate suggestions and acceptance.

Defines editor settings model mapping VSCode-like defaults to runtime behavior (cursor blink, minimap, scrollbars, diagnostics, search, etc.). Provides conversion from SettingsContent and utility traits for scrollbar visibility and Jupyter gating.

Renders UI controls for editor/font settings (family, size, weight, ligatures) and toggles (inline blame, line numbers) using editable settings hooks. Applies changes by updating SettingsContent through menu and checkbox interactions.

Highlights matching bracket pairs around the cursor using buffer bracket queries, respecting cursor shapes and empty selections. Applies themed background highlights and includes tests verifying behavior across contexts.

Computes and highlights active indent guides within the visible range, tracking a background-resolved enclosing indent region near the cursor. Filters guides inside folds and recalculates when cursor moves or indent changes.

Detects JSX-like open tags on input and generates auto-close edits, heuristically determining if a tag is already closed by scanning ancestor elements. Handles grammar alternates for tag names and navigates syntax nodes safely under error correction.

Refreshes linked editing ranges by querying language servers for related regions around current selections, debouncing and aggregating sibling ranges per buffer. Stores sorted non-overlapping anchor ranges for synchronized edits.

Fetches and caches document color ranges from LSP per visible buffer and renders them as inlays or background/border highlights based on settings. Manages cache versions, splice operations for inlays, and conversion to display coordinates.

Utilities to find specific language servers for selections and collect LSP-provided runnables across buffers with timeouts. Builds TaskContext from worktree/env, resolves tasks/locations, and groups by server/language.

Builds and deploys the editor context menu at a screen or editor-anchored position, moving the cursor if needed and wiring dismiss on blur or selection change. Provides actions for navigation, code actions, clipboard, and reveal/open operations.

Implements display-level movement and boundary calculations (left/right/up/down, line start/end, word boundaries) respecting soft wraps, goals, and text layout. Provides helper types and algorithms to compute positions across folds and variable-width glyphs.

Defines an SQLite-backed domain for persisting editor state (paths, scroll positions, contents, language, mtime, selections, folds) with migrations. Exposes queries to save/load serialized editors and associated ranges, batching for large writes.

Editor view showing proposed changes by composing branch buffers and diffs against base buffers, refreshing diffs on edits with debounce. Supports resetting locations, toolbar integration, and semantics provider delegation outside edited regions.

Hooks Rust Analyzer-specific actions (go to parent module, expand macro, open docs, flycheck control), issuing collab or local requests and rendering results. Registers actions based on server availability and language presence.

Manages editor scrolling state and autoscroll behavior, enforcing beyond-last-line policies, saving scroll positions, and showing scrollbars with auto-hide. Tracks ongoing scroll axis locking, anchors, visible counts, and integrates with DB persistence.

Defines the Action trait and actions! macro for declaring keyboard-driven actions, including JSON construction, partial equality, documentation, and deprecation metadata. Maintains a global ActionRegistry with builders, schemas, deprecated aliases, and type erasure to resolve actions by name. Provides structured errors for building actions from keymaps.

Implements a bump-allocated Arena with fixed-size chunks for fast per-frame allocations and drop tracking, returning ArenaBox references validated against clears. Handles alignment, growth, and safe deallocation, with a use-after-clear guard. Supports mapping to sub-objects and deref operations for mutable access.

Provides a Resource abstraction (URI, Path, Embedded) and an Asset trait for async loading tied to App, with AssetLogger to log errors from Result outputs. Includes a fast non-crypto hash utility for asset identification. Enables standardized asynchronous asset retrieval across sources.

Defines AssetSource for loading/listing binary assets and a RenderImage cache that tracks frames, sizes, delays, and a unique ImageId with scale factor. Supports obtaining raw BGRA bytes, frame counts, and render size adjusted for scale. Facilitates efficient image caching for rendering.

Implements a tree that assigns draw orders to axis-aligned bounds via surface-area heuristics and intersection tracking, balancing the tree and minimizing overlap conflicts. Insert updates union bounds and propagates max ordering for efficient retrieval. Used to determine non-overlapping paint layering.

Defines Rgba and Hsla color types with conversions, blending, serde/schemars integration, and robust hex parsing with detailed errors. Includes premultiplied alpha handling and hashing/display implementations. Supports color operations across the UI styling subsystem.

Provides default light/dark color palettes and maps them to window appearance, exposing global access via GlobalColors and traits. Enables consistent styling defaults for text, backgrounds, borders, and containers. Bridges appearance to theme selection in the App.

Defines the core Element lifecycle (request_layout, prepaint, paint) with per-phase state, IDs, and source locations, along with IntoElement, Render, and RenderOnce abstractions. Supports components, fluent builder composition, and dynamic AnyElement conversion for layout and painting orchestration. Forms the backbone of GPUI’s immediate/retained rendering pipeline.

Implements foreground and background executors integrated with a PlatformDispatcher, providing Task futures with detach/log utilities and blocking helpers. Enforces thread affinity for foreground tasks and deterministic test scheduling with labeled priorities. Serves as the async runtime underpinning GPUI’s event-driven architecture.

Defines a Global marker trait and helper traits to read/update/set globals through App contexts with BorrowAppContext. Encapsulates type-safe global state access and controlled mutation patterns. Enables modular system-wide state integration.

Crate root that documents GPUI’s architecture, declares modules, and re-exports key traits and types for public consumption. Introduces AppContext and VisualContext traits to unify entity, window, global, and async operations across contexts. Acts as the central entry point and architectural hub.

Defines EntityInputHandler for text input semantics and an ElementInputHandler adapter that delegates input handling to view entities during painting. Integrates with Window::handle_input to compute ranges, replacements, selection, and geometry. Provides canonical input bridging for editors and text fields.

Introduces InspectorElementId and conditional inspector components that track active element selection, hover/pick mode, and per-type state. Provides a registry to render inspector UIs for stored element states via type-based dispatch. Supports debug-time introspection of elements and their lifecycles.

Defines typed input events (keys, modifiers, mouse, clicks) and their conversion to platform inputs, plus utility methods for click semantics. Encapsulates buttons, navigation, and touch phases with sealed traits for controlled implementations. Supplies the event model feeding interaction handling.

Implements DispatchTree to collect key/action listeners with context stacks, focus tracking, and view associations, handling node reuse and replay. Coordinates keybinding resolution across nested views and dispatch phases using the Keymap and ActionRegistry. Central to action-based keyboard interaction and precedence.

Manages key bindings with versioning, indexing by action type, and NoAction overrides, providing matching algorithms with context predicates and precedence. Produces matched/pending bindings and filters disabled rules based on context depth. Powers user and built-in keymaps for action invocation.

Wraps lyon to build, transform, and tessellate stroke/fill paths into GPU-ready meshes, supporting dash arrays and geometric conversions. Applies transforms (translate/scale/rotate) and outputs Path primitives for rendering. Bridges vector path construction to the renderer.

Collects primitives and paint operations, computes insertion orders using a BoundsTree, and batches/sorts primitives by draw order for rendering. Supports layer push/pop, clipping via content masks, and replay from previous scenes. Forms the render command buffer and final batching pipeline.

Provides SharedString backed by ArcCow for cheap cloning across tasks with serde/schemars support and broad conversions. Implements comparisons and display while preserving borrowed vs owned optimization. Serves as a lightweight shared string utility.

Defines the Styled trait with Tailwind-like style helpers and macros to refine StyleRefinement and TextStyleRefinement on elements. Offers fluent APIs for layout, text, flex/grid, overflow, borders, cursor, and shadows. Enables declarative styling integrated with GPUI elements.

Implements a SubscriberSet keyed by emitters with activation semantics, safe retention, and removal handling during callback iteration. Provides a Subscription handle that unsubscribes on drop, supports detach and join. Facilitates robust pub-sub patterns within GPUI internals.

SVG renderer that loads assets from an AssetSource and uses usvg/resvg to render to pixmaps or alpha masks with a smooth scale factor. Configures a font resolver and ensures non-zero sizes. Supplies scalable vector rendering for icons and graphics.

Defines per-project settings including language-wide defaults, worktree file scanning, LSP/DAP configuration, context servers, direnv loading, slash commands, and custom git hosting providers. Provides detailed structs like LspSettings with defaults and ContextServerCommand with redacted env in Debug. Includes Git UI settings and helpers for enabling/disabling context servers.

Configures terminal behavior and appearance, including shell selection, working directory, fonts, line height, cursor style and blink, environment overrides, venv detection, scrollback, toolbar/scrollbar visibility, and contrast minimums. Supplies enums and helpers to compute line heights and rendering attributes.

Provides theme settings for UI and editor fonts, weights, features, line heights, and theme/icon selection (static or dynamic) with system appearance. Supports UI density, unnecessary code fade, and per-theme overrides with validation for custom line heights.

Declares workspace-level settings controlling pane split directions, dock layout, autosave and restore behavior, system dialogs, window/tab behavior, command aliases, and UI padding. Includes tab item settings and preview tabs configuration with enums tailoring close button behavior and diagnostics indicators.
Procedural macro deriving MergeFrom by recursively merging all struct fields or cloning enums. Generates impls that call merge_from on nested fields and rejects unions.

Implements a modal picker to switch active settings profiles, with fuzzy matching and immediate application by setting a global ActiveSettingsProfileName. Restores the original profile if dismissed without confirmation.

Standalone example application that initializes settings UI, watches the user settings file for live updates, and opens a settings editor in a fake local project/worktree. Binds keymaps and sets up necessary subsystems.

Defines a SettingsEditor component wrapping a single-line editor with optional placeholder and confirm callback, rendering a styled container. On confirm, it reads the current text and invokes the handler.

Parses LSP snippet syntax into plain text and tabstops, supporting placeholders, choice lists, nested structures, and escapes. Produces ranges per tabstop and ensures a final tabstop at the end when not explicitly provided.
Deserializes VS Code snippet files and generates JSON schema, supporting single or list forms for prefix/body/description. Provides a flexible list-or-direct type with display helpers.

Watches snippet directories and aggregates snippets by language or globally, parsing VS snippets into internal structures and merging registry/global/user sources. Uses a global watcher and async processing of file changes.
Global registry storing preloaded snippets keyed by language kind, with registration from file contents and retrieval APIs. Acts as an in-memory extension-provided snippet source.
Provides UI actions to configure snippets by scope via a fuzzy picker, opening the appropriate JSON snippet file or the snippets folder. Displays language icons and handles modal lifecycle.

Defines traits and implementations to bind Rust values to SQLite statements and read columns back, covering primitives, blobs, strings, options, arrays, and paths. Ensures type-safe binding/column extraction with error contexts.

Manages SQLite connections including opening with flags, backups, and compile-time SQL syntax checking with special handling for ALTER TABLE via a temporary in-memory DB. Tracks write capability, surfaces last errors, and cleans up on drop.
Defines Domain and Migrator traits for namespaced database migrations, with blanket impls to compose multiple domains. Delegates migration execution to the connection.

Runs eager, formatted SQL migrations tracked in a migrations table and validates against stored text, with a hook to allow changes. Cleans up orphaned foreign key references post-migration and uses savepoints for safety.
Provides helpers to execute operations within SQLite savepoints, releasing on success or rolling back on error or optional None. Includes tests demonstrating nested savepoints and rollback behavior.

Wraps prepared SQLite statements (including multiple statements) with typed binding and column access, stepping across statements and enforcing read-only operations on non-writable connections. Offers blob/text/number accessors and type inspection.

Builds a thread-safe facade that serializes writes per database URI via background queues, runs migrations with retries and foreign key toggling, and exposes async write APIs while derefing to a read-only per-thread connection. Supports custom queue constructors and initialization queries.
Convenience APIs on Connection to prepare typed closures for exec and selects with or without bindings, integrating Bind and Column traits. Simplifies common query patterns and error handling.

Proc macro that formats SQL and performs compile-time syntax checks against SQLite, mapping token spans to error offsets for precise diagnostics. Uses a lazy ThreadSafeConnection and custom token stream flattening to track positions.
Utility components for building storybook-style demo pages, including containers, titles, sections, items, and layout helpers. Provides consistent styling and separators.
Enumerates component stories and resolves a selected story from CLI input, integrating with clap ValueEnum. Produces views for each story and caches available selectors.

Main entry for the storybook app that initializes themes, assets, settings, and opens a window to render the selected story. Loads embedded fonts, binds keys, sets menus, and supports fuzzy selection.
Demonstrates an auto-height editor with basic keybindings and soft wrap configuration. Renders the editor in a simple view.
Showcases various cursor styles by rendering labeled boxes with different cursor behaviors. Useful for visual verification of cursor classes.
Demonstrates focus handling, keybinding contexts, and focus/blur event subscriptions across nested views, changing background colors on focus. Logs dispatched actions and key events.
Displays indent guides alongside a uniform list, computing per-item depths and applying decoration with configurable colors. Illustrates indentation visuals within scrolling lists.
Aggregates and renders all component stories in a scrollable 'kitchen sink' view for comprehensive UI inspection. Adds padding to avoid crowding.
Demonstrates horizontal and vertical overflow scrolling with repeated child elements. Serves as a visual test for scroll behavior.
Minimal picker demo implementing a delegate with fuzzy matching, selection cycling, and confirm/dismiss actions, wired to typical keybindings. Renders matched items with labels.
Renders a grid of colored blocks with tooltips and nested scroll areas to test scrolling interactions. Alternates colors and adds inner overflow regions.
Demonstrates text rendering scenarios including wrapping, horizontal flex behavior, and interactive text with highlighted ranges and click callbacks. Provides usage snippets.
Shows the WithRemSize utility by nesting examples with different rem sizes and border colors, displaying computed pixel equivalence. Useful for verifying rem-based layouts.

Implements a streaming diff algorithm using a dynamic programming matrix that penalizes insertions/deletions and boosts equal runs, then backtracks to produce char-level operations. Includes a line-oriented diff that tracks inserted/deleted rows against a rope.

Provides a Cursor over SumTree that supports seeking by dimensions, iterating next/prev across leaves, and maintaining position summaries. Handles traversal with filters and computes start/end positions robustly.

Defines a B+ tree-like SumTree storing items with per-subtree summaries and multiple dimensions, with constructors from iterators and parallel sources. Supports seeking, editing, and combining summaries to navigate and manipulate ordered data.

Builds an ordered TreeMap/TreeSet atop SumTree enabling key-based navigation and operations like insert, remove, extend, retain, and closest lookup. Adapts seek targets and summaries to keys and provides iterable views.

Defines the message protocol for communicating with the Supermaven agent, including outbound state updates and inbound responses for completions, tasks, popups, activation, and service tier. Structures are serde-serializable and version-tolerant.

Manages the Supermaven agent lifecycle by downloading/spawning the binary, sending API credentials, tracking completion states per buffer, and producing completions based on current cursor and buffer changes. Integrates with settings and exposes actions like sign out.

Implements EditPredictionProvider for Supermaven with debounced updates and a grapheme-aware diff that inserts inlays for missing completion text. Caches state per buffer, validates cursor position, and suggests edits derived from completion text.

Provides HTTP APIs to manage Supermaven external users and to download and cache the agent binary, handling platform/arch selection, versioned paths, and executable permissions. Cleans older binaries and surfaces server/client errors.

Workspace item that previews SVG files, either fixed to a given editor or following the active SVG editor. Listens for buffer saves and file handle changes to invalidate cached images and reloads, with actions to open in panes.

Collects and formats system specifications including app version/channel, OS, memory, architecture, commit SHA, and GPU details, exposing an action to copy to clipboard. Retrieves GPU info with platform-specific methods.

Implements a modal tab switcher with fuzzy matching across panes or current pane, modifier-driven confirm behavior, and the ability to close the selected item. Renders decorated icons with Git and diagnostic indicators and manages original selection restoration.

Tests tab switcher behavior for selection ordering, cycling via actions, closing selected items, and modifier-release activation, ensuring correct UI and focus outcomes. Uses a fake project and buffers to simulate panes.

Models debug task configurations for adapters, supporting launch and attach requests with serde and conversions to/from proto types. Defines build task references/templates and generates JSON schema with adapter-specific extensions.
Provides a deserializer ensuring arrays contain non-empty strings, returning detailed errors for empty entries. Used to validate configuration inputs.

Builds shell commands across various shells, handling interactive flags, variable escaping, stdin redirection, and user-facing command labels. Adapts to shell-specific argument conventions with tests for correctness.

Implements a tracked file source that deserializes task templates on change and notifies observers, retaining the latest parsed state. Supports conversion from alternate types and stops polling when no observers remain.

Defines core task infrastructure including task IDs, SpawnInTerminal, ResolvedTask metadata, variable naming conventions, and exports for templates and adapters. Manages resolved labels, substituted variables, and terminal spawn details.

UI component that renders Zed AI onboarding for edit predictions, detects if the user is on a free plan to optionally offer GitHub Copilot, and wires callbacks to continue with either provider. It composes ZedAiOnboarding and conditionally displays a Copilot configuration/use button based on setup state.

Centralized UI definitions that render feature lists for Free, Pro Trial, and Pro plans with v1/v2 differences and optional pricing/period notes. It standardizes how plan benefits are presented across the app.

Catalog of Anthropic models and modes, mapping display IDs to request IDs, display names, and cache configurations, with support for custom models and conversion to/from generic model modes. It provides robust parsing of model identifiers and normalizes API targets across model versions.

Implements a socket-based askpass flow using a temporary script and Unix listener to relay prompts and passwords between processes, with Windows-specific handling of secrets and an execution timeout. It coordinates prompting via AskPassDelegate and maintains session lifecycle to avoid SSH errors.

Provides an EncryptedPassword type with platform-specific in-memory encryption (Windows CryptProtectMemory) and zeroization on drop, exposing controlled decryption utilities. It integrates with process environment setup and proto conversions without leaking plaintext by default.

Embedded asset loader using RustEmbed that exposes an AssetSource for fonts, icons, images, themes, and sounds, plus helpers to load fonts into the app’s text system. It isolates asset access to speed incremental builds.

Test suite validating AssistantContext message insertion, splitting, merging across edits, and undo/redo of merges with precise anchor range tracking. It ensures buffer edits map correctly to message boundaries and offsets.

Central store orchestrating assistant context lifecycle, synchronization, and RPC interactions (advertise/open/create/update/synchronize) while watching the contexts directory and project state. It bridges local and host contexts, manages slash command integration, and enforces collab constraints.

Core framework for slash commands defining the SlashCommand trait, argument completion flow, and a streaming model for command output via SlashCommandEvent and SlashCommandOutput. It includes utilities to ensure valid section ranges and reconstruct outputs from event streams.

Adapter enabling extensions to register/unregister slash commands via the ExtensionHost, bridging LspAdapterDelegate to an Extension WorktreeDelegate. It implements a SlashCommand that forwards completion and execution to extension-provided handlers and streams results back.
Thread-safe global registry managing registered and featured slash commands by name. It provides lookup, insertion, removal, and access to the global registry instance.

Per-assistant working set that merges context-server-provided commands with the global registry, assigns IDs, and maintains name-to-command mapping. It recomputes its internal indexes when commands change for fast lookup.

Slash command that inspects Cargo.toml to insert workspace or package metadata, listing members, default members, and dependencies. It reads from the project filesystem and produces a single labeled section summarizing the project.

Slash command that integrates with a Context Server to complete arguments and retrieve prompt content, enforcing single-argument constraints and normalizing line endings. It concatenates user messages from the server into a labeled section and supports argument completion via server RPC.
Slash command that inserts a list of default prompts from the PromptStore as runnable slash commands in text. It streams a single labeled section and enables running embedded commands.

Slash command that re-runs file insertions and diffs them against previous sections to reinsert only changed file outputs. It aggregates new outputs, preserves sections, and fails if no changes are detected.

Slash command that inserts project diagnostics, with fuzzy path and flag completion including an --include-warnings option. It collects summaries across files, filters by path matcher, and builds a structured output section per match.

Slash command that fetches a URL via the HTTP client, detects content type, converts HTML to markdown (including Wikipedia-specific handlers), and returns plaintext or pretty-printed JSON. It labels the section with the URL and errors on empty content or client errors.

Slash command that inserts files and directories using fuzzy path matching, generating structured sections with code fences, directory folding, and streaming events. It provides rich argument completions with labeled suggestions and supports glob-like matching across worktrees.
Slash command that inserts the current date and time as a single labeled section. It requires no arguments and returns a fixed formatted string.

Slash command that searches the PromptStore for a prompt by title, supports completion with immediate run, and inserts its body while allowing embedded commands to run. It safeguards edge cases by prefixing a newline if the body starts with a slash.

Slash command that captures the active editor’s selections and emits sections with either blockquoted markdown or code-fenced excerpts, optionally including symbol breadcrumbs. It computes titles with file paths and line ranges and streams multiple selection sections.
Example slash command demonstrating streaming by emitting multiple labeled sections over time using timers. It showcases the event-based output model without requiring arguments.
Slash command that extracts and inserts an outline of symbols for the active editor tab. It labels output with the file path and returns a simple list of symbol names as a single section.

Explains two Cloudflare Workers used to serve install assets and proxy docs, how they are deployed via GitHub Actions on main, and how to test locally with wrangler. This supports the website delivery layer rather than core editor functionality.

Brief guide for constructing query test data and running examples, suggesting importing the generated SQLite DB into sqliteonline.com for inspection. Serves as a developer helper for the database crate.

Describes running the eval crate and its Explorer tool that renders agent threads into a navigable HTML view, with optional .env for secrets. Supports evaluating and visualizing agent behavior outside the core editor flow.
CLI to print various Zed schemas (e.g., theme, icon_theme) to stdout for tooling and inspection. Serves as a small utility supporting schema-driven parts of the system.
Command to import/convert external theme JSON into Zed’s theme format. A minor tool aiding theme ecosystem integration.
Notes the vendored snapshot of the LiveKit protocol repository and its pinned revision. Documents provenance for a third-party protocol dependency used by collaboration features.
Describes a simple test extension used by the extension crate’s tests, originally based on the Gleam extension. Primarily a fixture for internal testing.

Guidelines for proposing changes, reviewer expectations, and project scope boundaries, plus a bird’s‑eye overview of core crates and their roles in Zed’s architecture. Helps contributors align with the codebase structure and standards.

Top-level overview of Zed, installation and development platform status, build docs links, contribution entry points, and licensing compliance via cargo-about. Orients users and contributors to the project and its CI requirements.

Describes the mdBook-based docs pipeline, custom pre/postprocessor integration with crates, deployment to Cloudflare Pages via CI, and conventions for keybinding/action references. Explains the docs’ build architecture and constraints.

Explains the official extensions housed in-repo, how they relate to built-in languages, dev workflows, and the process for version bumps and publishing to the external extensions registry. Connects extension packaging with the broader release process.
SIL Open Font License 1.1 for IBM Plex Sans describing usage, modification, and redistribution terms. Legal documentation for bundled font assets.
MIT License for the Ayu theme assets bundled with Zed. Legal notice for third-party theme content.
MIT License placeholder for the Gruvbox theme assets. Legal notice for third-party theme content.
MIT License for the One theme assets originating from GitHub. Legal notice for third-party theme content.

Overview of the collaboration server powering collab.zed.dev, including local development (Postgres bootstrap, foreman flows), deployment via Kubernetes with tag-based releases, and migrations. Central to Zed’s real-time collaboration architecture.
Real-time audio denoising using a DTLN LSTM model via Candle, with example integration into a Rodio pipeline and acknowledgements. Supports higher‑quality voice in collaborative features.

Documentation for writing Zed extensions in Rust, covering manifest format, WASI/WASM build setup, extension trait registration, dev installation, and version compatibility. Core to Zed’s extension model and ecosystem stability.

Introduces GPUI, Zed’s GPU-accelerated UI framework, outlining the Application lifecycle, entity/view/element model, platform dependencies, and auxiliary services (actions, executor, testing). Foundational to the editor’s architecture and rendering model.
Design and sourcing guidelines for Zed icon assets (sizing, stroke, alignment, naming) and contribution workflow. Ensures consistent UI iconography across the application.

Developer-only inspector for examining and manipulating rendered elements, detailing current features, known issues, and future plans, plus thoughts on cleaner architecture. Aids debugging and iteration on GPUI components.

Design notes for terminal integration: an Alacritty-backed PTY loop with TerminalBuilder two-phase construction, TerminalView abstraction, and detailed input routing paths. Describes the architectural seams between protocol handling and GPUI integration.

Explains Zed’s Vim emulation philosophy (familiar, not strict parity) and test strategies including Neovim-backed golden tests and Zed-only behavior tests. Describes a key editor feature and its validation approach.
Step-by-step example for building a standalone slash-commands extension, including setup, installation, testing, and rebuild workflow. Demonstrates the extension API for conversational features.
Configures the Danger.js tool and PR hygiene plugin for CI checks via a simple npm package. Supports automated code review quality gates.
Python project configuration and dependencies for a utility that updates top-ranking GitHub issues. Ancillary tooling for community feedback workflows.
A comprehensive JSON Schema for npm package.json, defining people, dependencies, licenses, scripts, and conditional exports/imports. Enables schema-aware validation and tooling inside the editor.
Compile-time test verifying gpui_macros derive attributes for AppContext and VisualContext generate correct bindings to App and Window. Ensures macro ergonomics for GPUI integration.
Smoke test for the Render derive macro to ensure elements can implement the Render trait via proc-macro. Guards macro stability for GPUI rendering.

Defines several test AgentTool implementations (echo, delay, permission-gated, infinite, word-list) to exercise tool lifecycles, titles, authorization flows, and async execution. Validates the agent tool abstraction and event handling.

Schema-level tests asserting that ListHistoryToolInput and MemoryToolInput expose required properties via schemars without executing tools, plus a placeholder for future end-to-end tests. Prevents regressions in dynamic tool registration contracts.

Asserts that unified context-management tools (memory, list_history) are no longer part of agent2’s default tool registry and checks for duplicate tool names. Protects against schema conflicts and registration regressions.

End-to-end tests for channel notes buffers covering join/edit/undo synchronization, collaborator presence tracking, and disconnect/reconnect behavior under deterministic executors. Validates core collaborative text synchronization semantics.

Tests guest access in channels, promotion and revocation of roles, microphone permissions, and enforcement of Zed CLA requirements for granting write access. Ensures role-based permissions and policy constraints behave correctly.

Covers channel creation, nesting, invites/acceptance, role changes, deletion propagation, membership removal, and server rename reconciliation after reconnect. Exercises channel state management and propagation in the client/server model.

Validates the project diff UI and file status updates across collaborators by simulating repository contents and changes, ensuring excerpts and tracked statuses update correctly. Tests integration between git state and collaborative UI.

Verifies notification creation, delivery, read-state transitions, responses, and event emission for contact requests and channel invitations. Ensures the notifications store and event pipeline behave as expected.

Randomized test exercising joining/leaving/editing channel notes across multiple users and channels, asserting convergence of buffer text and collaborator sets. Provides fuzz-style coverage of collaborative buffer invariants.

Implements a randomized testing harness with plan generation, serialization/replay, server/client mutation operations, and concurrency orchestration using a deterministic executor. Supports robust fuzz testing across collaboration scenarios.

Integration tests for sharing SSH-based remote projects, verifying worktree scanning consistency across participants, language settings propagation, file edits/saves to remote FS, and git branch operations. Validates remote development collaboration flows.

Testing infrastructure to spin up a deterministic collab server with fake services (FS, HTTP, LiveKit), create authenticated clients, manage connections, and provide helpers to open channels and workspaces. Underpins the collab E2E test suite.

Database-layer tests for channel buffers validating join/update/leave flows, collaborator lists, operation collapse into base text, and latest-version tracking across epochs. Ensures persistence semantics for collaborative buffers.

Initializes the language subsystem by registering tree-sitter grammars and built-in LanguageInfo entries with their LSP adapters, contexts, toolchains, and manifests. Embeds non-Rust language assets and exposes a shared git-commit grammar. Registers globally available language servers and integrates with settings via the LanguageRegistry.

Parses package.json to detect test frameworks (jest, mocha, vitest, jasmine), collect scripts with their paths, and infer the package manager. Provides merge logic to combine data across multiple package.json files.

Implements the Tailwind LSP adapter with npm-based installation, cached/user-installed binary discovery, and version checks. Supplies initialization options, workspace configuration defaults, and language ID mappings for Tailwind-related filetypes.

Defines a TypeScript context provider that generates task templates for jest, vitest, mocha, and jasmine based on data extracted from package.json, exposing variables for runners and package paths. Integrates script discovery to create run tasks with disambiguated labels when needed.

Provides the VTSLS LSP adapter, handling npm installation of @vtsls/language-server and TypeScript, determining the tsdk path (including Yarn SDKs), and caching the server binary. Exposes workspace configuration with sensible defaults and supported code action kinds, and maps language IDs.

Implements a YAML language server adapter with npm installation, cached binary lookup, and user-installed detection. Produces workspace configuration that respects editor tab size and merges project-level overrides.

Provides a modal picker UI to switch the current buffer’s line ending between LF and CRLF, integrated with the editor’s actions and focus. On confirm it updates the buffer and triggers a save via Project.

Defines a LiveKit API client trait and a concrete HTTP client that performs Twirp protobuf requests for room management and participant operations. Each request uses a JWT grant, and responses are decoded with robust error reporting.
Creates and validates JWTs for LiveKit using VideoGrant, enforcing identity when room_join is requested and applying a default TTL. Offers helpers to construct admin, join, and guest grants.

Example application that opens two windows, connects to a LiveKit room, handles room events, toggles microphone and screen sharing, and renders remote video tracks. Serves as a manual test harness with menus and key bindings.

Defines the public API for the livekit_client crate, including core enums (Participant, tracks, RoomEvent) and conditional re-exports of the real or mock client. Includes audio device selection helpers and generic sample data conversion utilities.

Concrete LiveKit client that connects rooms, maps SDK events into a unified RoomEvent stream, and manages publishing/unpublishing tracks. Provides audio playback paths (legacy mixer or rodio) and async wrappers for participant and publication operations with background task lifecycle management.

Mock client wiring that re-exports test participant/track/publication types and stubs for playback, enabling tests or non-supported targets to use an in-memory implementation. Replaces the real client via cfg conditions.
Utility to capture microphone input via cpal, buffer samples, and write a WAV file for diagnostics. Exposes a simple start/finish lifecycle and converts samples to f32 using rodio utilities.

UI component that subscribes to a remote video track, stores the latest frame, and renders it while handling platform-specific resource management and cleanup. Emits a Close event when the stream ends.

Implements an in-memory LiveKit test server and client-side harness that manages rooms, participants, and tracks, validates tokens, and emits RoomEvent updates. Provides operations to modify permissions and simulate joins/leaves and disconnections.

Implements the live audio pipeline with an APM, mixer, and two output strategies (legacy mixer and rodio-based), plus capture of local microphone tracks. Manages background tasks for receiving, mixing, and outputting audio, and exposes a stoppable remote audio stream abstraction.
Mock LocalParticipant and RemoteParticipant that publish tracks via the test server and enumerate track publications for a participant. Includes a minimal screenshare stream implementation for tests.
Mock Local and RemoteTrackPublication types exposing sid, mute state, and enable/disable toggling by mutating shared test room state. Provides basic accessors and control methods for tests.
Mock track types for local and remote audio/video that expose sids, publisher identity, and enabled state via the test room. Used by the mock client and test server to simulate media tracks.

Wraps a LiveKit NativeAudioStream into a rodio Source by queuing decoded frames, selecting legacy or modern sample rate and channel counts. Streams frames on a background task and exposes standard rodio Source traits.

Defines the LM Studio chat completions client types, including roles, message content, tool calls, model metadata, and streaming response structures. Provides the complete() function to send HTTP requests and parse JSON responses with error handling and capability flags.

Background handler for an LSP server’s stdout that parses headers until CRLFCRLF, extracts Content-Length, reads the JSON body, and dispatches notifications or responses to registered handlers. Logs I/O, supports auxiliary IoHandlers, and includes unit tests for header parsing.

Example app rendering a styled Markdown document with syntax highlighting, initializing assets, themes, and languages. Demonstrates integration with the LanguageRegistry and language server setup for demo purposes.

Example showing a Markdown component embedded within a custom UI layout, with configurable styles and theme integration. Initializes languages, themes, and assets to demonstrate usage in a real window.

Manages tab navigation order via TabStopMap, recording Insert/Group operations and ordering TabStopNodes by hierarchical TabStopPath plus insertion index using a SumTree. Provides next/prev traversal that skips non-tab-stop nodes, mapping FocusIds to handles, and supports replay/clear while tracking insertion history for paint indexing.

Wraps the Taffy layout engine, exposing request_layout for regular and measured nodes, compute_layout with custom measure callbacks, and caching of absolute layout bounds to avoid recomputation. Converts GPUI Style into Taffy styles and defines a LayoutId wrapper for safe interop.

Provides deterministic test harness utilities: run_test with seed iteration and retry logic driven by env vars, and Observation streams converting entity notifications into async events. Enables robust, reproducible GPUI tests across executors.

Implements the TextSystem bridging to the PlatformTextSystem, caching font IDs and metrics, resolving fonts with fallbacks, and exposing glyph bounds/advances and typographic metrics. Includes pools for wrappers/font runs and precomputed raster bounds to optimize text layout and rendering.

Utility module with a FluentBuilder trait for conditional fluent construction, FutureExt with timeout combinator backed by executors, and atomic_incr_if_not_zero for safe counter updates. Includes a smol-based timeout helper and tests.

Integrates views into the element pipeline, implementing Element for Entity<V> and introducing AnyView with optional caching that reuses prepaint/paint ranges when bounds, content mask, and text style are unchanged. Coordinates window render state, downcasting, and weak handles to optimize frame reuse.
Example application showcasing image rendering from local files, remote URIs, and assets with basic layout, menus, and key bindings. Demonstrates img usage and window setup.
Example rendering the same SVG in different colors using the svg element, with a simple window and layout. Illustrates asset loading and styling.

Defines AsyncApp as an AppContext over a weak App, enabling async-safe entity/window operations, global state access, and spawning foreground/background tasks. Provides AsyncWindowContext and on_drop utilities to bridge async workflows with UI lifecycles.

Entity-scoped Context offering observe/subscribe/notify APIs, lifecycle hooks (release, restart, quit), task spawning, and convenience wrappers to access view state in event handlers. Facilitates focusing, deferred execution, and integration with window rendering while preserving type safety via WeakEntity.

Core entity storage managing reservation, insertion, leasing (stack movement) and strict end_lease, with accessed-entity tracking and reference counting for safe lifecycle. Supports AnyEntity/AnyWeakEntity conversions, leak detection, and collection of dropped entities via a RwLock-backed ref-count map.

Implements TestAppContext as an AppContext for tests, wiring test executors, platform, and TextSystem, and providing helpers to open windows, retrieve visual contexts, and control app lifecycle. Enables deterministic interleaving and cleanup via on_quit and refresh methods.

Anchored element positions children relative to a specified corner and origin, adjusting to avoid window overflow by switching anchor sides or snapping with optional margins. Supports local vs window coordinate modes and offsets, computing child union bounds to place content safely.

AnimationElement wraps any element with time-based animations, supporting easing, chaining, looping, and state tracking to drive requestAnimationFrame. Provides AnimationExt for ergonomic APIs and computes delta progression per animation with optional auto-advance.
Canvas element enables custom drawing via prepaint/paint closures while participating in normal layout and styling. Useful for ad-hoc rendering without defining bespoke elements.
Deferred element preserves layout but defers child painting, queuing draws with priority to control z-order relative to ancestors. Useful for overlays or late draws without reflowing the layout tree.

Provides an ImageCache element and trait with AnyImageCache abstraction to supply caches to subtrees, loading resources asynchronously and notifying views upon completion. Includes RetainAllImageCache to retain images, share tasks, and drop GPU images on clear/remove to free resources.

Img element renders images from multiple sources (resources, cached render, raw Image, or custom loader), with styling (grayscale, object fit) and optional subtree/global cache. Manages layout/paint state, loading delays, hitboxes, and animated frames (e.g., GIF/WebP), leveraging AssetLogger and format decoding.

Virtualized list element for heterogeneous item heights using a SumTree to track counts/heights and compute visible ranges efficiently. Supports top/bottom alignment, overdraw, splice/reset with focus-handle awareness, and scroll event translation, minimizing re-renders by storing state intrusively.

Surface element renders platform-specific surfaces (e.g., macOS CVPixelBuffer) with object-fit behavior and styling. Paints directly via window APIs, acting as a thin bridge from system buffers to the UI.

Svg element with interactivity and optional geometric transformation, loading a path and drawing via window.paint_svg with current text color. Computes hitboxes and composes a transformation matrix around the element center for scaling/translation/rotation.

Text elements (&str, SharedString, StyledText) compute layout and rendering via TextLayout, supporting white-space handling, wrapping/truncation, and styled runs with highlights. Prepaint caches geometry for index-to-pixel mapping, and paint draws using window text style and metrics.

Implements the 'tab' slash command to insert content from open editor tabs, with argument completion including an 'all' option and active tab suggestion. It collects open buffers across panes, deduplicates by remote id, sorts by activation timestamp, and fuzzy-matches queries against file paths before appending buffer snapshots to the output. Cancellation-aware background tasks and UI label formatting are used to keep interactions responsive.

Defines the core Tool abstraction, result model (text/image), async execution contract, and optional renderable cards for UI. Provides AnyToolCard type-erasure and rendering hooks, tool source tracking, and integration points for language models, including schema handling and confirmation logic. This is the foundational architecture enabling tools to run and present results in the Assistant.

Generates and renders per-file symbol outlines with line numbers, waiting for parsing to complete and supporting pagination. Provides a helper to return either full buffer content or an outline for large files, allowing the system to avoid sending oversized file contents. Used by tools to supply concise context when reading large files.

Implements a global registry for managing Tool instances, supporting registration, unregistration, lookup by name, and enumeration. Uses a gpui Global and a locked state to coordinate tools across the app, serving as the central catalog for assistant capabilities. This enables dynamic tool availability throughout the system.

Adapts tool input JSON schemas to different model provider formats by preprocessing and normalizing (e.g., enforcing additionalProperties=false, converting oneOf to anyOf, removing unsupported keys). Recursively transforms nested structures and adds default types when missing, with tests ensuring compatibility. This ensures tool schemas are accepted across providers like OpenAI and Gemini.

Manages a per-session working set of tools, merging native tools with context server tools and resolving name conflicts by prefixing with server IDs and truncating. Provides lookup by unique name, grouping by source, and change notifications to keep UI tool lists coherent. This layer isolates session-specific tool availability from the global registry.

Copies files or directories within the project after validating source and destination paths are inside the project. Runs the copy operation asynchronously and reports success or detailed errors, with a schema describing source and destination paths. It is marked as performing edits to project state.

Creates a new directory inside the project, validating the target path and executing the operation asynchronously via project APIs. Returns a confirmation message or errors when paths are outside the project. Provides a simple schema and UI text for clarity.

Deletes a file or directory with confirmation, first streaming affected paths to mark buffers as pending deletion in the action log, then performing the deletion. Validates project membership and worktree presence, and reports detailed errors or success. Uses async traversal and messaging to handle recursive deletes safely.

Reports diagnostics for a specific file (errors/warnings with line numbers) or summarizes diagnostics across the project. Waits for parsing to finish, reads grouped diagnostics from snapshots, and formats a human-readable output. Useful for guiding fixes without modifying project state.

Fetches a URL and returns content as Markdown, converting HTML via tag handlers (with special Wikipedia handling), pretty-printing JSON, or returning plaintext. Validates protocols, handles HTTP errors, and runs in background/foreground executors to produce a safe textual summary. This provides web content ingestion for the assistant.

Searches the project for paths matching a glob, paginates results, and returns both a textual summary and structured JSON output. Includes a ToolCard that renders clickable results to open files within the workspace. Uses PathMatcher and project worktree snapshots, respecting path styles.

Performs a project-wide regex search with include/exclude glob filtering derived from settings, then builds readable context around matches including syntax ancestor ranges and merges adjacent hits. Paginates results across buffers and formats per-file sections while skipping excluded/private paths. This implements a robust search algorithm for code context.

Lists contents of a project directory, separating folders and files, while respecting global and worktree exclusion/private settings. Handles root/glob-like inputs by listing top-level worktree directories and formats Markdown output with sections. Includes tests to verify behavior across platforms.

Moves or renames a file/directory within the project after validating both paths, then performs the operation asynchronously and reports results. The UI text differentiates between simple rename (same parent) and move. Provides a schema for source/destination inputs.
Returns the current datetime in RFC 3339 format, supporting either UTC or local timezones. Simple, stateless tool with a minimal schema and no side effects.

Opens a given project-relative path or external URL with the system default application, resolving project paths to absolute locations when possible. Runs the operation in the background and reports success, with tests verifying path resolution behavior. Requires user confirmation due to launching external applications.

Flushes and reports user edit notifications from the action log by emitting a unified diff, compressing it to fit size limits by eliding hunk bodies or listing changed files only. Splits multi-file patches and reconstructs compact outputs to ensure delivery. Provides a simple schema and immediate textual results with tests covering compression.

Reads a file or image from the project while enforcing exclusion/private path settings, supporting optional line ranges and setting the agent location anchor for context. For large files it returns an outline instead of full content, and for images it constructs a LanguageModelImage if the model supports images. This is a central content ingestion tool with careful privacy and size handling.

Generates JSON schemas for tool inputs via schemars and adapts them to the target format (e.g., JsonSchemaSubset) using a transform that flattens option types and converts oneOf to anyOf. Serves as a utility to produce provider-compatible schemas used by all tools.

Executes shell commands in a project directory with environment setup, either embedding a TerminalView in the workspace or using a native pty for headless runs. Processes and normalizes output, manages truncation and status, and renders a ToolCard showing command, working dir, and expandable output preview. Requires confirmation due to external command execution.
A no-op utility tool that accepts input for 'thinking' and returns a simple completion message without performing actions. Serves as a scaffolding for structured reasoning steps.

Performs web searches via the active provider and returns serialized results, while rendering a ToolCard with clickable result buttons and tooltips. Handles async task integration and card deserialization for restoring UI from structured output. Registration is toggled based on the default language model provider.

Initializes and registers all built-in assistant tools and context management tools in the global registry, wiring HTTP clients and dynamic web search tool availability based on the default model provider. Re-exports core types and subscribes to model changes to keep tools in sync. This is the central bootstrap of the assistant tools subsystem.
A test-only tool used to verify tool registration and execution, emitting a known log message and simple success output. Useful for validating the context management and tool plumbing.

Manages editor selections, tracking disjoint and pending selections, merging overlaps, and converting between anchors, buffer points, and display coordinates. Supports line-mode expansion and provides efficient range queries over selections using the display map and buffer snapshots.

Implements editor signature help: toggling auto behavior, detecting bracket-enclosed contexts to open/close, querying LSP, and rendering highlighted signature UI with theme settings. Integrates with editor state to avoid conflicts with selections and completion menus.

Builds a task context from the editor’s current selection and buffer location, capturing variables from nearby task annotations. Also aggregates which buffers map to LSP task sources by language server configuration.

Provides test utilities for the editor, including constructing editors, generating display snapshots with markers and blocks, selecting ranges, and asserting text with selections. Also includes helpers to render custom block content during visual tests.

Represents fold and block regions (“creases”) over the buffer using a SumTree for efficient queries, insertions, and removals. Supports inline and block creases with optional UI render hooks and metadata, and querying by buffer rows or ranges.

Streams buffer chunks while applying custom highlight ranges by maintaining active highlight endpoints and combining styles, splitting chunks at highlight boundaries. Ensures correctness of chunk bitmaps and highlight application via tests.

Detects and substitutes invisible or confusable whitespace/control characters based on curated Unicode ranges and rules. Provides replacement glyphs or fixed-width spaces while preserving combining characters critical to glyph rendering.

Integrates git blame with the editor by maintaining per-buffer blame entries in a SumTree, syncing with buffer edits and repository updates, and rendering blame UI elements on demand. Tracks commit details and supports inline popovers and navigation.

Defines scroll actions to move the viewport relative to the newest cursor (next screen, center, top, bottom) while respecting editor modes and margins. Coordinates with autoscroll state and debounce to cycle center/top/bottom behavior.

Implements autoscroll strategies (fit, newest, center, focused, top/bottom, relative) to keep cursors or anchors visible with minimal movement, considering highlighted rows and viewport metrics. Tracks last autoscroll to support cycling behavior and updates scroll position precisely.

Encapsulates scroll amounts (lines, pages, columns, page width) and converts to line or pixel deltas, handling full-page anchor line retention and direction derivation. Used to normalize scroll gestures across axes.

Builds an end-to-end LSP-backed editor test harness, registering fake language servers, opening buffers, waiting for worktree scans, and exposing helpers for ranges and LSP conversions. Includes language configs for Rust/TypeScript/HTML tailored to tests.

Provides a high-level test context for interacting with an editor instance: creating multibuffers, reading/updating buffers, simulating keystrokes, computing display/pixel positions, and asserting selections and diagnostics. Facilitates deterministic UI and buffer testing.
Defines assertion reporting for eval runs, including pass/fail tracking, percentages, and formatted table rendering. Supports error capture and truncation with boundary-safe string handling.

Main entry point for the agent evaluation harness: parses CLI args, initializes application and models, filters and prepares examples, clones/fetches repos, and orchestrates concurrent runs with telemetry. Manages worktrees, proxy settings, and cumulative tool metrics aggregation.

Defines the Example trait and ExampleContext runtime that drives conversations, handles agent thread events, logs assertions, and accumulates tool metrics. Provides utilities to run turns until stop reasons and to assert outcomes programmatically.

Generates an HTML explorer by injecting serialized thread data from JSON files into a template, with support for resolving inputs from files/directories and escaping embedded script tags. Provides a CLI for batch generation.

Encapsulates a single example execution: sets up/fetches git worktrees at specific revisions, initializes a project and optional LSP, runs the example in the app, and collects outputs (diffs, diagnostics, messages, token usage, tool metrics). Produces inputs for judges and persists run artifacts.
Tracks per-tool usage and failure counts during eval runs, merges metrics, and renders a sorted failure-rate table. Provides a simple API to record tool outcomes.

Evaluation scenario that asks to add a window argument to a trait method and verifies edits across affected tools, including prefixed unused arguments. Encodes assertions against specific files and added lines.

Evaluation that requests trait method bodies in separate code blocks and verifies citation formatting and content ranges against source files, including de-indentation and range parsing. Ensures code blocks use backtick fences and match referenced snippets.

Evaluation that instructs translating comments in specified files and asserts that edits use the non-destructive edit mode and only targeted files change. Limits assertions count to constrain test scope.

Evaluation ensuring the agent does not acknowledge file change notifications after a buffer edit, by tracking a file, editing it, and running additional turns to observe message behavior. Includes a hard turn limit.
Evaluation prompting UI work that triggers a find_path tool call, then asserts the generated glob structure (prefix and suffix) matches expectations. Validates tool parameter formation.

Evaluation verifying that grep tool parameters are not HTML-escaped when searching for angle brackets, asserting absence of entity encodings in the regex. Runs a small number of turns and checks for tool invocation.

Aggregates all procedural and declarative examples, loading TOML-defined scenarios into Example implementations with prompts and assertions. Supports requiring LSP, custom profiles, and existing thread playback.

Evaluation verifying that the edit_file tool edits instead of overwriting an existing file by inspecting tool inputs from a pre-recorded thread. Asserts that overwrite mode is not used on a sensitive path.

Evaluation requesting a plain JS animated solar system without npm and asserting no misuse of open/terminal tools, plus diff assertions about functionality and stack choices. Tallies tool usage from the response.

Windows shell extension implementing IExplorerCommand to add an “Open with Zed” context menu, locating the Zed executable and invoking it for selected items. Exposes a class factory and reads metadata from the registry.

Defines the core extension system: initialization, Extension trait API for language servers, context servers, slash commands, DAP integration, and capability checks. Includes delegates for worktree/project I/O and parsing a custom wasm section for API versioning.

Builds and validates extensions: compiles Rust WASI components, sets API version, verifies debug adapter schemas, and compiles grammars via clang from the wasi-sdk, with caching and repo checkout. Also strips custom sections from wasm components.
Provides a global extension event bus to emit and subscribe to events such as install/uninstall and configuration requests. Integrates with gpui’s entity/event system for cross-app notifications.

Global proxy aggregating sub-proxies for extension features (themes, grammars, languages, language servers, snippets, slash commands, context servers, debug adapters) with registration and pass-through methods. Serves as the host-side facade for extension integrations.

Defines the extension manifest schema (TOML/legacy JSON), loaders, and helpers for capabilities (e.g., process exec allow-list) and language server mappings. Handles schema versioning and debug adapter/grammar metadata validation.

Shared types for the extension host, including commands, code label structures with spans, and utility formatting that redacts sensitive env vars. Forms the data model for label rendering and command execution.
Capability type that whitelists downloadable URLs by host and path patterns with * and ** semantics, providing an allows method with comprehensive tests. Used to constrain extension network access.
Capability to allow npm package installation by exact package name or wildcard, with a simple allows check and tests. Supports guarding package installs by extensions.

Capability that authorizes running external processes by command and argument patterns, supporting single and trailing wildcards, with thorough tests. Used by manifests to restrict subprocess execution.
Lightweight types mirroring LSP completions and symbols for extensions, including kinds and insert text format. Used by extension labelers without binding to full LSP crates.
Types for assistant slash commands, including command metadata, output sections with ranges, and argument completion items. Enables structured command UIs and execution feedback.

Public Rust API for building Zed extensions atop WIT bindings: defines the Extension trait surface (language servers, context servers, slash commands, DAP) and reexports core types. Provides utilities to set language server status and a Result alias for extensions.

Convenience wrapper over WIT HTTP client providing a builder for requests, header/body configuration, redirect policy, and synchronous fetch/fetch_stream helpers. Simplifies making HTTP calls from extensions.
Thin ergonomic wrapper for building and running process commands via the WIT process API, with chaining methods for args and envs. Returns captured output on execution.

Accessors to retrieve language, LSP, and context server settings scoped to a worktree or project by delegating to the host via WIT and deserializing JSON. Handles global vs per-worktree precedence for context servers.
WIT-derived settings model for API v0.2.0, defining language tab size, LSP settings, context server settings, and command settings structures. Used for stable compatibility with older extensions.
WIT-derived settings schema for API v0.3.0 mirroring language, LSP, context server, and command settings. Maintains versioned compatibility for extensions.
WIT-derived settings schema for API v0.4.0 covering language, LSP, context server, and command settings. Supports evolving extension API without breaking older versions.
WIT-derived settings schema for API v0.5.0 with the same command/language/LSP/context server structures. Enables versioned extension settings parsing.
WIT-derived settings schema for API v0.6.0 defining language tab size and LSP/context server/command settings. Latest versioned settings used by the extension API.

Defines TaskTemplate and related enums for terminal reveal/hide behavior and shells, plus TaskTemplates schema generation. resolve_task performs variable substitution from TaskContext, computes a stable TaskId via hashing, merges environment variables, and produces a ResolvedTask with optional truncated labels for readability.

Parses VS Code launch.json configurations into Zed DebugScenario entries, performing environment variable replacement and mapping VS Code debug types to adapter names. Supports optional TCP connection templates and normalizes JavaScript configurations.

Converts VS Code tasks.json to Zed TaskTemplate instances, supporting npm, shell, and gulp tasks with variable substitution for command, args, and options. Skips unsupported dependsOn tasks and maps common VS Code variables to Zed variables.

Implements a picker-based modal to search and run tasks, including generating one-shot tasks from user input and applying optional reveal target overrides. Manages candidate lists from used, LSP, and current tasks, integrates with TaskStore, and emits attach modal events for debugging.

Wires actions to spawn or rerun tasks by name, tag, or via modal, optionally re-evaluating context and overriding concurrency/new terminal flags. Queries task inventory based on file/language context and schedules matching tasks in the workspace.

Provides a telemetry event macro to construct and enqueue FlexibleEvent payloads, with helpers to initialize and send events via a global queue. Designed for lightweight instrumentation with optional debug logging.

Defines the telemetry data model including request bodies, event wrappers, and a Flexible event type, along with rich structs for assistant interactions, panics, and hang reports. Includes enums and helpers for serialization and display formatting.

Retrieves and tracks PTY process information cross-platform, acquiring process group IDs with fallbacks and refreshing details via sysinfo. Exposes current process name/cwd/argv, supports killing the process, and detects changes to update UI.

Represents terminal settings (shell, fonts, env, behavior) and maps them from app settings and VS Code import. Converts settings shell variants to task::Shell, applies platform-specific imports, and supplies terminal UI preferences like cursor shape and scrollback.

Maps gpui keystrokes and terminal modes to precise escape sequences, handling special keys, modifiers, and application cursor modes. Combines manual mappings with autogenerated modifier encodings, including Alt-as-Meta behavior.

Generates terminal mouse reporting sequences (SGR or normal/UTF-8) for clicks, drags, motion, and scroll events based on TermMode. Converts pixel positions to grid points and encodes button/modifier states with bounds handling.

Serializes and restores terminal panel layouts, panes, and items, omitting running tasks and reconstructing views asynchronously. Rebuilds nested pane groups with active item and pinned state, and creates a new terminal when needed to avoid blank splits.

Resolves path-like targets from terminal output by searching worktrees (and optionally the filesystem) to identify files or directories, accounting for prefixes like a/ and b/ in diffs. Updates terminal hover tooltips with resolved paths and supports tests with configurable background checks.

Implements a ScrollableHandle that maps UI scroll offsets to the terminal’s display_offset using line metrics from terminal content. Tracks viewport and total lines to compute bounds and future scroll targets.

Implements a /terminal slash command that inserts recent terminal output into the editor, with optional line count argument and contextual labeling. Locates the active terminal and returns a structured output stream for insertion.
Renders a tooltip for terminal tabs showing the item title and process ID with styled presentation. Provides simple, non-interactive display logic.

Defines a timestamped buffer Anchor with ordering, biasing (left/right), and validity checks against visible fragments, plus conversions between offsets and points. Provides selection range helpers and ensures robust comparison across buffer snapshots.

Implements an order-preserving Locator identifier supporting dense insertions via between(min,max) without renumbering. Integrates with sum_tree traits for summaries and keys, with randomized tests validating ordering properties.

A test network harness that simulates unreliable delivery by duplicating, reordering, and dropping messages, with peer disconnect/reconnect support. Provides inbox management and randomized receive semantics for robustness testing.

A SumTree-backed OperationQueue keyed by Lamport timestamps that sorts, de-duplicates, and stores operations with efficient length/iteration/drain. Defines summaries and dimensions ensuring monotonic keys and fast aggregation.

Represents and composes sequences of edits with a non-trivial compose algorithm that merges disjoint/overlapping edits and maps offsets across versions. Supports invert, old_to_new offset mapping, and retains/merges adjacent edits; heavily tested.

Encapsulates selections with head/tail semantics, reversed state, and goal tracking, providing operations to set/collapse and map positions. Resolves anchor-based selections to display dimensions via buffer snapshots.

Implements a lightweight pub/sub for edit patches using weak subscriptions storing composed Patch<usize> per subscriber. Publishers compose incoming edits into each subscriber’s patch, which can then be consumed atomically.

Comprehensive tests for the text buffer covering random edits, undo/redo, edit propagation, summaries, and line endings. Validates versioned rope retrieval and subscription patch application under randomized scenarios.
