Tracks undo state per edit via a SumTree keyed by (edit_id, undo_id) Lamport timestamps, providing queries like is_undone and was_undone at a version. Maintains maximum undo counts per edit to support toggle semantics.

Defines Zed’s default theme family and a One Dark theme with curated color constants, plus logic to derive background defaults from foreground status colors. Applies theme color defaults based on player colors for consistent selection visuals.
Caches the system’s font family list with lazy loading and background prefetch to avoid expensive repeated queries. Exposes a global cache with synchronous and try-read accessors.

Defines the icon theme data model, including families, directory/chevron icons, and mappings of file stems and suffixes to icon keys with bundled defaults. Supports resolving icons across file types via compact lookup maps.
Schema types for serializing/deserializing icon themes, covering theme metadata, directory/chevron icons, file stem/suffix maps, and icon definitions. Used to load user-defined icon themes.

Manages global theme and icon theme registries, loading bundled and user themes, listing metadata, and retrieving themes by name. Provides mutation APIs (insert/remove/clear) and resolves default icon themes.
Defines 12-step color scales and scale sets for light/dark and alpha variants, with helpers to pick steps per active appearance. Centralizes theme color palettes used across theme definitions.

Defines serializable theme family/content schemas and refinement helpers to map user theme JSON into internal structures, enforcing opacity constraints. Provides utilities to extract syntax overrides and convert status/theme colors to HSL.

Holds theme-related settings (active theme/icon theme, fonts, line height, UI density) with system appearance awareness and reload logic. Integrates with SettingsStore to react to changes and provides selection types for static/dynamic themes.

Theme system entry point initializing registry, settings, and font caches, exporting theme components and constants. Implements ThemeFamily refinement to materialize Theme from content and provides ActiveTheme access via App.

Defines AccentColors with default light/dark palettes and merging from user overrides, providing indexed access for repeating assignments. Intended for accenting editor visuals like indent-aware lines.

Specifies a comprehensive ThemeColors struct with refineable fields for UI surfaces, text, icons, editors, scrollbars, and terminal colors. Serves as the backbone for theming the application’s components.

Configures PlayerColors for collaborative cursors and selections with default light/dark sets and utilities to pick per-participant colors. Supports merging user overrides and generating read-only variants.
Defines StatusColors for semantic states (created, modified, error, etc.) with light/dark defaults and derived diagnostic colors. Used across UI to color status indicators consistently.
Represents a syntax theme as a list of token highlight styles with APIs to fetch colors and merge user-defined styles over a base. Ensures additive overrides without losing unspecified attributes.

Bridges the extension host with the theme registry, exposing APIs to load/remove user themes and icon themes, set extension load state, and trigger reloads. Performs filesystem operations asynchronously via a background executor.
Utility to parse color strings into HSL and pack colors back to RGBA integers, ensuring round-trip fidelity. Used by the theme importer to normalize VS Code color formats.

CLI tool that converts a VS Code theme JSON into a Zed theme JSON, with logging, argument parsing, and optional output file writing. Uses a converter to map colors, status, and syntax into Zed’s schema and adds a $schema URL.

Converts VS Code theme structures into Zed ThemeContent by mapping UI colors, status colors, and token styles, inferring font styles/weights from strings. Consolidates values from VS Code color sections and token colors, including defaults.

Models VS Code token colors and maps them to a curated set of ZedSyntaxToken identifiers, ranking matches by scope specificity and weighting. Provides fallbacks between related token categories to improve coverage.
Defines the VS Code theme file structure (colors and token colors) with lenient serde mappings and optional metadata. Serves as input to the converter pipeline.

Modal picker to preview and select icon themes with fuzzy matching, immediate theme application, telemetry, and settings persistence. Handles dismissal by restoring the original theme if not confirmed.

Modal picker to preview and select UI themes with fuzzy search and live application; integrates actions to toggle selectors and reload themes. Persists selection to settings and logs telemetry, with an option to filter available themes.

Formats timestamps in absolute, enhanced absolute (Today/Yesterday), medium date, and relative forms, respecting platform-specific locale behavior. Provides helpers to format date/time components and compute human-friendly deltas.

Renders an application menu using popover menus, sanitizing items (e.g., removing redundant separators) and supporting keyboard navigation across menus. Handles platform-specific presentation and deferred opening based on actions.

Implements title bar collaboration controls for screen sharing, mute, and deafen with telemetry, and renders participant avatars with presence/follow state. Integrates with ActiveCall and Workspace to follow/unfollow peers and display role-based visuals.

A dismissible onboarding banner component that promotes new features, persists dismissal timestamps via key-value store, and logs telemetry on interactions. Supports conditional visibility and global restoration for testing or feature resets.

Platform-adaptive title bar component that sets height/colors, integrates window controls, supports drag-to-move and double-click actions, and hosts system window tabs. Adjusts rounding/borders based on client/server decorations and tiling.

Integrates with the OS’s system window tab controller to display and manage window tabs, including drag-and-drop reordering and actions to switch/merge/move tabs. Reacts to settings changes to enable tabbing and renders themed tabs with close controls.

Integration tests validating channel lifecycle and permissions: creating root/sub-channels, membership invites/acceptance, role updates, room join gating by membership, renames, and deletion of single channels or entire trees. Verifies visibility and participant details across users and enforces admin-only operations on parent channels.
Tests contributor tracking by adding contributors and asserting get_contributors returns a growing, ordered list starting empty. Ensures consistency between created users and contributor records.

Covers user retrieval and upsert by GitHub account, access-token rotation with capped history (including impersonation exceptions), and contact requests flow including dismissal and acceptance. Ensures correctness of core user and token-management behaviors across both backends.
Verifies saving and retrieving vector embeddings by digest for a model and purging entries older than 60 days. Ensures correct handling of array data and time-based cleanup in Postgres.

Exercises extension metadata storage: inserting multiple versions, listing known versions, filtering by schema version, tracking download counts, and ordering by total downloads. Also validates backfilling older versions and returning the latest manifest per extension.
Tests setting and clearing users’ accepted_tos_at timestamps and verifies cascade deletion of access tokens upon user destruction. Confirms persistence and cleanup semantics for user lifecycle.

Validates attach-to-process behavior: direct attach uses task definition without showing a modal, and the attach modal can display, filter, and select processes to initiate an attach then dismiss. Ensures correct DAP attach arguments and UI state transitions.

Ensures console output handling captures messages both before and after a Stopped event and renders them in order. Also verifies processing of ANSI escape sequences and updating the visual console buffer.

Tests the DAP logger integration to capture and persist all session RPC messages per project, starting with initialization and reacting to events like Stopped. Confirms session discovery and message storage in LogStore.
Verifies the modules pane requests Modules once on user activation and renders the returned modules. Tests dynamic updates via Module events for New, Changed, and Removed cases.

Validates variable substitution and path normalization for debug configs (absolute, relative, home, and $ZED_WORKTREE_ROOT) and asserts only intended fields are transformed. Tests saving scenarios to .zed/debug.json with correct content and caret placement, and covers modal UX across multiple worktrees.

Checks that moving the debug panel between docks inverts the split axis of the serialized pane layout while preserving pane ordering and flex ratios. Ensures layout stability across UI position changes.

Tests fetching and displaying stack frames on pause, selecting the current thread, and asserting the active frame and frame list contents. Also validates navigation/opening of source files associated with frames.
Exercises the actions! macro and Action derive to generate actions and registers a custom action to ensure macro plumbing compiles and integrates. Confirms serde bounds and registration flow.

Tests the derive_inspector_reflection macro by reflecting over methods with fn(self)->Self signatures, invoking by name, and verifying captured documentation. Ensures filtering of non-matching signatures and chaining works as intended.

Implements license detection by canonicalizing text and matching against parsed, parameterized patterns for common open-source licenses, scanning standard license filenames. Ties into a watcher that classifies worktrees/files and exposes results within the app’s architecture.
Command to audit each workspace crate for expected license files and report missing or non-symlink licenses. Helps enforce consistent licensing across the repository during development or CI.
Cloudflare Worker that proxies incoming requests to docs-anw.pages.dev and falls back to zed.dev/404 for missing content. Provides a simple edge gateway for documentation hosting.
Cloudflare Worker that serves static assets from an R2 bucket keyed by path and falls back to zed.dev/404 if absent. Preserves metadata and ETag headers for caching.
Windows-only build script embedding a manifest and app icon using winresource, and watching for manifest changes. Ensures correct Windows binary metadata for the auto-update helper.

Build script toggling a feature flag from an env var, setting macOS deployment target, and embedding the current git commit SHA as ZED_COMMIT_SHA. Adds reproducible version metadata to the CLI binary.
Build script that reads the crates/zed package version and exposes it as ZED_PKG_VERSION at compile time. Keeps evaluation tooling version-aligned with the main app.
Build script encodes the crate’s semantic version into six bytes and writes them to OUT_DIR for runtime use. Facilitates API version handshake across components.
Build script computes the repository root from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and exports it as ZED_REPO_DIR. Allows inspector UI to locate repository resources at runtime.
Build script propagating the ZED_BUNDLE environment variable to rustc, enabling bundled asset builds. Provides a switch for packaging behavior.
Build script generating protobuf code for LiveKit Room API via prost with a lint allowance on an empty docs case. Automates LiveKit client type generation.
Build script generating protobufs for zed.proto via prost, deriving serde traits and Hash/Eq for key types, and tracking changes in the proto directory. Centralizes typed RPC message generation.
Build script exposing the zed package version and TARGET as env vars and embedding the git commit SHA if available. Provides runtime metadata for the remote server binary.
Windows/MSVC-specific build script increasing the linker stack size to 8MB. Avoids stack overflows in storybook builds on Windows.
Build script mirroring crates/zed version into ZED_PKG_VERSION for the zeta CLI. Keeps CLI version synchronized with the app.
Aggregates agent subsystem modules (context, thread store, history, tools) and provides init to wire thread storage and embedded MCP server. Re-exports core agent types and errors for consumers.
Module aggregator re-exporting agent2 components (agent, db, history, server, templates, thread, tools) and tests. Serves as the crate’s public API surface.
Re-exports ACP-related UI modules including completion provider, model selectors, thread views, and history. Provides a single import point for ACP UI components.
Re-exports various agent UI elements like onboarding modals, notifications, tooltips, and usage callouts. Centralizes UI component access for the agent UI.
UI component rendering a tooltip that informs users editing previous messages is not yet available for a given agent. Uses shared theme styling and tooltip container.
Renders a warning banner explaining trial ineligibility for very new GitHub accounts and directs users to support. Encapsulates the message in a themed Banner component.
Re-exports a suite of assistant slash commands (context, file, diagnostics, etc.) and provides label creation utilities. Consolidates command implementations for consumers.
Embeds and registers Handlebars templates at build time and provides a Template trait to render typed contexts without escaping modifications. Central utility for rendering assistant tool outputs.
Re-exports assistant tool UI components like tool call headers and output previews. Acts as a façade for UI parts of assistant tools.
Re-exports tools for context management (calling context server, listing history, memory operations) and their input types. Groups context-related tool interfaces for easy use.
Minimal Python fixtures for a reactive cells API used in edit-agent evaluations, providing placeholder InputCell and ComputeCell types. Serves as test data rather than functional logic.
Defines the call module boundary and re-exports its implementation alongside call settings. Central entry point to the calling feature.
Defines CallSettings and a Settings implementation to load mute/share-on-join preferences from settings content. Integrates call behavior with the global settings system.

Parses Markdown with pulldown-cmark into a stream of (Range, MarkdownEvent), converting tags to internal MarkdownTag variants, tracking when inside links/metadata, and merging adjacent text events. It extracts fenced code block content ranges and line counts, interpreting info strings as either a language or a file path (via PathWithRange) while collecting unique language names and paths.

Implements PathWithRange and LineCol to parse strings like 'path/to/file#L10:5-L20:15' (tolerant to 'L' variations and optional columns) into a path plus an optional line/column range. It trims any leading language/words before the path and includes thorough tests for edge cases.

Defines the parsed Markdown model used by the preview (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, block quotes, code blocks, images) with source ranges, text highlights, and regions. It includes link identification (web vs filesystem), image metadata, and utilities to map MarkdownHighlight to UI HighlightStyle.

Implements the Markdown preview pane integrated with the workspace, managing an active editor, a 'follow' mode, focus, list state, and debounced re-parsing/rendering. It registers actions to open previews in-place or to the side, reuses existing views when possible, and filters to Markdown buffers.

Renders ParsedMarkdown into GPUI elements using a RenderContext that applies theme-derived fonts, colors, and scaled sizing. It provides per-block renderers (headings, paragraphs, lists with interactive task checkboxes, code blocks, tables, images) and assigns stable IDs from source ranges to support interactivity.

macOS-only FFI wrappers around CoreMedia/CoreVideo expose Rust types for CMSampleBuffer, CMFormatDescription, CMBlockBuffer, and CVMetalTextureCache to inspect buffer contents, H.264 parameter sets, and create Metal textures. It bridges CF/OSStatus APIs and manages lifetimes via TCFType wrappers.

Aggregates and re-exports date-stamped migration modules for settings and keymaps, serving as the registry of available transformations. Each submodule exposes pattern sets or functions consumed by the migration engine.

Provides reusable tree-sitter JSON query patterns to match keymap structures including action arrays, string actions, contexts, and array arguments as objects. These patterns underpin multiple keymap migration passes.

Defines tree-sitter JSON query patterns for settings documents: root and nested pairs, per-language overrides, assistant profiles/tools, and edit prediction-related keys. Migrations use these patterns to locate and transform settings reliably.

Replaces deprecated boolean values in specific nested settings (e.g., chat_panel.button, scrollbar.diagnostics) with new string enums using a lookup table. It matches nested key/value pairs and emits exact range replacements.

Normalizes keymap actions by converting [action, argument] arrays to new action strings, unwrapping object-argument arrays, renaming several action identifiers, and updating context predicate strings. Replacements are driven by lookup tables and precise tree-sitter captures.

Renames inline completion settings to edit prediction equivalents across root, nested (features), and per-language scopes, including changing features.inline_completion_provider to edit_prediction_provider. It performs controlled string substitutions based on whitelists.

Enforces snake_case for specific keymap action argument keys/values by rewriting array-with-object forms, converting keys and string values while preserving non-string values. Targets a fixed set of actions via a mapping.

Migrates tabs.always_show_close_button to show_close_button and maps boolean values to string modes ('always' or 'hover'). It matches the nested 'tabs' object and replaces the key and/or value accordingly.

Renames 'Prev' variants to 'Previous' for several actions and expands certain string actions into array forms with additional options (e.g., center_cursor: true). It chooses the appropriate replacement based on the matched action name.

Simplifies specific array-form actions (editor::GoToHunk and editor::GoToPreviousHunk with options) back to plain string actions. It matches array patterns and replaces the entire array span with the action string.
Renames 'hide_mouse_while_typing' to 'hide_mouse' and converts boolean values to new string enums ('on_typing_and_movement' or 'never'). It coordinates edits to both key and value.
Renames the keymap action 'outline_panel::Open' to 'outline_panel::OpenSelectedEntry' via straightforward string substitution. It targets only string-form actions matched by the pattern.

Renames the top-level 'assistant' key to 'agent' and updates the nested 'enabled_in_assistant' field to 'enabled_in_text_threads' under edit_predictions. It uses two focused matches to perform the changes.
Changes agent.preferred_completion_mode value 'max' to 'burn' when present under the 'agent' object. The migration is narrowly scoped to that specific key/value.

Augments context_servers entries by inserting a 'source' field set to 'custom' if a 'command' exists or 'extension' otherwise, and injects an empty 'settings' object when neither 'command' nor 'settings' is present. It computes insertion points and indentation and skips entries already specifying 'source'.

Removes 'version' fields from 'agent' and language_models providers (anthropic/openai), carefully adjusting adjacent commas and absorbing whitespace/comments. This avoids leaving dangling commas and preserves formatting.

Flattens context_servers.*.command objects into sibling keys ('command', and optional 'args' and 'env'), preserving indentation and reducing nested indentation in multi-line values. Only the command pair is replaced, leaving other server settings intact.
Migrates 'drag_and_drop_selection' from a boolean to an object form by replacing the value with { enabled: <bool> }. It only triggers when the existing value is a plain true/false.

Converts formatter code_actions configurations (object or array forms) into an array of entries like { code_action: '<name>' }, preserving indentation and removing empty code_actions blocks when applicable. It collects enabled code actions from the object and rewrites or deletes the matched span.

Programmatically migrates configurations where 'format_on_save' encodes a formatter by moving that value to a new 'formatter' field and setting 'format_on_save' to 'on', erroring if a 'formatter' is already present. The transformation is applied at the root and per-language under 'languages.*'.

Stateful streaming parser that extracts code-fenced content from model output, emitting NewTextChunk events as text inside the first ``` block arrives and handling partial chunks and finishing. It trims trailing fence characters, skips optional language tags, and best-effort handles malformed suffixes. Includes randomized chunking tests for robustness.

Format-agnostic edit parser that streams model output into OldText/NewText events using either XML-like tags or diff-fenced markers, with metrics for tag mismatches. It selects an optimal format per model, tracks state machines for both formats, and supports optional line hints. This is core to applying model-generated edits reliably.

Incremental fuzzy matcher that consumes query lines chunk-by-chunk and locates the best matching buffer range using a dynamic-programming search with costs for edit operations. It supports a line_hint to bias selection and resolves matches even with partial input or fuzziness. Used to map model-provided context back to the buffer.

Reusable UI header component for tool call cards displaying icon, primary/secondary text, optional code path, disclosure affordance, loading animation, and error tooltip. Encapsulates styling and inline animation behavior.

Collapsible UI container that limits displayed content to a fixed number of lines with optional gradient fade and a toggle button. Exposes a callback on expand/collapse and adapts icon/tooltip accordingly.

Unified tool that dynamically delegates to ListHistoryTool or MemoryTool based on input, forwarding schema, confirmation, UI text, and execution. Simplifies invoking context-management operations via a single tool entry point.

Assistant tool that outputs a markdown summary of recent conversation messages with indices, roles, kinds, character counts, and optional full content. It clamps parameters, pulls messages from the model request, and formats an overview table plus JSON metadata.

Conversation memory tool supporting store/load/list/restore/prune/stats of archived message ranges, with persistent storage, placeholder parsing via regex, and optional auto-summary. Manages a global memory store, file-backed persistence, and operations that modify thread content via placeholders.
Fixture code modeling git blame parsing and structures used in edit-agent evaluations after an edit. Provides realistic parsing logic and data structures for test scenarios.
Fixture file representing code state before an edit in git blame parsing, used to evaluate edit-agent correctness. Contains async process spawning and error handling for git blame output.
Pre-edit fixture for evaluating extraction logic within a larger blame parsing example. Serves as test input for edit-agent behavior.
Large graphics-related fixture (font-kit Canvas) used as input for edit-agent tests. Provides realistic, complex code to stress parsing and transformation.
Fixture mirroring a graphics module with rich comments, used to test documentation translation or comment edits by the agent. Not used in production logic.
Python unit tests for a reactive cell exercise used as evaluation data. Validates callback and dependency behavior across inputs and computed cells.

Core audio subsystem managing output stream/mixer, echo cancellation integration, microphone capture pipeline (denoise, AGC), and replay buffering for diagnostics. Provides APIs to play sounds/VOIP streams, save replays, and initialize live settings across platforms with conditional dependencies.

Audio settings model with live, atomic flags for denoise and auto volume controls tied to the settings store and updated via observers. Exposes a LiveSettings singleton for audio threads and initializes values on startup.

Infrastructure to capture and package recent audio streams into a tar of WAV files, retaining only active streams and returning path and longest duration. Uses background executor and rodio replay sources.

Extends rodio Source with utilities for buffer inspection/processing, constant sample rate/params, channel folding to mono, denoise, bounded sample taking, and creating replayable sources. Implements internal queueing and conversion wrappers used by the audio pipeline.

Cross-platform auto-updater managing version checks, polling, downloading, and installation flow with UI hooks and release notes access. Handles environment/channel nuances, Windows-specific restart/finalization, and macOS disk image mounting/unmounting.
Windows-only helper executable entrypoint that drives the update process in a separate process, showing a dialog and handling errors. Non-Windows builds provide a no-op main.

Win32 dialog implementation for the updater with a progress bar, custom font rendering, and message loop integration. Receives job updates via custom window messages and displays errors via message boxes.

Windows updater jobs that remove old files, copy new binaries, and clean up installer folders with retry/timeout logic, posting progress messages to the dialog. Optionally relaunches the app post-update and includes tests for timeouts.

UI glue for auto-update, including in-app release notes rendering for stable/preview and a notification prompting to view notes after an automatic update. Integrates with workspace/editor to show markdown preview.

Adapter that bridges the app's HttpClient to AWS Smithy runtime by implementing a connector and client returning SharedHttpConnector. Converts between AsyncBody and AWS SdkBody for request/response bodies.

AWS Bedrock integration that streams completions via converse_stream, maps request fields (messages, tools, reasoning), and converts between serde_json Value and AWS Document. Wraps errors and provides a typed streaming response interface.

Defines Bedrock model enums, modes, and configuration with mappings between human-friendly IDs and Bedrock request IDs, including thinking variants and cache options. Provides defaults and helpers for model selection by region.

Toolbar breadcrumbs component rendering a truncated, styled path with highlights and an outline toggle for editors. Subscribes to item events to update location and styling (e.g., bold dirty filename).

Global ActiveCall manager coordinating room lifecycle, invites, incoming call handling, and event subscriptions across workspaces. Provides debounced join logic, tracks pending operations, and emits UI events; integrates with audio and client layers.

Data models for local and remote call participants, including location variants, roles, track management, and convenience methods (e.g., can_write, has_video_tracks). Parses proto locations to runtime enums.

Represents a collaborative remote buffer bound to a channel, applying incoming ops, sending local changes, acknowledging versions with debounce, and tracking collaborators. Manages connection subscription lifecycle and emits buffer/channel events.

ChannelStore maintains channel metadata/index, participants, invitations, and connection state, subscribing to server updates and handling reconnects/timeouts. Exposes ordered traversal, waits for initial load, opens buffers, and emits events.
Unit tests validating ChannelStore ordering, order-independence across permutations, and deletion of dangling paths. Builds a test environment and asserts structured channel listings.
Index structure tracking channels by ID and a sorted order vector, with bulk insert guard ensuring stable sort and uniqueness based on parent path and order. Supports deletions and order retrieval.

CLI entrypoint for Zed that detects/launches the app or runs in foreground, handles IPC handshake, argument parsing (paths, diff, WSL, uninstall), and environment handling across platforms. Includes URL/path normalization and special modes like askpass.

Proxy connector that parses a proxy URL to either SOCKS or HTTP, establishes a TCP connection, then wraps the stream using the appropriate handshake. Avoids insecure fallback on parse errors and returns an AsyncReadWrite stream.

Telemetry subsystem managing event queueing, coalescing, periodic flushing, and metadata (IDs, versions, OS) with settings-driven enablement. Integrates with app lifecycle, writes a log file, and exposes helpers for usage and session initialization.

Test utilities for the client: a FakeServer that simulates HTTP auth and in-memory RPC connections, allowing controlled responses and connection behavior. Provides helpers to receive/send envelopes and build a UserStore in tests.

UserStore managing users, contacts, plan usage, and authenticated user state, reacting to client status changes and cloud API responses. Emits events for contact changes and maintains participant indices and invite info.
Helpers to build environment-aware URLs (account, upgrade, docs) based on the configured server URL. Centralizes link construction for UI.

HTTP/HTTPS proxy connector that issues a CONNECT request (optionally with Basic auth) and, for HTTPS proxies, wraps the TCP stream with TLS before tunneling. Parses and validates HTTP responses with basic limits and includes unit tests.

SOCKS4/SOCKS5 proxy connector supporting user identification (v4) and username/password auth (v5), with optional local DNS resolution. Adapts rpc_host to TargetAddr and returns a wrapped stream; includes parsing tests.

Utility that coalesces bursts of events into time periods per environment to reduce telemetry volume, with a timeout and simulated minimal duration for single events. Provides tests covering timeout and environment-switch behavior.

Implements Lamport timestamps and a vector clock (Global) for causality tracking across replicas, with operations to observe, join, meet, and compare clocks. Provides iteration, conversion, and debug utilities used throughout collaborative features.
Abstracts a SystemClock over std::time::Instant with a real implementation and a test-only fake clock supporting manual advancement. Enables deterministic timing in tests and pluggable timestamps.

Cloud API client handling authenticated HTTP requests and WebSocket connections to Zed Cloud, managing credentials and building signed requests. Provides endpoints like get_authenticated_user, create_llm_token, validate_credentials.

Wrapper for a yawc WebSocket connection that splits send/receive, spawns a task emitting parsed MessageToClient frames, and sends periodic keepalive pings. Returns a stream of messages and a task handle.

Shared types for cloud API responses (user, plan, tokens), a header constant for system ID, and helpers to derive Plan from plan versions. Used across client and services to serialize/deserialize API payloads.
RFC 3339 timestamp wrapper that serializes with millisecond precision and deserializes various forms, converting to UTC. Includes comprehensive round-trip and format tests.

LLM client type definitions and headers for telemetry and quotas, including plan enums, usage limits, completion bodies/events/status, and request metadata. Central to interacting with Zed's LLM services and enforcing limits.

Defines a highly optimized, scrollable list element for uniform-height items that measures one item to layout all, and lazily renders only visible ranges. Includes a scroll handle with strategies (Top/Center/Bottom), y-flip awareness, and integrates with Interactivity and sizing behaviors.

Represents a keybinding mapping a sequence of keystrokes to an action with optional context predicate and metadata. Provides parsing via a platform keyboard mapper, partial/complete matching, cloning of boxed actions, and accessors for keybinding data.

Implements KeyContext and a small predicate language (with ==, !=, &&, ||, !, and descendant) to resolve whether actions should dispatch in a given element context stack. Includes parser, evaluator with depth scoring, and helpers to manage context entries.

Defines application menu types (Menu, OsMenu, MenuItem) and owned equivalents, including OS-recognized system menus and actions with optional OsAction hints. Wires platform callbacks to clear keystrokes, validate commands, and dispatch actions when the OS menu is used.

Declares traits for platform-specific keyboard layout identification and keystroke mapping, plus a dummy mapper implementation. The mapper can translate key equivalents and provide layout-specific equivalence tables.

Defines Keystroke and KeybindingKeystroke with robust parsing, display, and matching semantics across IME/platform differences, including simulated IME and error reporting. Supports serializing/deserializing keystrokes, unparse, and matching against user-typed events.

Top-level macOS platform module re-exporting subsystems (dispatcher, display, events, keyboard, renderer) and providing Cocoa/ObjC interop utilities (NSString/NSRange bridging and pixel conversions). It abstracts platform specifics behind unified types used throughout GPUI.

Implements cross-platform screen capture on Linux/Windows using scap, exposing sources and streams via async channels and dedicated threads. Converts scap frames to GPUI types, manages stream lifecycles, and supports a default target selection (including Wayland prompting).

Encapsulates OpenType feature configuration with tag/value pairs, offering helpers (e.g., disable ligatures) and serde/JSON Schema support with validation. Provides query APIs and a Debug representation keyed by feature tags.

Defines ShapedLine and WrappedLine with decoration runs and painting routines for text and backgrounds, handling alignment, wrapping boundaries, underlines, and strikethrough rendering. Central to text painting, it orchestrates glyph positioning, layer painting, and decorations across wraps.

Models a laid-out line with shaped runs and glyphs, providing hit-testing (index/x mapping), font lookup by index, and a wrap boundary computation respecting word breaks and width constraints. Also defines the wrapped layout abstraction and utilities for position-to-index mapping across wrapped lines.

Implements a performant line wrapper and truncator that calculates character widths via the platform text system with caching and language-aware word character heuristics. Supports wrapping mixed fragments (text/elements) and returns wrap boundaries/indents or truncated text with updated runs.

Provides a prompt abstraction with event emissions and focus management and a default in-GPUI fallback renderer. It wires selection responses back into window focus state and supports a builder hook for custom prompt rendering.

Thin Apple compatibility layer to construct a Blade renderer using raw_window_handle on macOS. Wraps a BladeContext and produces a configured BladeRenderer for a view with given bounds and transparency.

GPU atlas implementation on Blade that allocates textures, packs tiles with etagere, and uploads data via a BufferBelt, flushing before/after frames. Manages tile lifetimes, texture initialization, and exposes raw texture views to the renderer.

Initializes a Blade graphics context, optionally honoring a forced PCI device ID from an environment variable with validation and error reporting. Includes a helper to parse hex device IDs and tests for it.

Defines GPU render pipelines and shader data for quads, shadows, paths, sprites, underlines, and video surfaces using Blade, with per-pass buffers and blending rules. It is the core renderer marshalling scene primitives into GPU draw calls with multisampling and premultiplied alpha handling.

Implements a Linux dispatcher using calloop for main-thread tasks and timers, plus a pool of background worker threads. Provides dispatch, delayed execution, and park/unpark semantics integrated with GPUI’s executors.

Abstracts platform functionality for Linux (Wayland/X11) including executors, text system, menus, clipboard, windows, and prompts, delegating to client implementations. Handles compositor info, restart logic, file dialogs via portals, and integrates keyboard mapping/layout.

Text system implementation for Linux using cosmic-text for shaping and swash for rasterization, with font family loading, feature support, and emoji handling. Exposes metrics, glyph queries, raster bounds, and line layout, caching family candidates for performance.
Maps GPUI cursor styles to Wayland cursor shapes for Wayland-based compositors. Provides a simple conversion utility used by the Wayland client.

Provides a calloop event source feeding XDG Desktop Portal settings (color scheme and cursor tweaks) into GPUI via the background executor. Emits WindowAppearance and cursor-related events and updates on changes.
Bridges missing Cocoa APIs for NSAttributedString/NSMutableAttributedString to support rich text clipboard operations. Offers methods to append attributed strings and export RTF/RTFD data.
macOS dispatcher built on Grand Central Dispatch to run tasks on global queues or the main queue, with delayed execution and parking. Includes a C trampoline to run async_task Runnable instances.
Wraps macOS displays, retrieving bounds and UUIDs and providing primary/all display enumeration. Implements PlatformDisplay to supply ID, UUID, and pixel bounds.
Encapsulates CVDisplayLink for frame-synced callbacks, dispatching frame events onto the main queue via a dispatch source. Manages start/stop and ensures safe teardown to avoid segfaults.

Translates NSEvents into GPUI PlatformInput events, including keys (with modifiers), mouse, gesture-based navigation, and scroll with phases and pixel/line granularity. Includes native key symbol mapping for function keys and special keys.

Implements macOS keyboard layout and mapping with key-equivalent remapping based on Apple’s behavior, providing layout IDs/names and key-equivalents tables. The mapper can translate keystrokes to display-oriented keys respecting use_key_equivalents.

Metal-based atlas for sprites/glyphs, allocating textures with etagere, uploading regions, and managing reference counts per tile. Supports monochrome and polychrome textures and exposes the underlying Metal textures.

Primary Metal renderer setting up pipelines, buffers, and a CAMetalLayer, and drawing quads, paths, underlines, sprites, and video surfaces with optional MSAA. Integrates a Metal atlas and instance buffer pool, and compiles shaders at build/runtime.

Applies OpenType features and font fallback cascades on macOS using CoreText descriptors, incorporating user-provided fallbacks and system defaults based on preferred languages. Produces a modified font for subsequent layout/rendering.

Implements screen capture using ScreenCaptureKit, exposing display sources with metadata and streaming frames to a client callback. Manages Objective-C delegates/blocks and stream lifecycles with proper cleanup.

Creates a macOS status bar item backed by a custom NSView that renders a Scene via the platform renderer and forwards input events. Exposes basic window-like APIs for bounds, appearance changes, and event callbacks.

Text system for macOS built on font-kit/CoreText that loads families with features and fallbacks, selects best matches, and provides metrics, glyph rasterization, and line layout. Includes defensive checks against problematic fonts and conversions to GPUI structures.
Maps AppKit NSAppearance names to GPUI’s WindowAppearance variants, defaulting to Light for unknown values. Provides the bridging needed to reflect macOS theme in GPUI.

Deterministic test dispatcher simulating foreground/background execution, delays, and randomized scheduling with park/unpark and time control. Supports deprioritization by TaskLabel and tools to debug blocking behavior.

Implements a test Platform with in-memory executors, windows, clipboard, prompts, and stubbed screen capture. Enables driving GPUI behavior in tests, including simulating prompt choices and window focus changes.

In-memory PlatformWindow for tests that simulates resize, input, activation, fullscreen toggling, and provides a simple atlas. Offers hooks to install callbacks and to drive window events during testing.

Windows clipboard integration to read/write text, images, and file lists, including app-specific metadata and content hashing. Selects best available format by enumerating formats and can convert various image formats to PNG for interoperability.
Builds and updates Windows Jump Lists with recent folders and dock menu actions via COM interfaces, handling removed entries. Creates shell links with arguments, titles, and optional icons.

Direct3D 11 atlas implementation managing texture allocation, SRV creation, and region uploads, with separate monochrome/polychrome pools. Handles device-loss by rebuilding resources and tracks tile lifetimes for cleanup.

Creates a D3D11 device/context with feature checks, selects an adapter, and exposes a retry mechanism to recover from device loss. Logs GPU and feature levels and ensures required StructuredBuffer support.
Windows dispatcher using ThreadPool for background work and PostMessage to signal the main thread, with delayed execution via ThreadPoolTimer. Provides park/unpark and validates main thread identity.

Enumerates Windows monitors, computing logical/physical bounds, scale factors, and stable UUIDs, and implements PlatformDisplay. Offers utilities to find the primary monitor and validate bounds containment.

Windows keyboard layout/mapper mapping between characters and virtual keys, including shifted equivalents computed with ToUnicode, and layout name discovery. Supports key-equivalent mapping for US layout and resolving display keys from vkeys with modifier normalization.
CLI tool that compiles, validates, and packages a Zed extension by building WASM, testing grammars/languages/themes, copying resources, and emitting a manifest and tar archive.
Criterion benchmark that compiles a test extension and measures loading performance in the Wasm host using a controlled test app context and fake HTTP client.
Validates and enforces runtime capabilities (process exec, download, npm install) for extensions, checking both extension manifest allowances and host-granted permissions.
Defines settings controlling auto-install and auto-update of extensions and integrates with the global settings store to determine extension management behavior.
Integration test scaffolding for the extension store, creating a fake filesystem with sample extensions and verifying indexing of manifests, languages, grammars, and themes.
Manages headless extension lifecycle: synchronizes installed versions, loads manifests, registers languages and language servers, and handles install/uninstall with filesystem operations.
Core Wasm host that instantiates extensions, mediates API calls (LSP, slash commands, debug), manages capabilities and host proxies, and bridges WASI/component interfaces.
Versioned WIT bindings broker that selects and instantiates the correct extension API version, enforces supported API ranges, and maps calls across versions.
WIT bindings for the v0.0.1 API, bridging basic worktree and platform/node functionality and translating types to the latest representation.
WIT bindings for v0.0.4 API with download, node, platform, and language server status integration, including type conversions to latest API shapes.
WIT bindings for v0.0.6 introducing LSP integration via since_v0_1_0, settings, and extended type conversions for commands and labels.
WIT bindings for v0.1.0 adding HTTP client streaming, key-value store delegation, slash commands, and extensive type mappings to internal models.
WIT bindings for v0.2.0 enhancing project and worktree APIs, HTTP client support, and key-value store, with conversions to latest API types.
WIT bindings for v0.3.0 adding process and common module support and maintaining conversions for labels, settings, and language server status.
WIT bindings for v0.4.0 similar to v0.3.0 with updated module paths and continued type conversions for settings and downloads.
WIT bindings for v0.5.0 adding context server module support and consistent conversions for debugging and settings APIs.
Latest WIT bindings with max version 0.7.0, covering debug adapter/task integrations, TCP templates, build tasks, and comprehensive type translations.
Suggests relevant extensions for files based on name or extension, prompting installation with persistable dismissal via a key-value store.
Picker UI for selecting an extension version, filtering with fuzzy match, enforcing compatibility, and updating settings to disable auto-update on manual selection.
UI component for rendering an extension card with optional overlay indicating override by a dev extension.
UI component to present feature upsell banners with optional documentation link and custom actions.
Feature flag infrastructure with staff overrides, async waiting, subscriptions, and helpers for views and app to observe and gate behavior.
Registers workspace actions to submit feedback, open repo links, and copy system specs, orchestrating UI prompts and clipboard interactions.
Modal UI to present feedback channels (bug report, feature request, email, repo) with dismissal and event telemetry hooks.
File finder settings model mapping JSON schema to runtime config for icons, modal width, focus behavior, and ignore rules.
Path picker delegate that lists directories, supports creation, hidden entries, fuzzy filtering, and OS-specific path styles with completion behaviors.
Tests verifying open path prompt matching and completion behaviors across POSIX and Windows path styles and remote scenarios.
Resolves file and folder icons from the active icon theme based on file name, suffix, and hidden file handling, with fallbacks to defaults.
Fake Git repository implementation backed by a fake filesystem, simulating index/head content, status, blames, and refs for testing git workflows.
Filesystem watcher registering notify watchers per path, collecting and debouncing path events, and exposing a global watcher API across platforms.
Mac-specific FSEvents-based watcher that manages event streams and handles path registration and removal with latency control.
Low-level macOS FSEvents wrapper managing CFRunLoop, stream lifecycle, event parsing, and automatic stream restart on dropped events.
Efficient character bag representation tracking letter counts, digits, and dash to prefilter fuzzy candidates with bit ops.
Core fuzzy matcher scoring algorithm that aligns query to candidate chars with distance penalties, smart-case, memoization, and match position extraction.
Fuzzy path matching across candidate sets with parallel segmentation, prefix handling, relative distance ranking, and Windows path normalization.
Fuzzy string matching utility that segments candidates across CPUs, returns ranked matches with contiguous highlight ranges and supports smart-case/length penalties.
Runs git blame with custom contents, parses incremental output into structured entries, loads commit messages, and computes author timestamps with timezone.
Retrieves commit messages via 'git show' with chunking on Windows, parses 'git diff --name-status -z', and includes tests for diff parsing.
Defines git action types, constants, Oid wrapper with conversions and serialization, and re-exports modules for repository interactions.
Abstracts Git hosting providers with permalink building, PR extraction, avatar URLs, and a global registry to register and select providers by URL.
Parses Git remote URLs, rewriting scp-like forms to ssh URLs and providing tests for valid/invalid URL patterns.
Parses stash entries from null-separated strings into structured data and provides a GitStash model with error handling and tests.
Models file status and staging summaries, provides conversion from git status bytes, utilities to classify changes, and summary aggregation.
Initializes default hosting providers and registers additional self-hosted ones based on repository origin URL, with helper to extract host from remotes.
Reads provider settings from the settings store to populate and update the registry with custom hosting providers and base URLs.
Bitbucket provider implementation parsing remotes, building commit/file permalinks, extracting PR references from messages, and tests.
Chromium (Gerrit) provider building permalinks, extracting review URLs from commit messages, and fetching author avatars via REST with XSSI handling.
Codeberg provider parsing remotes, building permalinks, and fetching commit author avatars via API with optional token auth and error handling.
Gitee provider parsing remotes, building commit/blob permalinks, and tests covering URLs and line fragment formatting.
GitHub provider handling public and self-hosted instances, parsing remotes, building permalinks with md/plain logic, PR extraction, and avatar fetch via API.
GitLab provider supporting public and self-hosted origins, parsing nested group paths, building permalinks with md/plain handling, and tests.
Sourcehut provider parsing ~owner remotes without trimming .git, building commit/tree permalinks, and tests for URL and fragment behavior.
Modal prompting for credentials in git operations, masking input as needed and providing helpful hints linking to GitHub auth docs.
Renders git blame in editor gutter and tooltips, with avatars, commit popovers, and actions to open commit views and context menus.
Branch selection picker with fuzzy filtering, recent branches, and actions to switch or create branches, listening to repo updates.
Commit modal managing amend/signoff states, commit editor synchronization, branch selection, and tailored UI actions within workspace panels.
Commit tooltip showing avatar, author, message, time, PR link, and actions to open commit view, loading remote avatar via provider API.
Commit view displaying diff hunks across files using multibuffer excerpts, resolving project paths, and supporting navigation and search integration.
Editor addon that highlights merge conflicts with custom blocks and row highlights, reacting to conflict set updates and excerpt changes.
Standalone diff view between two buffers, recalculating diffs on edits with debounce and integrating into workspace item lifecycle.
Settings for the Git panel including button visibility, dock position, default width, status style, scrollbar behavior, and VSCode import mapping.
Bootstraps Git UI features, registering panels, pickers, actions (fetch/push/pull/stash/etc.), conflict rendering, and onboarding modal.
Modal introducing native git support with CTA to open panel and link to blog, emitting telemetry on interactions.
Generic picker prompt with fuzzy matching for option selection, returning the selected index via oneshot channel and dismissing correctly.
Formats remote command outputs into user messages, inferring result style (toast/log/PR link) by parsing stdout/stderr and extracting URLs.
Modal picker to select an active repository from the project's git store with non-searchable list and simple filtering placeholder.
Picker for viewing and managing git stash entries with fuzzy search, timestamps formatting, and actions to drop, pop, or apply stash.
Diff view between clipboard and selected text region, updating live on source buffer edits with debounce and showing excerpts in a multibuffer.
Status bar component showing caret position and selection stats, with click-to-open go-to-line modal and debounce for singleton buffers.
Go-to-line modal that parses row/column input, highlights and autoscrolls to the target, and updates editor selections with tab/confirm handling.
Client for Google Generative Language API supporting streaming generation, token counting, request validation, and rich request/response models.
Example app demonstrating GPUI animation APIs by rotating an SVG using easing and repeat behaviors.
Example rendering a large uniform list with custom scrollbar and interactive rows, showcasing performance considerations.
Example demonstrating drag-and-drop interactions with draggable items and a drop target updating visuals on drop.
Simple example displaying a GIF with containment using GPUI image rendering.
Example showcasing solid colors and linear gradients in different color spaces and canvas drawing.
Example demonstrating CSS-like grid layout by rendering a 'holy grail' web design layout.
Basic example rendering styled text and colored boxes, illustrating simple GPUI composition.
Example of manual and automatic image caching strategies, loading many images and toggling cache to test memory usage.
Example showing image asset loading with delays, fallbacks, and removal of cached assets.
Rich text input example implementing selection, grapheme navigation, IME-marked text handling, and clipboard actions via custom input handler.
Example illustrating quitting the app when all windows are closed, binding cmd-w to close window.
Example animating a panel's opacity with a background task and showcasing assets loading.
Example drawing paths, gradients, and shapes on canvas with custom shadows and hitboxes.
Benchmark-like example painting many gradient paths to stress rendering performance.
Example rendering slashed patterns and gradients, demonstrating background pattern utilities.
Example showing nested scrollable areas with vertical and horizontal scrolling behavior.
Example demonstrating setting application menus and quitting via menu actions.
Example showcasing box shadows on various shapes and preset shadow utilities with labeled displays.
Example demonstrating focus handling, tab stop order, and keybindings for tab navigation.
Typography example exploring specimen rendering, character grid, global text context, and scaling with type scale.
Example demonstrating text alignment, decoration, truncation, and layout within borders.
Example showing ellipsis, line clamps, truncation, nowrap, and text overflow behaviors.
Example rendering a deep nested div hierarchy to test GPUI's handling of deep trees.
Example using uniform_list to render a list efficiently with click handlers and virtualization.
Example demonstrating opening windows of various kinds, prompts, resizing, and window-level actions.
Example creating multiple popup windows positioned across displays, showing bounds and transparent backgrounds.
Example implementing client-side window decorations with custom shadows, hitboxes, cursor styles, and draggable titlebar.
Documentation explaining GPUI's ownership model, entity contexts, notify/observe versus emit/subscribe patterns, with illustrative examples.

Bootstraps the channel system by initializing the ChannelStore and ChannelBuffer, wiring them to the Client and UserStore. Re-exports channel-related types and events to unify the interface for messaging and buffering.

Defines the IPC handshake and CLI request/response protocol for opening paths/URLs and communicating stdout/stderr and exit status. Includes a flag to force CLI mode when running outside an app bundle.
Specifies the Cloud WebSocket protocol version and header, and defines MessageToClient with CBOR serialization/deserialization helpers. Currently supports user refresh notifications.
Placeholder module importing RPC proto types, likely for collaborative completion integrations. No logic is implemented here.
Extends tide::Result with context and with_context methods, bridging Tide errors with anyhow for richer error messages. Wraps original errors preserving status codes.

Provides an Executor abstraction that spawns tasks and sleeps using tokio in production or a deterministic BackgroundExecutor in tests. Enables consistent async behavior and controllable timing in test environments.
Declares the llm::db submodule for collaborative LLM features. Acts as a module scaffold.
Command-line utility that prints environment variable exports from dotenv files, adapting output for PowerShell or POSIX shells. Useful for local development setup.
Organizes and exposes database query modules for various entities (buffers, channels, projects, users, etc.). Serves as the entry point to query logic.
Declares SeaORM entity modules for a wide range of collaborative features, including buffers, channels, notifications, projects, and worktrees. Centralizes schema mapping for persistence.
SeaORM model for access tokens with user linkage and optional impersonation, including relations to users. Encapsulates token hashing and ownership metadata.

SeaORM model for buffer operations with a compound primary key capturing epoch, Lamport timestamp, and replica ID, related to a buffer. Persists CRDT-like operation payloads for collaborative editing.
SeaORM model for buffer snapshots storing text and operation serialization version by epoch, linked to buffers. Enables consistent state recovery and checkpointing in collaboration.
SeaORM model for user contacts and notification flags, relating users through room participants. Tracks invite/accept states and directionality.
SeaORM model recording CLA-signing contributors with signed_at timestamps and relation to users. Used for compliance tracking.
SeaORM model storing vector embeddings by model and digest with dimensions and retrieval time. Supports feature embedding caching and reuse.
SeaORM model for extensions with metadata such as external ID, name, and download statistics, and a relation to the latest version. Forms the basis of extension catalog management.
SeaORM model for language servers per project with capabilities and optional worktree association, related to projects. Records installed servers and their features.
SeaORM model for notifications including kind, recipient, content, read state, and optional response. Relates to users for delivery and tracking.
SeaORM model listing notification kinds by ID and name for categorization. Provides a simple lookup table.
SeaORM model representing servers and their environment classification. Minimal schema for deployment contexts.
SeaORM model tracking signups with email verification, platform flags, and optional user associations. Supports onboarding flow state.
SeaORM model for project worktrees with paths, visibility, and scan tracking, linked to projects. Persists indexing state across scans.
SeaORM model summarizing diagnostics per file and language server within a worktree. Stores error and warning counts for quick status views.
SeaORM model for worktree entries capturing file metadata, git status, and scan IDs, keyed by project/worktree. Drives file indexing and project panel views.
Initializes collaboration-related notifications UI by registering incoming call and project shared notifications. Provides feature-gated stories for development.
Re-exports collaborative notification stories for UI demos under the stories feature. No logic beyond module exposure.
Defines Fx-based HashMap/HashSet aliases and re-exports indexmap and std::collections for performance-optimized containers. Serves as a uniform collections facade.
Specifies a Transport trait with async send and streaming receive/receive_err, and exposes a stdio transport implementation. Abstracts message I/O for the context server.
Declares types for inline value lookups in debugging, including variable vs expression and local vs global scopes with source positions. Forms the data model for rendering inline debug values.
Initializes debugger logging tools by wiring the DAP log component into the app. Serves as a minimal bootstrap.
Demonstrates denoising an audio wav by resampling and processing with Denoiser, writing output to a file. Example-only code.
Shows periodically toggling the denoiser enabled state while processing audio, writing the result to a file. Example-only code.
Declares the git::blame module for editor integrations. Acts as a stub for Git functionality.
Provides helpers to read or generate persistent UUIDs stored on disk, creating parent dirs as needed. Defines default paths under the local data directory for system and installation IDs.
Defines the ExtensionCapability enum for process execution, file download, and npm install, with serde tagging. Establishes the contract and serialization for extension capabilities.
Encapsulates configuration for setting up a context server, including installation instructions, a JSON schema, and default settings template. Used by extensions to guide user setup.
Re-exports debugging-related types and templates for adapters, tasks, and requests, forming the extension API for DAP integration. Consolidates debug configuration interfaces.
Defines language and LSP settings structures, including binary config, initialization options, and server settings with serde support. Serves the WIT-based extension API schema.
Provides updated language and LSP settings schemas mirroring earlier versions, defining binary path/arguments and JSON options. Used by newer WIT API versions.
Collects and re-exports UI components like extension cards and feature upsells for the extensions interface. Acts as the components entry module.
Declares feature flag markers for various experimental or gated features, each implementing a common FeatureFlag trait with unique names. Centralizes feature toggles.
MacOS-only example that streams and prints file system events for supplied paths, falling back with a message on non-macOS. Demonstrates usage of EventStream.
Aggregates fuzzy matching modules and re-exports key types and functions for path and string matching. Provides the core fuzzy search API used across the project.
Defines and re-exports provider modules for common git hosting services (GitHub, GitLab, etc.). Standardizes provider-specific integrations.
Example demonstrating GPUI entity ownership, event emission, and subscription behavior, validating state updates via emitted changes. Intended for learning and testing.
Exports the GPUI prelude of widely used traits and types to simplify imports across applications. Provides a canonical import surface for GPUI.
Defines SharedUri as a SharedString wrapper with Deref, Display, Debug, and From conversions for URIs. Lightweight typed string abstraction for URIs.
Collects and re-exports core UI element modules (div, text, svg, canvas, lists, etc.), forming the GPUI element catalog. Centralizes UI building blocks.
Groups macOS-specific rendering modules (blade atlas/context/renderer) with Apple compatibility shims. Encapsulates platform graphics backend.
Organizes Linux platform subsystems (dispatcher, keyboard, Wayland/X11, text system, headless) with conditional compilation and screen-capture frame types. Provides the Linux GPUI backend.
Exposes test platform modules (dispatcher, display, window) and screen capture test types to simulate platform behavior. Supports deterministic UI testing.
Defines the Windows GPUI backend components (DirectX renderer/devices, clipboard, input, windowing) with optional screen capture frame types. Aggregates platform-specific subsystems.
Introduces FontFallbacks, a serde-enabled list of fallback font family names with accessor and constructor helpers. Used to configure font fallback chains.
Re-exports the Linux headless client module for offscreen or test rendering. Minimal platform wiring.
Implements a LinuxKeyboardLayout conforming to PlatformKeyboardLayout, exposing ID and name. Provides a simple layout representation for Linux input.
Collects X11-specific client, display, event, window, and XIM handler modules for the Linux backend. Re-exports components for integration.
Implements a TestDisplay with a fixed ID, random UUID, and default bounds, conforming to PlatformDisplay. Supports display-related tests.
Provides SafeCursor and SafeHwnd wrappers that are Send/Sync and deref to raw Win32 handles, enabling safe cross-thread usage. Facilitates thread-safe Windows handle management.
Implements WaylandDisplay with hashing by wl_output ID and UUID generation from the display name, conforming to PlatformDisplay. Encapsulates display metadata and bounds.
Proc macro that derives gpui::IntoElement, returning a Component wrapper for the type. Automates element construction for GPUI components.
Proc macro that derives gpui::Render with a default no-op render returning Empty, streamlining simple component implementations. Provides a boilerplate Render impl.
Declares the wikipedia submodule for HTML-to-Markdown structure handling. Module scaffold without logic here.
Initializes and caches a rustls ClientConfig with platform verification using OnceLock, ensuring crypto provider installation. Centralizes TLS configuration for HTTP clients.
Defines ImageViewerSettings with a file size unit and loads it from the SettingsContent via gpui. Provides typed configuration for the image viewer.
In debug builds, exposes an inspector initializer; in release, registers a handler that reports unavailability and hides the toggle action. Controls dev-only inspection tooling.
Exports platform-specific CLI installation and URL scheme registration actions, skipping binary install on Windows. Entry point for CLI setup.
Defines a RegisterZedScheme action and async handler that registers the zed:// URL scheme via gpui's AsyncApp. Integrates scheme handling into the app.
Declares the keystroke_input UI component module for the keymap editor. Module aggregator.
Exposes cloud_model for language model integrations, re-exporting its contents. Module entry point.
Collects and re-exports provider modules for multiple LLM backends (OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral, etc.). Centralizes model provider integrations.
Defines and re-exports InstructionListItem for the language models UI. Provides a UI building block.
Includes generated LiveKit protocol bindings from OUT_DIR. Bridges compile-time generated code into the crate.
Defines actions and modules for markdown preview, registering the MarkdownPreviewView with the workspace and window. Orchestrates preview creation and navigation.
Includes generated macOS Objective-C bindings for media interop, gated by target_os. Provides low-level platform integration.
Declares core menu actions and provides a no-op init to prevent linker elimination of action registrations. Establishes user interaction commands for menus.
Re-exports tree-sitter-based migration patterns for keymap and settings transformations. Acts as a registry of structural edit rules.
Defines a migration that replaces the assistant tool name 'bash' with 'terminal' by matching a named capture in the settings AST. Performs targeted token substitution using tree-sitter ranges.
Renames specific assistant tools ('find_replace_file' to 'edit_file', 'regex_search' to 'grep') by matching captured names in settings. Applies selective replacements via tree-sitter.
Updates the assistant tool name 'path_search' to 'find_path' where found in settings matches. Simple capture-based rename using tree-sitter.
Comments out duplicated agent key/value pairs, expanding the range to include the trailing comma and inserting an explanatory comment. Uses tree-sitter captures to determine the edit span.
Exposes the notification_store and status_toast modules for app-wide notifications management and UI. Acts as the notifications entry point.
Collects debugger locator modules for multiple runtimes (cargo, go, node, python). Provides discovery logic for starting debug sessions per language.
Implements ReversibleIterable, offering find and reverse-find semantics over iterators, including single-ended and double-ended variants. Enables direction-aware searches in project panel logic.
Defines ProxyLaunchError with mapping to and from a custom exit code for reconnect failures. Standardizes process exit semantics for proxy startup.

Defines Mistral chat model types, capabilities, and request structures, including role enums, model IDs, token limits, and tool/image/thinking support flags. Provides conversion helpers and configuration for tool definitions and response formats for building API calls.

Implements an Anchor representing positions across multi-buffer excerpts with comparison that accounts for excerpt remapping, bias (left/right), and optional diff-base anchors. Provides conversion to offsets/points and range operations to compare, include, and overlap selections in a MultiBufferSnapshot.
Provides strongly-typed wrappers around offsets, points, and rows with phantom types to prevent mixing units. Supports arithmetic, ordering, and formatting utilities for editor coordinate math.

Implements a simple netcat-style mode that shuttles lines between stdin/stdout and a Unix socket asynchronously; on Windows it is intentionally unsupported. Uses smol to multiplex socket and stdin reads with newline framing.

Exports UnixListener/UnixStream types with cross-platform async wrappers, using smol on Unix and custom Windows adapters around synchronous AF_UNIX sockets. Provides AsyncRead/AsyncWrite impls to integrate with async I/O.

Windows-only UnixListener around AF_UNIX via WinSock that binds, listens, and accepts connections, returning a wrapped UnixStream. Bridges raw sockets to higher-level types and exposes AsSocket for integration.

Top-level net module re-exporting platform-specific Unix socket types and utilities, with tests validating both sync and async Unix sockets. Serves as the facade for consumers to use local IPC across OSes.
Windows AF_UNIX socket wrapper handling creation, accept, send/recv, and handle inheritance flags via WinSock APIs. Converts WinSock return codes to std::io::Result and ensures sockets close on drop.
Windows UnixStream implementing Read/Write and connect over AF_UNIX, plus IoSafe integration for async contexts. Adapts the raw UnixSocket to a standard stream interface.

Windows helpers to initialize WinSock once, build sockaddr_un from paths with validation, and map WinSock return values into Results. Includes careful length calculation and path copying for AF_UNIX addresses.

Manages discovery and lifecycle of a Node.js runtime (system or Zed-managed), including installing/updating, environment synchronization, and running npm commands with proxy support. Caches instances based on settings and exposes helpers to query/install npm packages with robust error handling and logging.

Stores, loads, and updates notifications using a SumTree for efficient ordered access and summary counts, emitting UI events on changes. Subscribes to client connection status and message handlers to fetch, insert, splice, and mark notifications, coordinating with user/channel stores.
UI component for status toasts with optional icon, action button, and dismiss control, emitting dismiss events on interaction. Provides preview examples and integrates with workspace toast APIs.

Defines Ollama model metadata, chat request/response types, tool call structures, and options, with helpers to estimate context length and capabilities. Implements HTTP calls to stream chat completions and to list/show models with capability detection.

Renders the onboarding page for configuring AI providers, highlighting featured providers and privacy messaging. Integrates with the language model registry and opens provider-specific configuration modals.
Implements a modal picker to select the base keymap using fuzzy matching, updating settings and dismissing on confirm. Hooks into workspace actions to toggle the selector.
Onboarding UI for choosing theme mode/themes and telemetry preferences, writing changes to settings with telemetry events. Provides interactive theme previews and system mode handling.

Onboarding UI for editor preferences such as minimap, inlay hints, git blame, fonts, ligatures, format-on-save, and settings import from other editors. Writes to settings and optimistically updates globals for responsive UI.

Toolbar hint component promoting multibuffer editing, tracking display count per session via a KV store and dismissible after a threshold. Reacts to active item changes to determine visibility and persists counts.

Wires onboarding and welcome flows into the workspace with actions to open pages, register items, and import settings from VS Code/Cursor. Manages navigation between pages and sets up global behaviors and telemetry.

UI component that renders miniature editor/theme previews (bordered, borderless, or side-by-side) using theme colors and synthetic code skeletons. Encapsulates layout constants and reusable skeleton generators.

Welcome screen UI presenting common actions (new file, open, clone, command palette) and configuration links with keybindings and focus navigation. Integrates with workspace routing back to onboarding.

Defines OpenAI model catalog with IDs, token limits, and feature flags (parallel tool calls, prompt caching, reasoning effort), plus request/message/tool schemas for chat. Includes helpers to map between IDs and structured types and to conditionally include parameters supported by models.

Defines OpenRouter model configuration, request/message/tool schemas (including reasoning options), and streaming response deltas. Implements rate limit parsing, conditional tool/parallel call support, and request building with provider/usage metadata.

Implements an outline picker modal for navigating buffer symbols, with fuzzy search, selection highlighting, and autoscroll/selection updates in the editor. Registers actions to toggle the outline and cleans up highlights on dismiss.

Maps outline panel settings from global settings content, including UI options, indent guides, and scrollbar visibility (inheriting from editor defaults). Provides VS Code settings import for icons and git decorations.
Defines traits and helpers for panel headers and tabbed panels, including standardized panel editor styling derived from theme settings. Provides small button/icon helpers for consistent panel UI.

Centralizes resolution of config/data/temp/log paths across platforms with optional custom data dir override, caching results in OnceLock. Exposes locations for settings, logs, databases, extensions, and server state, guarding initialization order and path sanitation.
Internal picker head abstraction that is either an input editor (with event subscription) or an invisible focusable head. Provides focus handling and placeholder setup for searchable pickers.

Utilities to render highlighted text matches and accompanying path segments, preserving byte-based highlight positions when concatenating parts. Offers a compact view component and tests to ensure boundary correctness with UTF-8.

Generic, async-capable picker component with a delegate trait for matches, rendering, and confirmation, supporting uniform or variable-height lists, keyboard navigation, and optional search editor. Manages background matching tasks, selection changes, and optional documentation asides, suitable for modals and embedded contexts.
Adapter to present a Picker inside a PopoverMenu with a trigger and tooltip, forwarding dismiss events and focus to the picker. Allows anchoring and handle injection for external control.

Prettier integration that locates installations/ignores within workspaces (handling monorepos and workspaces), coordinates with a background Prettier server, and defines configuration and constants. Traverses directory ancestry with guards (e.g., skip node_modules) and validates workspace roots before using a Prettier instance.

Node.js script that implements a minimal JSON-RPC-like protocol over stdio to format text with Prettier, resolving config/plugins and honoring .prettierignore. Parses framed messages with Content-Length headers and supports cache clearing and initialization commands with robust error reporting.

Manages the set of external agent (AI) servers per project, assembling commands from settings/feature flags and exposing them locally or via remote proxy. Subscribes to settings changes, publishes updates to clients, and supports both built-in and custom agents with status/version channels.

Parses color literals (hex, rgb/rgba, hsl/hsla) from LSP completion items, favoring strict full-label/detail matches and relaxed doc edge matches. Converts to theme colors with robust regexes and component parsing, verified by unit tests.

Tracks client-server connectivity and maintains remote project connections, attempting to rejoin projects on reconnect with timeout and limited retries. Orchestrates rejoin messages and disconnects projects cleanly on failure.

Coordinates context server configurations and lifecycles per project from settings or extensions, starting/stopping servers and emitting status events. Resolves commands asynchronously via a descriptor registry/worktree context and supports testable factories.

Provides a generic debounced delay utility that cancels and reschedules tasks, ensuring previous tasks complete before firing a new one after a timeout. Useful for coalescing frequent events into a single async action.

Module-level organization for the debugger subsystem, exposing stores and session components, and re-exporting test helpers when enabled. Documents the architecture separation between DAP store, sessions, and breakpoints.

Executes direnv to load environment variables (via `direnv export json`), handling errors and parsing JSON output into key->Option value deltas. Differentiates failure modes and maps them to user-facing messages for environment setup.

Manages project environment variables, preferring CLI-inherited env when available or spawning shells per directory/shell to capture env, with optional direnv integration. Caches results per path/shell, emits error events, and exposes async retrieval for buffers/worktrees.

Handles opening and tracking image files as project items, loading metadata asynchronously and reloading images when files change. Maintains mappings between project paths/entries and image IDs, emitting events for UI updates.

Maintains a trie of detected manifest roots per worktree to determine subproject roots for language/toolchain resolution, updating in response to worktree changes. Queries providers to fill unknown paths and caches presence/absence states to minimize scanning.

Manages discovery and lifecycle of Prettier instances per worktree, choosing between workspace-local or default servers and tracking ignore files. Starts/stops language servers for formatting and emits events when Prettier servers are added or removed.

Defines project-level settings structures (LSP, DAP, context servers, diagnostics, git, Node, direnv, session) and maps them from settings content. Provides conversions, enablement helpers, and severity utilities compatible with LSP and UI.

Implements project search queries for plain text or regex across buffers/projects with path include/exclude matchers, handling case sensitivity (including inline \c/\C modifiers), whole-word boundaries, and multiline detection. Provides conversions to/from protocol messages and aggregates results with limits.
