Simple search history with configurable insertion behavior and a cursor to navigate previous/next queries, capped by an optional maximum length. Includes tests for replacement semantics and multi-cursor behavior.

TaskStore orchestrates task inventories and computes task contexts (cwd, env, captured variables) for locations, supporting local and remote modes via RPC handlers. Updates user tasks/scenarios from settings and integrates with buffer/worktree and environment stores.

Creates terminal tasks locally or via remote, composing environment from CLI, settings, and toolchain activation scripts (e.g., virtualenv) and handling working directory resolution. Builds appropriate shell commands and wires task completion channels for UI.

Stores and resolves language toolchains per project path and language, supporting activation, listing (including user-defined scopes), and remote delegation via RPC. Integrates with manifest detection and project environment and emits change events.

Manages project worktrees (local or remote), handling creation, lookup, path resolution, and file operations, and broadcasting detailed events on changes. Provides RPC handlers and caching for loading worktrees, plus utilities to absolutize paths and map entries to worktrees.

Defines the request/response schema for LLM-powered code edit predictions, including excerpt context, referenced declarations with scoring components, diagnostic groups, and prompt format options. Provides event modeling for buffer changes and edit payloads, plus DebugInfo timing fields and utility serialization helpers.

Plans and generates LLM prompts from code snippets using a greedy one-pass knapsack strategy that selects signatures or full declarations based on score density and budget. Produces system prompts for different formats, merges overlapping snippets, and injects parent signatures as needed.

Defines HTTP routes for the collab API, including access token creation, RPC server snapshot, and contributors endpoints, protected by middleware that validates an admin API token. Implements custom headers (e.g., Cloudflare country, system id) and composes axum layers to attach shared state.

Implements authorization via access tokens, adding a Principal to requests and supporting admin impersonation in development. Handles token creation, SHA-256 hashing with optional scrypt migration, encryption with client public keys, verification timing metrics, and secure constant-time comparison.

Provides a high-level Database wrapper over SeaORM with transactional helpers and per-room/project locking to serialize state changes. Implements TransactionGuard semantics, background execution behavior in tests, and utilities for coordinating concurrent operations and notifications.
Loads environment variables from .env.toml files for the collab crate and injects them into the process. Parses TOML values and supports optional secret overrides.

Defines core types and configuration for the collab service, including error handling, runtime Config, service mode, and AppState initialization. Builds optional AWS S3/Kinesis clients and database connections, wiring external services and feature flags.

Entrypoint CLI that supports version, migrations, seeding, and serving API/collab modes with tracing and graceful shutdown. Initializes databases (including LLM DB), starts RPC server, registers routes, and wires periodic tasks and signal handling.
Runs database migrations via sqlx, verifying checksums of applied migrations and applying missing ones while reporting durations. Abstracts execution over AnyConnection for portability.

Seeds the database with admins and channels, fetching user metadata from GitHub and inserting contributor records. Supports idempotent behavior and optional force reseeding with basic error reporting.
Provides test helpers and modules for collab features, including language setup and utilities to inspect room participants and channel ids. Aggregates randomized tests and integration suites.
Exposes endpoints to query contributor status and list contributors, with special handling for Renovate bot. Allows adding a contributor and optional auto-joining a channel.

Handles telemetry ingestion for events and panics, validating payload checksums with a seeded hash and forwarding normalized rows to Kinesis. Computes contextual properties, includes staff flags, and gracefully accepts deprecated crash endpoints.

Serves extension listings and updates with schema/version constraints, and generates presigned S3 download URLs. Periodically scans a blob store to discover published versions, reconciling known versions in the DB.

Declares typed ID wrappers for DB entities and enums for channel roles and visibility, with helper methods for capability checks and proto conversions. Encodes role/visibility semantics used across access control.

Provides test database setup for SQLite and Postgres with migrations, teardown logic, and random failure simulation. Includes macros to run tests on both backends and utility functions for generating users.

Implements a dedicated LLM database wrapper mirroring transactional patterns from the main DB, with controlled executor behavior in tests. Provides isolation and consistent transaction lifecycle management.
Tracks active client connections, per-user connection sets, and channel subscriptions, exposing iterators for notifications. Enforces client version compatibility and cleans state on disconnect.
Implements DB operations for access tokens including creation with retention limit, retrieval, and hash updates. Uses paginated deletion of excess tokens and protects against missing records.

Manages joining and rejoining channel buffers, provisioning buffer state, collaborators, and vector-clock operations. Updates observed edits per-user and streams missing operations to resynchronize clients.

Implements channel creation, join logic, visibility changes with nesting constraints, deletion of hierarchies, and membership invitation/acceptance flows. Performs transactional access control checks and live room association.

Provides contact list retrieval with busy status, existence checks, sending and removing contact requests, and dismissing notifications. Encodes symmetric contact relationships and notification side-effects.
Queries contributor sign timestamps and inserts contributor records, considering admin users as implicitly signed. Filters users by GitHub login or ID and performs upsert-like behavior.
Reads and writes code embeddings keyed by model and digest, updating retrieval timestamps and purging stale entries. Streams rows for efficiency and handles batch insert with conflict do-nothing.

Fetches extensions with fuzzy name filtering and provides constraints, resolves latest versions per extension with schema/WASM API filtering, and records known versions. Produces metadata by joining extension/version tables.

Initializes notification kinds and provides CRUD for notifications with deduplication and marking as read with optional responses. Converts between DB models and proto types and supports lookup by composite criteria.

Maintains server records per environment, identifying and deleting stale servers and cleaning associated room/channel artifacts. Performs batched deletion of worktree-related entries tied to old servers.

Implements user creation/upsert by GitHub account, various lookups, metrics id retrieval, and flags updates like connected_once and TOS acceptance. Seeds channel membership for new users and provides pagination.
Defines the Buffer entity with epoch fields and relations to operations, snapshots, and channels. Encodes ORM relations for navigating buffer state.
Declares the Channel model with visibility, parent path, and sibling order, plus helpers to derive ancestor paths and filters. Exposes relations to room, buffer, members, and collaborators.
Represents collaborators on a channel buffer, tying user and replica to a specific server/connection. Provides conversion to ConnectionId and relation to Channel.
Tracks participants in channel chat with their server/connection and relation to Channel. Offers conversion to ConnectionId.
Models channel membership with role and acceptance flags, and relations to Channel and User. Includes a linked relation to traverse users to channels.
Stores channel messages with sender, body, timestamps, nonce, and optional reply linkage, plus relations to Channel and User.
Captures user mentions within channel messages with positions, linking to message and user entities.
Defines extension versions with metadata, schema/API versioning, provides flags, and relation to the latest extension record. Computes a set of provided features from boolean fields.
Represents follower-leader relationships within rooms/projects, storing both leader and follower connection ids. Relates to the Room entity.
Tracks the last observed buffer operation per user for resync logic, with relations to Buffer and User. Stores epoch/timestamp for vector clock reconciliation.
Records which channel messages a user has observed to manage unread counts and notifications, relating to Channel and User.
Defines the Project entity with host connection details and relations to worktrees, repositories, collaborators, and language servers. Provides a helper to construct a ConnectionId.
Stores project collaborator records with per-replica and committer info, mapping to a ConnectionId and relating to Project.
Represents repositories within a project with path, entry ids, merge/conflict metadata, and tracking flags. Relates to Project.
Models repository status entries with kind-specific fields supporting tracked/untracked/ignored/unmerged states and deletion flags.
Defines the Room entity with LiveKit id and optional channel linkage, plus relations to participants, projects, and followers.
Represents room participants with answering/calling connection details, optional role and location, and relations to User and Room. Provides helper for answering ConnectionId.
Declares the User model with GitHub and app metadata, metrics id, admin status, and relations to tokens, projects, channels, and contributor. Adds helpers for account creation time and age.
Stores per-worktree settings files with content and kind (settings/tasks/editorconfig/debug), keyed by project/worktree/path.

Implements the ChannelView that wraps an Editor for a channel buffer, wiring collaboration hub, markdown language selection, context menu actions, and deep-linking to section positions. Subscribes to channel buffer events and synchronizes UI state.
Initializes collaboration UI components (panel, notifications, channel view) and provides window options for notification popups. Registers settings for panel configuration.
Renders a notification panel with streaming updates, lazy loading, mark-as-read flows, and toast handling. Persists width settings and presents notifications with actor context and response actions.
Defines settings structures for collaboration and notification panels, parsing from global settings content to control button visibility, dock placement, and default widths.

Provides a channel management modal to toggle visibility, copy links, invite/manage members, and render filtered user lists with context menus. Integrates with ChannelStore actions and picker navigation.
Implements a picker-based UI for inviting or removing contacts by fuzzy-searching users and toggling contact request state. Emits dismiss events and integrates with UserStore.
Defines a reusable notification UI component that shows an avatar, content, and accept/dismiss actions in a compact layout. Used by incoming call and project share notifications.
Displays incoming call notifications per display with accept/decline actions, spawning windows with appropriate options. On accept, joins the shared project if specified.
Shows a notification when a remote project is shared, allowing users to open or dismiss the invitation. Manages multiple windows per screen and cleans them up on state changes.
Provides storybook-style previews for the collab notification component to demonstrate layouts for incoming calls and project shares. Useful for visual testing.

Implements a modal command palette with fuzzy matching, command interception hooks, and alias normalization, including history-aware sorting. Registers workspace actions and supports opening Zed URLs via interceptor.
Persists command palette usage in a local SQLite database with queries for latest invocation, usage counts, and pruning to 1000 entries. Exposes test helpers and typed row mapping using sqlez macros.
Provides global hooks to filter visible actions by namespace/type and intercept queries to produce custom actions. Exposes an API to set, clear, and update these behaviors via globals.

Defines a component registry and trait for UI previews with metadata like scope, status, and optional live preview function. Uses inventory for registration and exposes helpers to query/sort components.
Provides layout helpers to render component examples and groups with titles, widths, and themed styling. Includes convenience functions to build example groups.

Implements a JSON-RPC client for Model Context Servers over pluggable transports, handling request/response dispatch, notifications, and timeouts with per-request handlers. Manages IO tasks and background channels with structured logging.

Wraps the client with MCP protocol semantics, performing initialization with capability negotiation and exposing typed request/notification APIs. Validates supported protocol versions and registers handlers.

Provides a FakeTransport for testing MCP clients by registering request handlers and simulating streams with controlled delays. Generates standard initialize responses and supports async message flow.
Defines MCP request/notification types, parameters, and responses, including resources, tools, prompts, logging, and completion APIs. Encapsulates protocol versioning and message content models.

Implements a lightweight MCP server over a Unix socket that registers tools and request handlers, and processes JSON-RPC frames. Handles tool invocation, request routing, and bidirectional IO with framing and error responses.

Provides a high-level context server manager that starts stdio-based or custom transports, initializes protocol, and exposes client access. Supports pre-registration of notification handlers and clean shutdown.
Implements a stdio transport by spawning a child process and wiring buffered read/write channels for JSON-RPC, including stdout/stderr streaming. Ensures process kill on drop and separates IO tasks.

Defines Copilot Chat configuration (including enterprise endpoints), model metadata and capabilities, request/response structures for chat and tool calls, and streaming event parsing. Manages OAuth token retrieval and model listing with robust deserialization.

Provides an EditPredictionProvider for Copilot completions that fetches, cycles, accepts, and discards suggestions with debounce and deduplication. Computes minimal insertion edits by common-prefix/suffix trimming and integrates with buffer state.
Declares LSP-style request/notification types used by Copilot for status checks, sign-in flows, editor info, and completion retrieval/feedback. Structures payloads for client-server interactions.

Implements the Copilot sign-in UX, including device code flow, toast notifications, reinstall handling, and modal lifecycle. Coordinates starting/stopping the Copilot service and opening verification URLs.

Initializes a crash handler subprocess, connects a client, and requests minidumps on crash with optional GPU info, compressing and saving artifacts. Sets a panic hook to capture messages and writes crash metadata for later analysis.

Abstracts credential storage behind a trait with implementations for system keychain and a development file-backed provider, selected by release channel and env vars. Exposes async read/write/delete APIs via the app context.

Defines core abstractions for debug adapters, task definitions, and binaries, including TCP connection templates and GitHub asset downloading/extraction. Converts user scenarios to adapter requests and serializes/deserializes adapter configurations.

Implements a DAP client that manages transport connection, request sequencing, pending response handlers, and reconnection logic. Supports child connections, logging hooks, and test-only fake request/event injection.
Provides common DAP exports and utilities including TCP configuration resolution and telemetry emission for session starts. Wires adapters and registry types with settings.

Maps persisted settings to debugger behavior, including stepping granularity, breakpoints persistence, timeouts, logging, formatting, and dock placement. Converts settings enums to DAP-compatible values.
Implements conversions between internal proto models and dap_types for scopes, variables, sources, checksums, and stack frames. Encapsulates enum mapping and optional fields handling.
Maintains a global registry of DAP adapters and locators, allowing add/remove and schema enumeration. Provides adapter lookup and language mapping for scenarios.

Defines transport abstraction (stdio/tcp/fake) for DAP, wiring IO tasks, RPC framing, and log handlers for adapter and RPC streams. Manages pending requests lifecycle, reconnectable channels, and structured error propagation.
Implements the CodeLLDB debug adapter, deriving request arguments and fetching VSIX assets from GitHub based on platform/arch. Normalizes configuration fields and prepares binary invocation.
Registers built-in adapters (CodeLLDB, Python, JavaScript, Go, GDB) into the global DAP registry, including a fake adapter in tests. Provides initialization during app startup.
Implements the GDB adapter by translating launch/attach scenarios into configuration JSON and invoking GDB's DAP mode. Resolves binary path from user settings or PATH.

Implements the Delve adapter with rich schema, dynamically downloading a platform-specific shim from GitHub, and configuring TCP connections. Normalizes settings and supports remote debugging mappings.

Implements the JavaScript adapter using vscode-js-debug, normalizing config (e.g., node-terminal, npm/pnpm runtime) and launching via Node with TCP parameters. Extracts environment variables and enables source map options by default.

Implements the Debugpy adapter by managing a base virtualenv, downloading/extracting wheels from PyPI, and generating adapter arguments, with fallback to user-installed paths. Builds request args and defaults console and cwd behavior.

Provides a domain-oriented SQLite wrapper that opens per-scope DBs with migrations, falls back to an in-memory DB on failure, and exposes a static_connection macro. Supports test DB opening and background write logging.
Implements a simple key-value store domain with global and local variants and a Dismissable trait for UI state. Exposes read/write/delete operations via generated query macros.
Defines macros to generate typed query functions for exec/select/select_row with bound parameters and contextual error messages. Streamlines DB access patterns across domains.

Bridges extension-provided debug adapters and locators into the DAP registry via a proxy, enabling extensions to register/unregister adapters and locators. Integrates with the extension host and logs failures.

Wraps an extension as a DebugAdapter, loading its schema and delegating binary acquisition, config translation, and request kind to the extension. Adapts a DapDelegate to a WorktreeDelegate for extension calls.
Wraps an extension-provided locator to create debug scenarios and run build steps, exposing them via the DapLocator trait. Relays adapter name and template data to the extension.

Provides a DAP log view and store that captures adapter logs and RPC messages per session, grouping by send/receive and building initialization sequences. Integrates with project sessions and renders selectable views.

Implements a modal to select a running process for attach using fuzzy matching of process name/command and updates the debug configuration accordingly. Integrates with the DebugPanel to start sessions.

Initializes debugger UI actions and panels, wiring workspace actions for stepping, pausing, restarting, toggling views, and telemetry. Adapts capabilities and session state to render appropriate controls.
Renders dropdown menus for selecting active debug sessions and threads, showing status indicators and allowing close actions. Builds hierarchical labels for parent-child session relationships.
Displays a debugger onboarding modal with actions to open the panel or view a blog post, emitting telemetry events. Manages focus and dismissal interactions with themed layout.

Defines the TitleBar view that composes project info, branch, collaborators, onboarding banner, connection/call controls, and an app menu, integrating with a platform-specific title bar. It registers actions for application menu navigation (non-macOS), conditionally embeds cross-platform menus, and subscribes to workspace, project, and active call changes for reactive updates.

Provides Linux window controls (minimize, maximize/restore, close) with hover styling and click handlers that call Window APIs or dispatch a close action. Encapsulates control types and an optional close action wiring for platform integration.

Implements Windows caption buttons using Segoe icon fonts, mapping to WindowControlArea for native hit-testing and system behaviors. It adapts the font family to the OS build and renders hover/active backgrounds consistent with theme colors.

Tracks the active editor buffer and language to determine and set the active toolchain for the current project/worktree, persisting defaults when none is selected. Subscribes to toolchain store and buffer events, runs async metadata resolution, and renders a button to open the toolchain selector.

Implements the toolchain selection UI and flows, including selecting from available toolchains and adding a new toolchain by browsing paths with validation and scope selection. Defines actions, picker delegates, keyboard navigation, and async resolution to update project state.
Aggregates and re-exports all UI components to provide a cohesive component library surface. Serves as the central module for consumers building UIs with common Zed components.

Collects common gpui exports, UI components, styles, traits, and helpers into a single import for building Zed UIs. Standardizes access to layout primitives, typography, icons, and theme-aware styling.

Provides an Avatar component with sizing, grayscale, border, and indicator slots, plus specialized audio and availability indicators. Used to render user presence with optional tooltips and status badges.
Defines a compact Badge with icon, label, border, and optional tooltip for displaying status or metadata. Emphasizes theme-driven colors and simple composition with dividers.
Renders an informational Banner with severity-based iconography, background/border styling, content, and an optional action slot. Used for non-blocking notices aligned with theme status colors.

Implements a Callout component for prominent notices with severity styles, optional icon, title/description, actions, and dismiss controls. Supports top/bottom border emphasis and customizable line heights.
Provides a Chip component for small labeled tokens with configurable label color/size and optional background. It uses theme borders and background to fit data display contexts.
Defines a ContentGroup container with optional border and fill, serving as a styled wrapper around grouped content. Offers convenience constructors for vertical or horizontal layouts.

Builds a flexible ContextMenu with entries, separators, headers, custom entries, toggleable states, and documentation asides, plus keyboard navigation and persistent rebuild behavior. Manages focus/dismissal and integrates with actions and tooltips.

A small toggleable Disclosure icon component (chevron variants) with click handlers and optional hover visibility group. Used to expand/collapse tree-like structures with disabled and selected states.
Implements horizontal and vertical Dividers with solid or dashed rendering, inset options, and theme-driven colors. The dashed variant approximates segments via repeated child elements.

Wraps a PopoverMenu to render a DropdownMenu with selectable trigger styles (solid/outlined/ghost), full-width behavior, disabled state, and an optional handle to control deployment. The trigger adapts to text or element labels and manages pointer/hover styling.
Renders a Facepile of overlapping avatars arranged right-to-left for proper stacking order. Offers simple padding customization and is suitable for collaborator lists.
Defines convenience constructors for horizontal and vertical groups with standardized spacing sizes. These helpers streamline consistent gap usage across the UI.

Provides the Icon system with size presets, SVG/image source handling, color/transformation, and an AnyIcon wrapper for animated variants, plus an IconWithIndicator overlay. Centralizes icon theming and sizing across the UI.
Implements Vector for fixed-size SVG images keyed by VectorName, with color and transform support. Intended for brand/illustration assets distinct from standard icons.

Implements rendering of indent guides within uniform lists and sticky items, with customizable color schemes, hitboxes, and click handlers. Computes guide layouts based on visible ranges and indents, optionally delegating rendering via callbacks.
Defines a versatile Indicator (dot, bar, or icon) with optional border and theme-aware colors for status/notification cues. Supports embedding small icons with custom sizing.

Renders keybindings (chords and modifiers) with platform-specific glyphs/text, resolves bindings from gpui actions, and supports vim mode display. Provides utilities to compose modifier sequences and per-size rendering.
Displays a KeybindingHint with optional prefix/suffix over a styled background, including theme-aware border/shadow and dynamic sizing. Integrates KeyBinding lookup to present shortcuts contextually.

Provides a Modal framework with header/footer sections, scrollable content, and optional back/dismiss buttons using theme spacing and elevation. Includes building blocks like Section and ModalRow to structure modal content.
Wraps content to enable keyboard navigation across registered focusable entries, integrating with scroll anchors to bring items into view. Handles next/previous selection via menu actions.
Implements a NumericStepper with decrement/increment buttons, styles (ghost/outlined), optional reset action, and keyboard tab ordering. Uses theme colors and icon buttons for consistent controls.
Defines a Popover container with optional aside, theme elevation, and padding to host menus or option lists anchored to triggers. Serves as a lightweight wrapper for popover content.

Implements PopoverMenu mechanics: building/showing/hiding menus with anchors, attachments, offsets, focus management, and external handles to control deployment. Integrates click triggers, tooltips suppression when open, and preserves previous focus on dismiss.
Provides a RadioWithLabel component that renders a circular selection control with theme colors and a click callback. Designed for selection groups where only one option is active.

Enables context menus triggered by right-click with optional anchor/attach behavior, managing focus and positioning relative to cursor or element corners. Internally tracks menu state and dismisses while restoring prior focus.

Implements customizable scrollbars with visibility modes (auto/system/always/never), autohide timings, reserved space management, and integration with scroll handles and uniform lists. Manages hitboxes, animations, and theme-driven track/thumb rendering while preserving layout.
A simple SettingsContainer that vertically stacks settings content with padding and gaps. Used to organize settings sections consistently.
Defines a SettingsGroup with a header and child items to organize related settings. Provides simple composition within settings UIs.

Provides a StickyItems decoration for uniform lists, computing sticky candidates and rendering drifting headers with optional decorations like indent guides. Handles layout/prepaint to position elements based on scroll offset and item heights.
Implements a Tab component with selected state, positional border logic, customizable slots, and theme-aware backgrounds. Encapsulates interactive behavior and sizing for use in tab bars.
Renders a TabBar container with optional start/end tool areas and a scrollable tab region, applying themed backgrounds and borders. Supports external scroll handle tracking for programmatic control.

Provides Checkbox and Switch-style toggles with multiple styles (ghost/elevation/custom), optional labels/tooltips, disabled/placeholder states, and click handlers. Computes background and border colors from theme and supports filled variants.

Defines a Tooltip view with optional meta and keybinding display, plus utility builders to bind action-derived keybindings in context. Includes a themed tooltip container and a simple link preview component.

Renders a TreeViewItem with optional disclosure toggle, selection/focus styling, hierarchical indentation line, and event handlers for click/hover/secondary click. Supports root item styling and tooltips.
Provides DefaultAnimations helpers to animate elements entering from edges with optional fade using themed durations and easing. Includes a component preview to demonstrate animation patterns.
Defines a semantic Color enum mapping to theme palette and status colors, with conversion from HSLA. Centralizes color semantics for consistent UI theming and documentation.

Declares ElevationIndex levels with corresponding shadows and background colors, guiding z-axis styling for surfaces and modals. Offers helpers to derive darker backgrounds based on elevation and theme appearance.
Generates DynamicSpacing values across UI density settings and exposes ui_density for non-spacing decisions. Standardizes spacing scales for consistent layout.
Provides typography utilities including StyledTypography for choosing UI/buffer fonts and text sizes, a TextSize enum, and a Headline component. Ensures theme-driven, scalable text rendering.
Utility for converting pixel values to rems and computing viewport-relative lengths (vw/vh). Encourages scale-aware sizing based on base rem size.
Adds a CommonAnimationExt to easily apply continuous rotation animations with IDs derived from call sites or custom IDs. Simplifies adding transform-based animations to components.
Extends Styled with Zed-specific helpers for flex layouts and elevation presets that apply backgrounds, borders, and shadows. Provides debug background color utilities and border color helpers.
Defines a Toggleable trait with a ToggleState enum, including inversion and construction from boolean/option. Encapsulates selected/indeterminate logic for toggleable UI elements.

Implements APCA contrast computation and utilities to adjust foreground colors to meet a minimum perceptual contrast, using binary search on lightness and saturation adjustments. Provides a more accurate contrast model for dark mode and perceptual uniformity.
Provides WCAG 2.x contrast ratio calculation via relative luminance and linearization routines. Used for validating or comparing color accessibility independent of APCA.

Provides utilities to compute inner and nested corner radii by subtracting border and padding from parent radii and clamping to zero; CornerSolver iteratively applies this across child levels. This helps ensure visually consistent rounded corners in nested UI elements.

Formats time distances between dates into human-readable strings with configurable seconds inclusion, suffixes, and prefixes, using a custom DateTimeType abstraction. Implements threshold-based wording (minutes, hours, days, months, years) and includes tests.
Defines an Element wrapper that sets a specific rem size for its children by scoping layout, prepaint, and paint within Window::with_rem_size. Enables density/typography scaling of nested UI content.

High-level Button component built on ButtonLike that supports labels, icons, selection, keybindings, sizing, styles, truncation, and click handling via a fluent builder API. Encapsulates UI behavior for common button use cases and variants.

Renders an icon inside buttons, handling disabled/selected states, optional selected icon/color, and indicator overlays. Maps ButtonStyle or tint to icon colors and composes with IconWithIndicator as needed.

Foundational button architecture with traits and enums (ButtonCommon, SelectableButton, ButtonStyle, TintColor) and style computation across enabled/hovered/active states, including elevation-aware backgrounds. Serves as the base for all button variants and their visual logic.

Icon-only button built atop ButtonLike with shape control (square vs wide), icon size/color configuration, selection/disabled states, click handlers, and optional indicators. Adapts width/height for square shape and composes ButtonIcon.

Composes a two-part button combining a primary ButtonLike on the left and an arbitrary element on the right, with configurable style (filled/outlined/transparent) and divider rendering. Adds elevation and shadow for the filled variant.

ToggleButton built on ButtonLike supporting selection state, label color adjustments, and group position-aware rounding (first/middle/last). Designed for grouped toggles with consistent sizing and styles.
Wraps an Icon with optional decoration overlay (e.g., X, triangle, dot) positioned relative to the icon size. Simplifies composing icons with status indicators.

Defines icon decoration kinds and knockout SVG assets to emulate strokes; renders foreground and background layers with hover color changes and group-based hover behavior. Provides positioning and styling for decoration overlays.

Label variant that highlights specific character positions by computing contiguous highlight ranges from UTF-8 indices and applying StyledText highlights. Supports standard label styling via LabelCommon.

Basic Label component delegating styling to LabelLike, supporting size, weight, line height, color, text decorations, truncation, single-line, buffer font, and inline code styling. Provides a simple text element for UI with a fluent API.

Underlying label builder implementing LabelCommon and rendering with theme-aware text styles, weights, line heights, decorations, truncation, and inline code visuals. Serves as the core abstraction for label-based components.
Animated label that reveals text progressively and then cycles trailing dots using timed animations, with an optional pulsating alpha effect. Useful for indicating loading states in textual UI.
Text-based spinner label cycling through predefined braille-like frames with configurable variants and duration, while exposing standard label styling. Provides lightweight activity indication.

List container supporting optional header, toggle behavior, and empty state messaging (text or element), with padding and vertical layout. Chooses between children, silence, or empty message based on content and toggle flag.
Renders a simple bullet list item with a muted dash icon and label, adjusting vertical alignment using window line height. Provides a basic non-selectable list row.

List header with start/end slots, optional hover-only end slot, toggle disclosure, inset spacing, and selected background state; supports click toggling via handler. Adapts density and composes label with muted styling.

Configurable list item with slots, hover-only meta, selection/disabled states, outlining/rounding, indenting (inset/outset), event handlers (click, hover, secondary mouse), tooltips, and overflow control. Implements rich interaction and visuals for list rows with focus and toggle support.
Subheader row for lists with optional leading icon, end slot, inset spacing, and selected highlight, using smaller muted label styling. Acts as a lightweight sectional divider.
Alert modal composed of a titled content area and a footer with dismiss and primary action buttons, styled with elevation, padding, and muted text. Provides a simple confirmation dialog pattern.

Progress bar element with configurable value/max and colors (background, foreground, over-limit), rendering a rounded track and a fill clamped to [0.02, 1.0]. Communicates process completion state with theme-aware shadows.
Demo story showcasing right-click context menus with actions and various anchor/attach positions. Useful for visual testing and documentation.
Story demonstrating IconButton variants, selection, disabled state, click handlers, tooltips, and square shapes/sizes. Serves as usage and preview examples.
Story illustrating KeyBinding rendering across modifiers, chords, and platform styles (Linux/Windows), generating permutations for display. Intended for visual verification.
Story presenting List with default items and sectioned layout including subheaders and separators. Provides example compositions for documentation.
Story demonstrating ListHeader with icon slots and meta actions. Used for previewing different configurations.
Story showcasing ListItem configurations such as inset, start/end slots, hover slots, click handlers, and overflow behavior. Aids in validating visuals and interactions.
Story rendering Tab components with indicators, close buttons, and positional grouping across selected states. Serves as a layout and behavior preview.
Story building a TabBar with navigation and action buttons and a set of tabs with selection and position meta. Used for demonstration and testing.
Story for ToggleButton including default and grouped configurations with selection, size, and style. Provides usage examples.

SingleLineInput wraps a single-line Editor into a text field with label, placeholder, start icon, disabled state, focus, and styling; exposes the Editor entity for advanced control. Handles theme-based text styles and min widths with fluent configuration.

Proc macro generating a DynamicSpacing enum and methods to compute rem and pixel spacing based on UI density (compact/default/comfortable), using either a base value or explicit tuple per density. Encodes spacing ratios and documentation for consistent layout scaling.
Defines proc macros for deriving DynamicSpacing and registering components with the ComponentRegistry. Automates boilerplate for density-aware spacing and component discovery.

Configures prompt rendering based on workspace settings and implements an internal Zed prompt UI with Markdown content, focus management, keyboard navigation, and action buttons. Emits PromptResponse events and applies theme-based text styles.

ArcCow provides a copy-on-write like enum that can borrow or own Arc-backed data for strings, slices, and generic T, with trait impls for Eq/Ord/Hash/Deref/Borrow. Facilitates efficient sharing while supporting conversions and comparisons.

Cross-platform zip extraction utilities handling streaming readers on Windows and seekable readers on Unix, preserving permissions where available. Iterates entries, creates directories/files, and copies content with error contexts; includes tests.

Async filesystem helpers to remove/collect entries by predicate, find by filename, move files between folders, and set executable permissions (Unix). Simplifies common FS operations with error-tolerant logging.

Utilities to escape Markdown text, format inline code and code blocks safely, and count consecutive characters, ensuring proper rendering and HTML entity handling. Includes tests for correctness and special cases.

Implements RelPath/RelPathBuf for normalized, relative, unicode POSIX-style paths with validation, normalization, component operations, joining, and style-aware display. Provides reliable cross-platform relative path handling and serialization.
Helpers to replace or add JSON schema subschemas and a transform to default additionalProperties to false unless overridden, leveraging schemars. Aids in producing stricter, curated schemas.

Determines the system shell (with Windows-specific detection) and maps environment variable syntaxes to different shells (PowerShell, Cmd, Nushell, etc.). Provides ShellKind identification and formatting utilities for cross-shell compatibility.

Captures the environment from a login shell in a given directory across Unix/Windows, handling shell-specific quirks (fds, events, prefixes) and JSON parsing via a helper binary. Enables consistent environment bootstrapping for processes.
Formats file sizes in decimal or binary units into concise strings (B, KB/MB, KiB/MiB) with one decimal precision. Includes tests covering thresholds.
Test utilities for creating temporary file trees from JSON, initializing git repos, and generating sample text; re-exports assertion and marked text helpers. Simplifies setup for integration tests.
Formats Duration into seconds for sub-minute values or into clock format (H:MM:SS/MM:SS), with tests. Provides concise human-readable time formatting.

Aggregates common utilities including string truncation variants, sorted vector extension and truncation algorithms, root execution prevention (Unix), and shell path helpers; exposes modules and macros. Offers widely used helpers and performance-sensitive functions.
Defines set equality helpers and macros (set_eq!, assert_set_eq!) with detailed mismatch errors. Supports clearer assertions in tests.
Test helpers to parse and generate marked text with ranges and cursor positions using special markers, producing offsets/ranges for verification. Facilitates robust text selection/cursor testing.

Provides test-oriented proc macros for path/URI/line ending normalization across platforms and a perf attribute to mark performance-sensitive tests with metadata and optional iteration control. Eases cross-platform testing and perf triage.
Defines a Vercel Model enum with built-in and custom variants, exposing identifiers, display names, token limits, and feature support flags. Centralizes model configuration for API interactions.

Adds Vim actions to navigate the editor's change list and implements logic to push positions during edits, mapping display points to anchors with mode-aware adjustments. Provides tests validating navigation and mark behavior.

Implements the Windows platform layer, initializing COM, DirectX devices, text system, executors, window class, and a hidden message window, and manages raw window handles and app-level callbacks. It provides jump list integration, broadcasts messages to windows, generates per-window creation info, and runs a VSync thread that detects device loss and triggers redraws. This is the central Windows backend entry point tying dispatch, rendering, and system features together.

Encapsulates Windows system settings such as mouse wheel scroll lines/chars and auto-hide taskbar position, reading from SystemParametersInfo and appbar APIs. It updates settings in response to system parameter change notifications and computes taskbar location relative to display bounds.

Provides Windows-specific utilities: OS version detection, WPARAM/LPARAM bit helpers, window long getters/setters, cursor loading with caching, DWM dark-mode configuration, logical point scaling, system appearance detection, error message box, and safe dynamic DLL usage. These helpers support platform code with low-level Win32/DWM interactions.

Implements a VSync provider that dynamically uses DirectComposition when available or falls back to DWM timing to determine the refresh interval. It exposes a wait_for_vsync that compensates for spurious early returns by sleeping for the computed interval, and includes robust interval derivation with high-resolution timers.

Defines WindowsWindow and its state, handling DPI scaling, logical bounds, DirectX renderer setup, input/click state, system settings, and fullscreen toggling by adjusting window styles and placement. It computes windowed/maximized/fullscreen bounds and integrates with executors and per-window callbacks.

Implements a headless Linux client using calloop to run queued tasks and stubs out window, display, clipboard, and screen capture operations. It provides a minimal event loop and common executor wiring for environments without a graphical display.

Manages Wayland clipboard and primary selection with internal/external storage, tracking current offers and MIME types, and reading text or images via pipe FDs from offers. It writes clipboard data asynchronously using calloop and normalizes incoming text to Unix line endings.

Loads and manages Wayland cursor themes at a scaled size, selecting icons with fallbacks and updating a surface/hotspot for a pointer. It reloads themes when size changes and warns on missing cursor assets.
Tracks various Wayland serial values (e.g., mouse/key press, data device) keyed by kind, allowing updates and lookups. This is a small helper for correlating protocol events.

Implements Wayland window state and lifecycle, creating xdg surfaces/toplevels, decorations/viewports, and a BladeRenderer target while tracking outputs/scales, decorations, and transparency. It cleans up Wayland objects on drop and exposes insets, output scale determination, and rendering configuration.

Provides an X11 clipboard implementation adapted from arboard, handling selection ownership, atoms/mime types, reading/writing via properties, and incremental transfers. It runs a serving thread, supports PRIMARY/CLIPBOARD/SECONDARY, and caches clipboard contents.
Represents an X11 display screen, computing logical bounds based on scale factor and exposing identifiers and UUID. It implements PlatformDisplay for use by the Linux backend.
Translates X11/XInput event data into GPUI button/scroll enums and modifier states, and provides helpers to map valuator masks to axis indices. These utilities normalize low-level event bitfields.

Implements an XIM ClientHandler that negotiates input context and processes commit and preedit events, forwarding key press/release callbacks. It maintains connection state, window association, and last callback event.

Derive macro for the Action trait, parsing attributes (name/namespace, no_json, no_register, deprecated aliases/message, docs) and generating Action implementations including JSON build/schema, cloning, equality, and registration. It integrates with inventory to register actions for discovery.

Derive macro for AppContext that forwards core entity/window operations to an embedded &mut App field indicated by #[app]. It reduces boilerplate by generating methods for entity creation, updates, window access, background tasks, and global reads.

Attribute macro that generates a reflection module for trait methods of the form fn self() -> Self, enabling runtime lookup/invocation with documentation and cfg propagation. It expands known style helper macros and produces type-erased wrapper functions for the inspector.

Derive macro for VisualContext that binds a &mut Window and &mut App (via #[window] and #[app]) to provide window-focused entity operations, replacement of root views, and focus handling. It bridges AppContext with per-window rendering/editing APIs.

Exports the suite of GPUI procedural macros for actions, elements, rendering, contexts, style helpers, tests, and inspector reflection, wiring their implementations together. This crate is the macro entry point used across the codebase.

Generates an inventory registration function for manually implemented actions, emitting a builder that captures type metadata, builders, schemas, and docs. It enables action discovery via a compile-time registry.

Implements the #[gpui::test] attribute to generate test harnesses with configurable seeds, retries, and iterations, constructing TestAppContext(s) and deterministic executors. It supports async and sync tests and optional failure hooks.

Integrates a Tokio runtime as a GPUI Global, providing spawn helpers that return GPUI Tasks and automatically abort the Tokio task if the GPUI task is dropped. It offers access to the runtime handle and supports both Result and anyhow::Result futures.

Defines HtmlElement with tag and attributes, offering inline element detection, attribute lookup, and class utilities. It is used by the Markdown conversion to reason about element semantics and classes.

Entry point to convert HTML to Markdown: parses HTML with html5ever into an RcDom, then runs a MarkdownWriter with provided tag handlers to produce cleaned Markdown. It configures parsing options (e.g., drops doctype) and returns the result.

Provides tag handlers for common HTML elements (paragraphs, headings, lists, tables, styled text, code) and a chrome remover for non-content tags. Handlers inject Markdown syntax into the writer and manage spacing/newlines for coherent output.

Core traversal and writing logic: visits DOM nodes, maintains an element stack, invokes handler hooks on start/end/text, and prettifies the output by collapsing empty lines. It coordinates Skip/Continue semantics and confines recursion depth.

Specialized handlers for Wikipedia pages: remove chrome (nav, scripts, references), skip infobox tables, and emit fenced code blocks with detected language classes. Includes tests validating citation removal.

Defines AsyncBody as a unified HTTP body type supporting empty, in-memory bytes, and asynchronous readers, implementing both AsyncRead and http_body::Body. It provides conversions from common types and a TryFrom for reqwest::Body.

Implements helpers to fetch GitHub releases via an HttpClient, parse release assets (normalizing sha256 digests), and build archive URLs that properly escape tags. It reports detailed deserialization errors and supports tag-based retrieval.

Defines the HttpClient trait and convenience methods for GET/POST JSON, redirect policy, multipart forms, and wrappers that add proxy and base URL capabilities with env-based proxy support. Includes a BlockedHttpClient for disallowed requests and URL builders for Zed services.
Declares a large IconName enum with serialization and iteration, and provides a method to map names to SVG asset paths. This supports consistent icon handling throughout the UI.

Renders image metadata (dimensions, file size, channels, format) into a status item, observing ImageView and its ImageItem for updates. It formats file sizes according to user settings and updates reactively.

Implements the ImageView item, subscribing to image events, managing focus, tab content/icon, breadcrumb text, serialization of state, and resource cleanup. It renders the image with a checkerboard background and integrates with workspace/project for opening and persistence.

Implements the Div inspector that constructs Rust and JSON style buffers/editors, computes style diffs/overrides, and updates window inspector state, including completions. It asynchronously initializes buffers with language support and synchronizes user edits across JSON/Rust representations.

Initializes and renders the GPUI inspector UI, toggling pick mode via an action and registering an inspector element that uses DivInspector. It displays element metadata and provides a click-to-open source location via the zed CLI.

Defines an action to install the Zed CLI by creating a symlink, attempting user-space creation first and escalating via osascript on macOS, while providing Linux guidance. It shows a toast on success and registers the zed URL scheme.

Provides a NewJournalEntry action that creates dated Markdown files under a journal directory, opens them in a workspace, and inserts a time-stamped heading based on user hour format settings. It handles opening in existing or new workspaces and focuses the editor at the end.

Implements a global SchemaStore that serves built-in JSON schemas (settings, keymap, tasks, debug tasks, package.json, tsconfig, inspector style) and notifies LSP clients when schemas change. It also builds schema file associations and resolves per-action schemas via normalized names.

Stores diagnostics from a single language server in a SumTree keyed by Anchors for efficient range queries and grouping, with conversion to various coordinate types and LSP stubs. It provides filtered iteration, grouping by diagnostic group, and ordering by buffer positions.

Maps tree-sitter capture names to highlight IDs by finding the longest matching theme key across dot-separated components, with a default fallback. It exposes lookup to HighlightStyle/name for syntax theming.

Central registry for languages and LSP adapters: loading/removing languages/grammars, reordering servers, tracking server status, and managing themes/settings with background executor integration. It seeds Plain Text by default and coordinates adapter availability and downloads.

Defines comprehensive language settings including indentation, soft wrap, formatting, LSP enablement, UI toggles, completion, debuggers, and task preferences, plus file-type glob associations. It exposes helpers to resolve settings for a file/language and registers global defaults.
Introduces ManifestName and interfaces for discovering a language manifest path via providers and delegates that query the file system context. It models queries with path depth and worktree scoping.

Represents buffer outlines with hierarchical items and supports fuzzy search and path-based matching, computing match positions across name ranges and reconstructing ancestor paths. It can convert ranges to point coordinates and find the most similar symbol via normalized Levenshtein.
Aggregates the remote subsystem by re-exporting client interfaces, connection states, and SSH/WSL transport options. Serves as the public entry point to remote connectivity abstractions.
Re-exports REPL UI components for kernel listing and configuration. Centralizes component access for the REPL feature.
Defines Jupyter-related settings, including kernel selections, and wires enablement via EditorSettings to avoid circular deps. Implements Settings parsing from the global SettingsContent.
Re-exports notebook cell types and UI components. Acts as a module surface for notebook functionality.
Configures REPL display behavior with bounded scrollback for lines and columns, parsed from SettingsContent. Enforces limits and defaults for buffer management.

Defines and re-exports the RPC framework including connection, peer, notifications, extensions, and protocol client with a fixed PROTOCOL_VERSION. Forms a core architectural layer for inter-process communication.
CLI tool to generate and print JSON schemas for theme and icon theme content using schemars. Useful for validating theme configuration files.
Trait for UI setting controls to read, apply, and persist values to the settings file via Fs and update_settings_file. Encapsulates side effects of writing settings.
Registers an extension snippet proxy that forwards extension-provided snippets to the global SnippetRegistry. Bridges extension host events to snippet storage.
Public module surface for a lightweight SQLite wrapper, exposing connections, statements, migrations, and typed statements. Provides anyhow re-export for error handling.
Provides UnboundedSyncSender to wrap std::sync::mpsc::Sender for thread-local unbounded sending. Minimizes contention by cloning per-thread.
Declares a Quit action via gpui actions macro for the Storybook app. Supports basic app lifecycle control.
Defines the Storybook application menu with a Quit action entry. Demonstrates menu construction in gpui.
Embeds UI assets using rust-embed and implements AssetSource to load and list assets. Centralizes bundled resources for the Storybook UI.
Re-exports multiple UI story modules for demonstration and testing. Acts as the catalog entrypoint for visual stories.
Renders a demo showcasing viewport width and height units with styled blocks. Validates layout primitives against window dimensions.
Declares actions to open SVG previews and registers the SvgPreviewView with new Workspaces. Integrates preview panels and following mode into the editor.
Defines adapter schema metadata for task adapters, including adapter identifiers and JSON schema values. Supports validation and discovery of adapter configurations.
Converts gpui RGBA colors to Alacritty Rgb, premultiplying alpha for terminal rendering. Provides a small color mapping utility.
Groups terminal mapping utilities for colors, keys, and mouse. Serves as a module index.
Collects and re-exports theme style modules such as colors, accents, syntax, and system. Establishes the public style API.
Defines SystemColors, including macOS traffic light colors and transparent defaults. Provides consistent system-level color constants.
Re-exports modules for importing VS Code themes, syntax, and conversion. Provides infrastructure for theme migration.
Declares platform-specific title bar modules for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Organizes platform implementations.
Re-exports title bar application menu story. Facilitates visual testing of title bar components.
Parses title bar settings from SettingsContent to control visibility of icons, banners, menus, and user elements. Drives UI configuration for the title bar.
Defines a macOS-specific pixel padding constant for traffic light controls accounting for border offset. Ensures accurate UI layout on macOS.
Story rendering for ApplicationMenu, creating and displaying a menu within a Storybook section. Demonstrates component integration.
Re-exports component traits and macros, including registration helpers and documentation utilities. Establishes the component registration and example infrastructure.
Collects UI style modules like appearance, color, elevation, spacing, and typography and re-exports them. Forms the styling API surface.
Exports UI extension traits for interactive and styled elements (clickable, toggleable, transformable, etc.). Encourages composable UI behaviors.
Crate root exposing UI primitives, components, styles, and proc-macro integrations. Serves as the central UI toolkit module for the application.
Provides UI utilities including color contrast tools, corner solving, search input sizing, and theme appearance helpers. Adds convenience functions such as is_light.
Aggregates and re-exports button-related components (icon, split, toggle). Simplifies access to button variants.
Aggregates and re-exports label components including highlighted and loading variants. Provides common labeling widgets.
Re-exports list components such as headers, items, separators, and bullets. Establishes list UI building blocks.
Re-exports alert modal for notifications. Supplies modal UI for alerts.
Re-exports progress bar component. Offers progress display widget.
Adds h_flex and v_flex helpers to create horizontal and vertical flex stacks with common styles. Reduces boilerplate for flex layouts.
Re-exports component stories for demo and testing (context menu, tabs, toggles, etc.). Centralizes visual demos.
Provides helpers to read window background appearance and determine transparency expectations. Guides UI rendering decisions for transparent themes.
Defines PlatformStyle enum and resolves style per target OS (Mac, Linux, Windows). Abstracts platform-specific UI styling decisions.
Declares Severity levels (info, success, warning, error) to drive component styling. Standardizes severity-based visuals.
Defines Clickable trait with on_click handler and cursor styling for interactive elements. Enables event-driven UI interactions.
Defines Disableable trait to control interactivity and visual state of components. Facilitates consistent disabled behavior.
Provides FixedWidth trait for setting explicit or full element widths. Simplifies layout sizing.
Exposes Transformable trait to apply visual transformations. Supports animated or adjusted UI presentation.
Defines VisibleOnHover trait and impl to toggle visibility based on group hover state. Implements hover-based reveal patterns.
Calculates search input width with threshold and max constraints based on container size. Ensures responsive input sizing.
Implements ListSeparator element as a styled horizontal separator with theme-based spacing and border color. Provides visual grouping in lists.
Renders a disclosure story demonstrating toggled and untoggled states of the Disclosure component. Useful for visual verification.
Proc macro to auto-register components with a global inventory at compile time, asserting Component trait implementation. Powers plug-and-play component discovery.
Provides cross-platform helpers to create std and smol commands, hiding console windows on Windows by setting creation flags. Normalizes process spawning behavior.
Determines whether environment variable names should be redacted based on common sensitive suffixes. Helps secure logs and diagnostics.
Utility serde helpers including default_true and generic is_default checks. Simplifies config defaults and pruning.
Defines NoReceiverError and NoSenderError with Display and Error impls for watch channels. Provides clearer error semantics for dropped endpoints.
Thin main wrapper that defers to zed::main while configuring Windows subsystem behavior for release. Ensures actions and gpui resources initialize correctly.
Macro for emitting onboarding telemetry events with a fixed source tag, allowing extra key-value data. Standardizes telemetry for onboarding flows.
Defines log filtering settings by scope and updates zlog filters when settings change. Integrates with SettingsStore to manage dynamic log levels.
Empty build script used to include build dependencies in the workspace. A cargo workaround for dependency resolution.
Stub library file to satisfy cargo crate structure. No functional code.
Implements a cargo xtask CLI with subcommands for clippy, licenses, and package conformity. Orchestrates developer tooling.
Declares task modules for xtask commands (clippy, licenses, conformity). Organizes tooling implementations.
Loads Cargo workspace metadata using cargo_metadata APIs with error context. Basis for tooling that needs workspace inspection.
Comprehensive async tests for agent threads covering echo, thinking, system prompts, caching, tool calls, and end-to-end paths. Validates agent integration behavior.
Integration tests for debugger panel behavior in collaborative sessions, including remote panel synchronization and session shutdown. Ensures UI consistency across participants.
Tests collaborative editor behaviors such as host disconnect handling, cursor movement on newline insertion, and reconnection flows. Verifies robustness of shared editing.
Multi-client tests for following behavior across participants, state replication, unfollow transitions, and workspace synchronization. Ensures correct leader-follower UI updates.
Integration tests for calls and room management, reconnection under DB failure, multi-user invites, screen sharing tracks, and status checks. Validates real-world collaboration flows.
Randomized collaboration tests generating varied client operations across projects, buffers, LSP interactions, and git operations. Stress-tests concurrency and state transitions.
UI tests for debugger panel lifecycle, selected threads, single panel per session, and shutdown persistence. Confirms panel state management and event handling.
Tests rendering of inline variable values for Rust across changing stack frames and evaluation calls. Validates correctness of inline value overlays.
Tests variable list fetching and visualization across scopes and stack frames, including expansion/collapse and watch actions. Ensures accurate variable display.
Python script that scans highlight.scm files to count tag occurrences and languages, optionally listing per-tag languages. Helps avoid redundant syntax tags in new languages.
Build script that copies external extension API Rust files into OUT_DIR for include! compatibility with rust-analyzer. Ensures IDE support for generated code.

Platform-aware build script for gpui that validates WGSL shaders, generates macOS bindings and shader headers, compiles platform shaders, and embeds Windows resources. Orchestrates graphics assets and platform integration.
macOS-only build script using bindgen to generate media-related FFI bindings with appropriate clang args. Prepares codecs and video types for Rust usage.
Build script configuring macOS link flags, deployment targets, weak frameworks, Git commit SHA env, and Windows icon resources. Establishes platform-specific build metadata.

Defines the AgentConnection trait and related session capabilities (auth, prompt, resume, truncation, titles, model selection, telemetry, modes), plus model listing abstractions. Core contracts for agent threads and ACP integration.

Implements Diff management for buffers, supporting pending and finalized states, excerpt visibility, and async diff computation with language-aware context lines. Powers markdown and multibuffer diff presentation in threads.

Parses and represents rich Mention URIs (files, directories, symbols, selections, threads, rules, fetched URLs) with icon selection and URL conversion. Enables robust context linking and rendering in agent threads.
Wraps terminal tasks and output for agent commands, tracking lifecycle, truncating large outputs, and exposing markdown and exit status. Integrates asynchronous output management via shared tasks.

Implements a developer-facing UI to inspect ACP client connections, capturing and rendering streamed requests/responses/notifications with method tracking and markdown formatting. Facilitates introspection of agent protocol traffic.
Status bar component aggregating language server statuses, environment errors, git jobs, and auto-update state, with actions to display errors. Central UI for surfacing background activity.

Defines the agent context model for files, directories, symbols, selections, fetched URLs, threads, rules, and images, including handles, loading, display, and stable identity semantics. Core domain abstractions for attaching context to agent messages.

Handles Yarn-specific path resolution by interpreting virtual paths and paths inside .zip archives, unpacking zip contents to temp directories to provide real filesystem access. Provides conversion of ‘zip:’ prefixed URIs and rebases extracted paths to temporary roots.

Integrates extension-provided context servers by registering descriptors via a proxy and producing ContextServerCommand and configuration based on the active worktrees. Bridges extension APIs with the project’s context server registry.

Maintains a global registry of context server descriptors keyed by server ID, with methods to register, lookup, list, and unregister descriptors. Notifies listeners on changes to drive dependent UI or services.

Manages breakpoints per file across local and remote modes, tracking per-session states and reacting to buffer events like saves and renames. Exposes RPC handlers to sync breakpoints and toggle them, emitting updates to the UI.

Orchestrates debug sessions and adapters (local, remote, collab), resolving adapter binaries, environment, and transport options while emitting DAP lifecycle events. Integrates with toolchains, worktrees, and breakpoints, and registers locator integrations.

Defines a paged memory model optimized for sparse unmapped regions, with a builder for incremental page reads and an iterator that yields mapped/unmapped memory cells. Encapsulates chunked page contents and background clearing to avoid blocking.
Provides test utilities to intercept running debug sessions, registering default DAP request handlers and validating breakpoint requests. Simplifies testing of debugger integration.

Parses merge conflict regions in buffers, tracks snapshots of conflicts, computes diffs between snapshots, and applies resolutions by deleting non-kept ranges. Emits updates to drive UI refreshes for conflict markers.

Traverses worktree entries and aligns them with Git statuses across potentially nested repositories, exposing iterators and utilities to advance within the tree. Produces per-entry Git summaries for directories and files.

Transforms LSP SignatureHelp into UI-friendly data with highlighted parameter ranges and markdown documentation, and provides conversions between LSP and proto representations. Supports language-registry-aware rendering of docs.

Registers clangd’s inactiveRegions notification, mapping regions into “inactive region” diagnostics and merging them into the store while filtering duplicates. Identifies clangd-origin diagnostics for consistent handling.

Implements vscode-json-language-server’s custom schema content request and a schema-change notification mechanism, delegating schema resolution via a global handler. Notifies relevant JSON servers when schema URIs change.

Aggregates language server logs, traces, and RPC messages per server with adjustable levels, and subscribes to project events to register servers dynamically. Streams IO logs from servers and emits UI events for new log entries.

Defines multiple LSP extension commands (e.g., expand macro, open docs, switch source/header, parent module) with conversions to/from LSP and proto, and response mapping. Each command validates capabilities and formats document identifiers and positions.

Handles rust-analyzer server status notifications and exposes actions to cancel, run, and clear flycheck, working across local and remote contexts. Finds appropriate rust-analyzer instances per buffer or project and emits status updates.
Provides a global registry for manifest providers keyed by name, enabling registration, lookup, and introspection of known manifest files. Supports discovery in the manifest tree.

Implements a trie over worktree-relative paths that records label presence (Present/KnownAbsent) to optimize ancestor lookups for project roots. Supports insertion, removal, and walking to find closest known nodes and unexplored segments.

Builds and maintains a per-worktree language server tree mapping manifest roots and adapters to nodes, tracking initialized servers and launch dispositions. Computes adapters per language from settings and initializes nodes with toolchains.

Implements a Rust cargo DAP locator that converts tasks into debug scenarios, tweaks cargo actions (e.g., ‘test --no-run’), and discovers the right executable via cargo JSON output and optional test name probing. Produces adapter-specific configs.

Implements a Go DAP locator that parses flags and maps ‘go test’/‘go run’ tasks into Delve launch configurations, separating debug flags from build flags. Constructs scenario configs with program, args, build flags, and optional cwd/env.

Provides a JavaScript locator that recognizes npm/pnpm/yarn or a TYPESCRIPT_RUNNER and produces a pwa-node launch scenario using terminal and inspect-brk. Adapts args, cwd, and env from the task template.

Creates Debugpy launch scenarios for Python, handling module execution (-m) vs script paths and rejecting ‘-c’ executions, assembling args and program/module fields. Includes tests for module-based runs.
Benchmarks parallel sorting of worktree entries using a pre-recorded repository snapshot to measure sorting performance. Helps optimize project panel entry ordering.

Defines settings for the project panel UI (layout, icons, git status, scrollbars), with import logic from VSCode settings and scrollbar visibility integration. Provides structured configuration for panel behavior.

Implements a symbol picker for projects with fuzzy matching across visible and external files, rendering matches with syntax styling and opening buffers at symbol locations. Integrates with workspace panes and in-editor navigation.

Implements a persisted prompt store using LMDB (heed), maintaining metadata and bodies with upgrade logic from v1 schemas, plus a metadata cache for efficient lookup and sorting. Provides global initialization and events for updates.

Builds prompts via Handlebars templates, supplying rich project and model contexts and a ‘has_tool’ helper, and watches filesystem to load template overrides dynamically. Normalizes line endings and supports rules file discovery.

Provides structured error handling bridging proto ErrorCode and anyhow::Error, supporting messages and key-value tags, and converting to/from proto error payloads. Enables downstream identification of error codes and metadata.
Defines macros to generate message trait implementations for typed envelopes, request-response bindings, entity messages, and LSP request mapping. Centralizes boilerplate for the RPC protocol layer.

Includes generated proto messages and registers a large set of application RPC messages with priorities and helpers. Exposes constants for remote server identity and orchestrates typed envelope construction.

Defines the typed envelope system and core traits (EnvelopedMessage, RequestMessage, EntityMessage, LspRequestMessage), with facilities for converting and inspecting payloads and tracking sender IDs. Powers type-safe RPC messaging and LSP responses.
Renders a modal overlay when disconnected from a remote project, with actions to close the window or reconnect to the remote server. Integrates with workspace modals and project events.

Implements a picker modal to open recent projects or remote connections, using fuzzy matching and handling workspace creation or reuse. Registers actions and handles platform-specific WSL workflows on Windows.

Manages SSH/WSL connection settings and a modal prompt for interactive password responses, forwarding status and cancellation to remote client delegates. Provides helper conversions between settings and connection options.
Parses SSH config files to extract host entries, handling multi-line ‘Host’ definitions, negations, and wildcards. Supplies a set of concrete host names for connection UIs.
Implements a WSL distro picker with fuzzy matching, fetching distro names from the registry and launching remote projects under the selected distro. Emits selection/dismiss events for modal handling.

Provides the Refineable trait and Cascade structure for hierarchical configuration with partial refinements, including ‘is_superset_of’ and ‘subtract’ semantics. Enables composable style/settings overrides across the app.

Proc-macro deriving refinement types and implementations for structs, supporting nested refineable fields, optional fields, custom trait derivations, and debug serialization of non-empty fields. Generates refine/apply/subtract logic automatically.

Encapsulates release channel state (dev/nightly/preview/stable), app version, and commit SHA, exposing globals and helper display names, app IDs, and update policies. Initializes globals at startup and supports Windows identifiers.
Serializes log records to JSON and reconstructs logs from JSON payloads, mapping levels and metadata to log::Record. Used for transporting structured logs over remote connections.
Implements a length-prefixed binary protocol for RPC messages, providing read/write helpers for prost-encoded Envelopes and raw buffers. Ensures correct framing and buffering over async streams.

Handles RPC transport over child process stdio, wiring async tasks for stdin/stdout/stderr, decoding envelopes, and streaming JSON logs. Includes debug-only logic to build remote server binaries from source via Zig, cross, or cargo.

Implements SSH remote connection lifecycle: master connection setup with askpass, command templating with environment and path styles, port forwarding, directory upload via scp, and proxy startup. Detects platform details and manages remote binary paths.

Implements WSL remote connection handling: detects platform and shell, ensures remote server binary by uploading or building, extracts and installs it, and starts the proxy. Converts Windows paths to WSL and executes commands via wsl.exe.

Constructs a headless project environment for the remote server by instantiating core stores (worktree, buffer, LSP, DAP, tasks, git, agent) and wiring RPC handlers. Shares entities with the proto client and subscribes to key events.

CLI entrypoint for the remote server, delegating to askpass/crash handling or subcommands (run/proxy/version) and printing version info per release channel. Non-Windows builds execute the server logic.

Defines remote server subcommands and dispatches to Unix-specific implementations for running the server or proxy, with a version command reflecting the release channel. Exposes headless project types.

Unix implementation of the remote server: initializes logging, manages sockets for stdin/stdout/stderr, bridges envelopes to the application loop, and handles crash file retrieval. Sets up headless app state and supervises idle timeout and shutdown.

Defines REPL output variants (plain, stream, image, markdown, table, error) with rendering and controls for copy/open-in-buffer, ranking MIME types to choose the richest output. Integrates with workspace and editor entities.
Initializes the REPL subsystem (settings, UI, store) and bridges the app’s PlatformDispatcher to async-dispatcher for scheduling. Exposes core REPL types and actions.

Implements REPL actions on editors: assigning kernels, running selected code cells, managing sessions (clear, interrupt, shutdown, restart), and opening outputs. Resolves kernel specs per language and worktree and wires session lifecycle events.

Implements Vim digraphs and literal character insertion, resolving characters from a default/custom digraph map (with reversed pair fallback) and inserting into the editor. Parses literal input prefixes for octal/hex/Unicode/decimal forms, coordinates with the operator stack, and defers unhandled keystrokes appropriately.

Registers and implements Helix-mode motions and selections (yank/insert/append/goto/select), including word-boundary navigation using classifiers and display-map traversal. Provides helpers to find forward/backward ranges and moves/collapses selections or cursors according to Helix semantics.

Defines indent, outdent, and autoindent actions over motions or text objects, saving/restoring selection anchors and handling Helix mode cursor behavior. Executes edits transactionally and exits visual modes appropriately.

Handles transitions out of insert mode (NormalBefore, TemporaryNormal) and insert-from-above/below actions per cursor. Adjusts selection/cursor positions (with Helix mode nuances), records marks, and inserts characters from adjacent lines using buffer snapshots.

Status bar view that shows the current Vim mode and pending keystrokes, including recording state, selected register, operator stack, and counts. Subscribes to Vim focus/events and renders a compact label reflecting active state.

Implements Replace mode and undo for multi-cursor replacements by tracking replaced ranges and restoring prior text. Provides an 'exchange' operator to swap text ranges selected via motion/object/visual selections, with background highlighting and careful range/offset handling.

Adds a rewrap operator to reformat selected/motion/object ranges to line width using editor rewrap options. Preserves and restores selection anchors, snapping the cursor to column zero of the original line.
Contains the static table of default digraph mappings copied from Neovim, used to resolve digraph character pairs to Unicode codepoints.

Defines bounded Helix text objects and algorithms to find next/previous starts/ends, compute matching ranges with nesting, zero-width handling, and 'inside/around' conversions. Provides offset utilities over display/buffer and implements robust range-closing traversal.
