Bridges Vim text objects to Helix equivalents by mapping objects to Helix implementations and exposing range/next/previous queries. Includes cursor-range calculation respecting selection direction and an error for unsupported objects.

Implements Helix-style paste that zips clipboard selections with current selections, handles before/after and line-mode semantics, and sets new selections to the inserted text. Coordinates multi-selection pastes and line-ending behavior.
Selects current/next/previous objects per Helix convention, falling back to Vim object expansion if needed. Updates selections’ head/tail and goals to reflect object boundaries.

Implements the change operator for motions/objects, including special cw/cW behavior, whitespace trimming, and copying replaced text before entering insert mode. Adjusts selections for line-based motions and refreshes edit prediction.

Provides case conversion and ROT13/ROT47 over motions/objects/modes, preserving anchors and collapsing selections post-edit. Includes a general manipulate_text helper that computes ranges based on mode and count.

Implements delete over motions/objects with linewise newline handling, yanks prior to deletion, and cursor fixups (column restoration, start-of-line behavior). Coordinates offset-based range tweaks for paragraphs and EOF/newline edge cases.

Implements increment/decrement for numbers under the cursor (decimal/hex/binary) with wrapping and zero-padding, and toggles booleans (true/false, yes/no, on/off). Scans within selection/line ranges, performs edits per cursor, and repositions cursors after edits.

Creates and jumps to marks across buffers and file paths, integrating with the workspace to focus/open items and update selections. Stores visual marks, records navigation history, and supports line-wise mark jumps.

Implements Vim paste with registers, preserve_clipboard behavior, block-mode expansion (generating extra cursors), before/after semantics, and optional auto-indent on paste. Computes insertion points for visual/line modes and sets selections to the inserted ranges.

Provides dot-repeat and macro recording/replay, normalizing insert-like actions and scheduling replays via a Replayer with action filtering. Restores mode/selection context, supports counts, and manages recording state in globals.

Implements scrolling actions (lines/pages/columns/half-pages) with optional cursor following and vertical margins, respecting viewport bounds and preserving columns. Uses editor scroll manager anchors and selection goals to keep cursors visible.

Integrates with BufferSearchBar to initiate searches (regex/case/word/backwards), move to next/previous matches, and submit results while preserving prior mode/operator state. Also wires ex-style find/replace commands and maintains SearchState across interactions.

Implements substitute (s/S) over counts and visual modes, expanding to current line when needed, yanking replaced text, deleting ranges, and switching to Insert mode. Handles newline at line-end in visual selections and first-non-whitespace alignment.
Toggles comments over regions expanded by motions or objects, preserving original anchors and collapsing selections back after edit. Executes edits transactionally with no-scroll selection effects.

Implements yanking/copying for motions/objects, writing registers with text and clipboard selection metadata, and setting [ and ] marks. Optionally highlights yanked ranges for a configurable duration.

Test harness that runs actions against both Neovim and the editor to verify parity, managing shared states, simulated keystrokes, and comparisons of modes, buffers, and registers. Provides utilities to configure wrap/scroll options and assert outcomes.

Encapsulates a live Neovim connection or a replay mechanism, sending keystrokes, setting state/options, executing commands, and reading registers, with feature-gated recording/playback. Ensures deterministic test scripts and synchronization.

Initializes a test editor environment with Vim/Helix keymaps and workspace UI, provides helpers to set state, simulate keystrokes, and assert mode/operator/editor state. Integrates search bars and status items for realistic testing.

Defines and registers VimModeSetting and HelixModeSetting to enable/disable modes from settings, exposing lightweight toggles without depending on the full vim crate. Integrates with global settings initialization.

Implements a lightweight watch channel with Sender/Receiver supporting async change notifications via wakers, version tracking, and graceful handling of no receiver/sender. Provides borrow/recv and constant receiver utilities with tests.

Defines a WebSearchProvider trait and a registry with global access to register/unregister providers, select the active provider, and trigger searches. Manages providers as Arc objects and exposes query dispatch as tasks.

Implements a cloud-backed WebSearchProvider that performs HTTP requests to Zed’s LLM endpoint using an API token with automatic refresh on expiration. Retries requests on token expiry and subscribes to global token refresh events.

Initializes web search providers by registering the Zed cloud provider when the default language model is Zed-provided, and unregisters it otherwise. Subscribes to default model changes to keep the registry in sync.

Provides the dock/panel framework around the window edges with Panel trait and handles, managing positions, sizes, focus, zoom state, and activation. Renders panel buttons, handles drag/resize, and integrates with workspace status bar and modal layer.

Manages recent workspaces history and updates the OS jump list, loading from persistent storage and responding to user-pruned entries. Exposes a global manager and updates history on workspace changes.
Renders a fallback view for failed buffer opens, showing the path and error message and offering to open in the system default app if local. Implements Item with tab labeling and focus management.

Implements a modal layer that shows/hides modal views with focus preservation, click-to-dismiss, and optional background fade. Exposes a trait for modal views to influence dismissal and integrates with the window focus chain.

Workspace notifications system to show/dismiss/suppress notifications and toasts, including a LanguageServerPrompt with actionable options and auto-hide behavior. Stores notifications by ID, supports app-wide initial notifications, and integrates clipboard/links.

Manages pane splits as a tree of axes/panes, supporting split, remove, resize, swap, bounding box queries, and rendering with leader decoration (e.g., collaboration indicators). Provides navigation to adjacent panes based on geometry and cursor position.

Represents an ordered list of absolute paths with a lexicographically sorted storage and a separate original order mapping, with serialize/deserialize helpers. Normalizes paths via sanitization for consistent comparison.

Defines the SearchableItem trait and handle wrappers for items supporting search, specifying options, match lifecycle, selection/activation, and replace operations. Bridges concrete item types to type-erased AnyVec for UI search toolbars and navigation.

Converts internal language data to and from rpc::proto messages, serializing edits, undos, selections, diagnostics, cursor shape, and line endings with Lamport timestamps. Includes batching operations into chunks and helpers to translate anchors, ranges, and LSP severities.

Defines the ContextProvider trait and supporting types to build per-language task contexts, discover associated tasks, and optionally source tasks via LSP. Captures project location metadata to drive task resolution.

Implements line- and word-level diffs using imara_diff with language-aware tokenization to produce precise edit patches and unified diff strings. Includes heuristics for when to perform word-level diff within hunks and utilities to apply unified patches.

Models language toolchains and their scopes, defines listers to discover and resolve toolchains, and abstracts a store to retrieve active toolchains. Provides grouping and default selection for discovered toolchains.

Tests syntax map range splicing, layer retrieval, and dynamic language injection behavior across edits and reparse cycles. Verifies layer changes in response to macro edits and delayed grammar availability.

Bridges extension-provided language servers into Zed via DynLspInstaller and LspAdapter, fetching commands, init options, and workspace config while managing server lifecycle. Includes a proxy to register/remove adapters and stop servers across workspaces.

Initializes extension host proxies to register grammars, languages, and language servers into the LanguageRegistry, with configurable access to LSP stores. Coordinates removal of languages and grammars via a central registry proxy.

Provides a test-only fake language model provider and model that stream completions, track pending requests, and allow injecting events/errors for deterministic testing. Includes helpers to control request allowance and emit text chunks.

Defines the core language model API including completion events, rich error taxonomy and conversions from upstream/cloud responses, provider constants, and initialization hooks. Re-exports submodules and integrates telemetry and settings initialization.

Implements a semaphore-based rate limiter that wraps futures and streams, holding permits for the lifetime of a stream to bound concurrent requests. Exposes guarded stream adapters to transparently limit throughput.

Maintains a global registry of language model providers and selected models, emitting events on changes, verifying authentication, and resolving defaults and inline alternatives. Supports dynamic provider registration and selection by string IDs.

Handles image ingestion for language model requests by encoding to base64 PNG, resizing within Anthropic constraints, estimating token costs, and forming data URLs. Deserializes tool result content flexibly into text or image variants.
Defines the Role enum with conversions to/from proto roles, cycling utility, and display formatting for user/assistant/system. Serves as a small interop helper.
Reports assistant telemetry events locally and, when enabled, forwards anonymized metrics to Anthropic with the user's API key. Builds and sends HTTP requests and logs errors on failures.

Declares cloud-specific errors (payment required, request/tool use limits) and an LLM API token manager that fetches and refreshes tokens via the client. Registers a listener to refresh tokens on user updates received from the cloud.

Manages provider API keys sourced from environment variables or the system keychain, handling storage, loading, URL mismatch warnings, and async retrieval. Exposes authenticate results and supports reactive reloads on URL changes.
Initializes and registers built-in language model providers, and observes settings to dynamically add or remove OpenAI-compatible providers. Centralizes provider setup at startup.
Aggregates and loads settings for all language model providers into a unified AllLanguageModelSettings structure. Parses provider-specific config (API URLs, available models) from Settings content.

Implements the Anthropic provider, handling API key authentication, model enumeration (including custom and recommended), configuration views, token counting (including images), and streaming completions with rate limiting. Merges project settings into workspace configuration.

Integrates GitHub Copilot Chat as a language model provider, sourcing models and authentication from Copilot state, supporting tools/images, and streaming completions. Counts tokens using tiktoken and maps vendor-specific capabilities.

Provides DeepSeek models (chat and reasoner) with API key handling, streaming completions through a rate limiter, and token counting via GPT tokenizers. Exposes configuration views and merges settings-driven model list.

Implements the Google AI (Gemini) provider with dual env var support, model modes including thinking, workspace configuration, and streaming content generation. Handles API key authentication, recommended models, and token counting.

Implements a local LM Studio provider that authenticates by querying the local server, fetches available models and capabilities, observes settings for changes, and streams completions with rate limiting. Does not select defaults to avoid auto-loading heavy models.

Implements the Mistral provider with API key management, model enumeration (including custom capabilities), tool/image/thinking support, and streaming completions with a rate limiter. Provides token counting and configuration views.

Integrates Ollama by discovering local/remote models and capabilities, optionally authenticating via API key, and streaming chat completions. Reacts to settings changes, builds model metadata, and avoids auto-selecting defaults.

Implements the OpenAI provider with API key handling, model catalog (including reasoning efforts), tool/image support, streaming completions, and token counting. Provides configuration UI and merges settings-defined custom models.

Provides a generic OpenAI-compatible provider configured via settings, deriving env var names from IDs and streaming via the OpenAI protocol. Creates models with declared capabilities and counts tokens using tiktoken heuristics.

Implements OpenRouter provider, authenticating via API key, listing models from the API and merging settings overrides, and streaming completions. Manages background tasks to refresh available models.
Wraps Vercel’s OpenAI-compatible API with models that support tools and images, streaming via the OpenAI request mapping. Provides token counting and configuration UI.
Implements the xAI provider with custom tool schema format handling, tool/image support, streaming via OpenAI mapping, and token counting. Merges settings-driven capabilities and model list.
UI component rendering a list item with optional action button for provider configuration instructions. Used to guide users to external docs or downloads from settings views.

Displays an onboarding banner announcing BasedPyright as the default Python server, with dismissal persistence and a link to documentation. Shows only in relevant Python editors via toolbar integration.
Status bar view showing the active buffer’s language and providing a button to open the language selector. Observes the active editor to update language display reactively.

Implements a modal language selector that fuzzy-matches available languages and applies the selection to the current buffer, with icons from path matchers. Registers a workspace action to toggle the selector.
Developer tool to inspect the current keybinding context stack and last keystrokes, listing possible matches and their predicates. Provides quick links to documentation and keymap files.
Initializes language tool views (LSP log view, syntax tree, key context) and provides a helper to create or place tool panes. Acts as a module wiring entry point.

Builds a status bar menu for language servers showing health and binary statuses, and actions to stop or restart servers and open logs. Tracks servers per buffer path and integrates with LspStore and project context.
Visual test validating the LSP log view’s menu items and log capture for a fake Rust server. Ensures correct integration with project, registry, and log store.

Provides a pane to inspect the tree-sitter syntax tree for the active editor, tracking selections and reparses, and offering toolbar integration. Manages switching to the last active editor and highlighting nodes.
Defines bash task templates and tests autoindent behavior across various constructs using buffer edits and AutoindentMode. Ensures indentation rules for functions, control flow, arrays, and shebangs.

Implements a clangd LSP adapter that downloads and verifies binaries from GitHub releases with digest checks and caches, falling back to user-installed binaries. Customizes completion labels with syntax highlighting based on kinds.

Implements the CSS language server adapter using NodeRuntime to install the vscode CSS server and construct stdio arguments. Provides initialization options and merges project-specific lint configuration into workspace settings.
Utility for downloading and extracting GitHub release assets with optional SHA-256 verification, supporting tar.gz, gz, and zip formats. Streams data to disk and extracts archives cross-platform.

Implements the gopls adapter, installing via the Go toolchain, naming cached binaries by gopls and Go versions, and verifying availability. Enhances completion labels with highlighted code snippets and includes helpers for Go test name handling.

Provides a JSON tasks provider exposing package/composer script tasks and a JSON LSP adapter installed via npm that integrates JSON schema associations. Supplies language IDs, initialization options, and merges workspace configuration from project settings.

Registers REPL actions in Workspace and modal Editors, opens the REPL Sessions panel, and triggers kernelspec refreshes based on project/language context. Defines ReplSessionsPage as a Workspace Item that renders available sessions or guidance when none exist. Integrates with JupyterSettings gating and ReplStore for data.

Global state for the REPL managing enabled state, active sessions, and kernelspecs (local, remote, and per-worktree Python envs). Provides async refresh pipelines, selection logic by worktree/language, and command-palette visibility integration.

Encapsulates a kernel session bound to an Editor, inserting sticky output blocks and routing Jupyter messages to ExecutionView. Manages kernel startup (native or remote), telemetry, buffer subscriptions, and error handling of launch and message flow.
UI component for rendering a kernel entry in a list with status indicator, custom buttons, and children. Provides a minimal, composable list item abstraction keyed by KernelSpecification.

Implements a popover Picker to browse and select kernels across local, Python env, and remote specs, with filtering and selection callbacks. Shows metadata (icon, type, path/url) and links to documentation, reading available/active specs from ReplStore.

Defines KernelSpecification variants (Jupyter, PythonEnv, Remote), kernel metadata (name, language, icon), and discovery of Python env kernelspecs via project toolchains. Declares the RunningKernel trait, KernelStatus, and Kernel lifecycle states.

Launches and manages a local Jupyter-compatible kernel process by creating a connection file, spawning the process, wiring ZeroMQ channels, and routing messages back to the session. Streams stdout/stderr for logging and exposes a RunningKernel implementation.

Interfaces with a remote Jupyter server to list kernelspecs and launch kernels via HTTP, then communicates over websockets. Implements a RemoteRunningKernel that forwards messages and supports clean shutdown via REST.

Loads nbformat cells (Markdown, Code, Raw) into renderable entities, creating editors for code cells and converting outputs to REPL Output views. Provides UI controls scaffolding and style refinements for notebook-like rendering.

Feature-flagged Notebook editor integrating with Workspace, rendering cells as a list with selection and navigation. Stubs actions for run/clear/move/add cells and handles basic state like cell ordering and outputs presence.

Decodes base64 image data, converts to render-ready BGRA frames, and renders inline with size adapted to line height; also prepares clipboard image data. Supports multiple image formats and exposes OutputContent for copy operations.
Parses markdown asynchronously and renders it with retained images, exposing plain-text and buffer representations for clipboard/export. Integrates with OutputContent for interoperability.

Terminal-like text renderer using alacritty_terminal to process ANSI sequences, layout a grid, and paint within editor output blocks. Provides style/size helpers, incremental append, and export of full text/clipboard data.

Renders tabular data from a Tabular Data Resource by measuring text widths per column, drawing headers/body with alignment, and exporting a Markdown table for clipboard. Adapts vertical padding to editor line height.
Displays kernel-side errors with a bold header and a styled traceback block using TerminalOutput. Encapsulates error data and rendering in a compact view.

Reqwest-based HttpClient implementation with optional proxy and user-agent, and an internal tokio runtime for async send. Streams request bodies, redacts sensitive query params on errors, and provides multipart helpers and tests.

Builds interactive rich text with markdown-like highlighting, link detection, mentions, and optional tooltips. Produces a Styled/InteractiveText element and includes a markdown renderer that annotates ranges and inline code styles.

Criterion benchmarks covering core Rope operations such as push/append, slicing, byte ranges, char iteration, clipping, and cursor movement. Generates randomized input to measure throughput and performance characteristics.

Core rope representation splitting text into fixed-size chunks with bitsets tracking char, UTF-16 length, newlines, and tabs. Provides slicing, splitting, text summaries, and conversions between offsets and points for efficient text operations.
Small wrapper for UTF-16 code unit offsets with arithmetic and assignment ops to aid conversion and indexing in rope. Supports safe combination and subtraction semantics.
Represents zero-indexed row/column positions with arithmetic, ordering, and utility methods for editor coordinates. Implements saturated subtraction and consistent comparison across architectures.
UTF-16 variant of Point for positions measured in code units, providing the same arithmetic and ordering utilities. Aids interop with protocols using UTF-16 positions.
A wrapper type to carry unclipped dimensions over sum-tree summaries with arithmetic ops. Used to parameterize dimension aggregation without clipping semantics.

RSA-based token encryption/decryption supporting legacy PKCS1v15 and OAEP-SHA256, plus base64 serialization of keys and random token generation. Includes thorough tests for formats and URL-safe tokens.

Thin wrapper over a duplex WebSocket stream splitting sink/stream, with a send method and an in-memory channel utility for tests. Test channel simulates delays and half-open behavior to exercise robustness.
Data model for extension manifests and metadata describing provided capabilities, schema versions, and publication info. Serialized forms support filtering and presentation in extension systems.
Macros to generate typed message envelopes and request/response mappings, including entity-scoped message extraction. Centralizes boilerplate for strongly-typed RPC messaging.

Encodes/decodes protobuf Envelopes over WebSockets with zstd compression and Ping/Pong handling, maintaining a reusable buffer with capped capacity. Provides async read/write APIs and tests for buffer sizing behavior.
Notification enum with serde tagging and conversion to/from proto, separating kind/entity_id from JSON payload for storage/indexing. Tests ensure round-trip correctness and compact content.

Manages multiple RPC connections with keepalive, timeouts, multiplexed request/response channels (including streaming), and typed message dispatch. Provides connection IDs, IO loops, and graceful teardown of in-flight streams.

High-level, type-erased proto client supporting typed request/response, LSP request routing with timeouts, and dynamic message handlers bound to entities. Tracks pending LSP requests via global registries and dispatches to subscribed views.
Clock trait abstraction with a TestClock that can be manually advanced and controlled UTC time for deterministic tests. Supports advancing both Instant and DateTime.

Foreground and background executors over a Scheduler with Task wrappers, block_on/with_timeout, timers, and safe local spawning annotated with spawn-site for panic diagnostics. Bridges scheduling to runnable queues.
Defines the Scheduler trait, session scoping, and a Timer future, and re-exports clock/executor/test scheduler modules. Establishes the core interfaces used by executors and tests.

Deterministic, single-threaded test scheduler with controllable randomness, timers, waker tracing, parking policies, and foreground/background queues. Provides helpers to run/advance time and capture pending traces.
Unit tests validating executor behavior, ordering, timers, blocking semantics, and deterministic vs randomized execution. Exercises interop of foreground/background tasks and timeouts.

Initializes search feature modules and defines the search action set with bitflag options and UI integration. Converts between SearchQuery/Settings and SearchOptions and shows 'no more matches' toast.
Helpers to render search action buttons with focus/dispatch behavior and themed text input for embedded editors. Encapsulates Editor styling for search fields.
Status bar button that triggers Project Search when enabled via settings, with tooltip/action wiring. Hides itself when disabled.

Action registration infrastructure decoupling BufferSearchBar from callers via a registrar that wires actions to search bar lifecycle states. Supports Workspace-wide registration and conditional execution strategies.
SemanticVersion type with parsing, Display, ordering, and serde as a dotted string. Provides simple component accessors and robust error contexts.
Manages app session identity and persists window stack to a key-value store, exposing last session info. AppSession periodically detects changes and saves on quit for restore behavior.
Defines BaseKeymap options with OS-specific lists, asset paths, display names, and conversions to settings content. Implements Settings integration and VS Code import mapping.

Generic deep-merge trait with blanket impls for primitives, Option, Vec, maps, sets, and serde_json::Value, controlling settings composition semantics. Enables defaults layered by user/profile/project.
Bootstraps SettingsStore from embedded defaults, exposes asset accessors for defaults/keymaps, and tracks active settings profile. Defines WorktreeId and registers BaseKeymap handling.

Top-level settings model aggregating project/theme/workspace/editor/agent/etc., with per-OS/channel/profile overlays and language maps. Provides profile selection and language settings mutation helpers.
Watches settings files/dirs via Fs to stream content updates and provides a helper to update settings atomically. Includes a test default settings generator with neutral fonts/theme.
Loads and parses VS Code or Cursor settings JSON from platform-dependent locations, extracting typed values and mapping to Zed settings. Offers lenient parsing and convenience accessors.
Defines agent-related settings (enablement, docking, models, profiles, permissions, UI prefs) and nested types for providers and parameters. Includes convenient setters and JSON schema hints.

Comprehensive editor settings (cursor, UI, scrollbars, search, LSP, diagnostics, Jupyter, etc.) composed of nested content structs with defaults. Governs editor rendering, interactions, and integrations.

Language settings model with global defaults, per-language overrides, file-type associations, and feature flags, including merge logic that layers defaults and user overrides. Covers formatting, soft wrap, servers, and prediction controls.
Settings for language model providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, etc.), available models, capabilities, endpoints, and cache/limits. Structures per-provider options for agent/model selection.

States GPLv3 licensing for the fuzzy crate, requiring copyleft on redistribution/modification with patent protections and no warranty. This constrains how fuzzy matching utilities can be reused and shared.
Provides GPLv3 licensing for the git crate, enforcing copyleft obligations and including patent protections and warranty disclaimers. This affects redistribution and integration of VCS functionality.

Specifies GPLv3 licensing, imposing copyleft requirements and patent protections with no warranty for git hosting providers. This impacts how provider integrations are distributed in the architecture.
Declares GPLv3 licensing for the git UI, requiring copyleft for derivatives and including patent/anti-circumvention protections. This influences distribution and reuse of git UI components.
States GPLv3 licensing with copyleft obligations, patent protections, and warranty disclaimers for the go-to-line crate. This constrains redistribution and reuse of navigation features.
Provides GPLv3 terms for the google_ai crate, mandating copyleft requirements and including patent protections and no warranty. This affects integration and distribution of AI-related functionality.

Specifies Apache 2.0 licensing for gpui, granting permissive copyright and patent rights with NOTICE/attribution requirements and no warranty. This allows broad architectural reuse of the UI framework without copyleft constraints.

Declares Apache 2.0 licensing for gpui_macros, providing a permissive copyright and patent grant with attribution/NOTICE requirements and warranty disclaimers. This enables flexible integration of macros across the project.

Specifies Apache 2.0 licensing for gpui_tokio, offering permissive reuse with patent grant and attribution/NOTICE requirements and no warranty. This supports wide integration of Tokio-related UI utilities without copyleft limits.

Implements a Windows DirectWrite-based text system that manages font collections (system and in-memory), font selection, glyph metrics, and rasterization via a D3D11 GPU pipeline with shaders and blend/sampler state. It caches selections, handles locale, and recovers from GPU device loss while exposing the PlatformTextSystem interface.

Provides the Windows DirectX 11 renderer, creating devices, swap chains, render targets, pipelines, and global resources, and drawing scene batches including paths with MSAA. It integrates with DirectComposition when enabled and implements robust device-lost recovery to recreate resources and continue rendering.

Translates Win32 window messages into GPUI window behavior, handling sizing, DPI changes, input events, IME composition, paint, and device-lost notifications. It updates window state, triggers renderer resize, manages move/enter/leave loops, and dispatches app callbacks for lifecycle and input.

Implements the Wayland client and event loop integration, managing globals, seats, pointer/keyboard/IME input, clipboard/primary selection, cursors, data offers, outputs, and window mappings. It tracks modifiers, clicks, repeats, and dispatches events to GPUI windows with per-protocol feature support.

Provides the X11 client handling connections, XInput2 devices, keyboard layout/xkb, XIM IME integration, cursor caching, scroll axes state, and window focus/visibility. It maps X11 events to GPUI semantics, manages per-window cursor styles, and coordinates with the event loop and Blade GPU context.

Manages X11 window creation and interaction, including visual selection, atoms, raw window/display handles, and input/resize callbacks. It integrates the Blade renderer, configures window properties and decorations, and provides helper conversions (resize edges, visuals) and XCB flush/error handling.

Defines procedural macros that generate ergonomic style helper methods (e.g., visibility, margins, padding, positioning, overflow, cursor) for UI elements. It parses optional visibility config and emits method sets to mutate style fields consistently across components.

Implements the Keymap Editor UI and actions, including creating/editing/deleting bindings, conflict detection and filtering, and keystroke or text-based search. It integrates with the workspace, settings, and platform keyboard mapper, and emits updates via a global event channel.

A UI component for recording keystroke sequences with logic to intercept input, manage modifier transitions, and avoid conflicts with the stop-recording binding through timed sequence capture. It supports search mode, placeholder keystrokes, and exposes recorded sequences via events.

Defines the core Buffer model for text editing, including transactional edits, versioning, parsing scheduling, diagnostics, selections, remote collaboration operations, and snapshots. It coordinates with syntax mapping, LSP integration, diffing, and maintains consistent state for rendering and tools.

Unit tests covering Buffer behavior such as line ending normalization, synchronization across replicas, language selection, and custom file type mappings. They validate protocol serialization, diff tasks, and language registry resolution.

Crate entry for language features, exporting language registries, grammars, highlighting, outline, diffing, and LSP adapter scaffolding with cached server properties. It pools tree-sitter parsers/query cursors, initializes settings, and centralizes public API for language services.

Maintains layered syntax trees using tree-sitter with support for injections, captures, and pattern matching across languages, and efficiently interpolates layers on incremental edits. It exposes iterators over matches/captures and manages parse steps and depth-aware ranges for highlighting.

Integrates Amazon Bedrock as a language model provider, handling authentication/credentials storage, settings (regions, profiles, endpoints), model modes (default/thinking), and constructing streaming clients. It maintains provider state via GPUI entities and maps events and tool use for completions.

Implements the Zed Cloud LLM provider, managing authentication, token refresh, model discovery/defaults, and streaming completion events while reflecting server status headers and limits. It maintains provider state, reacts to user/session changes, and exposes UI settings integration.

Provides an LSP log viewer tool that displays per-server logs, RPC traces, and server info, integrating with the project log store and workspace UI. It reacts to new log entries, maintains the current server selection, and renders content via an editor with auto-scroll and folding for large messages.

Defines a Python (Ty) LSP adapter and manifest provider, discovering environments via pyproject.toml and configuring workspace settings accordingly. It manages server binary download/verification per-OS from GitHub, toolchain wiring, and normalizes completion metadata (e.g., Pyright sort text).

Implements the Rust (rust-analyzer) LSP adapter, including GitHub asset resolution per-platform, download/installation, and configuration. It sanitizes diagnostics/messages, provides markdown conversion, and generates rich completion labels using syntax highlighting for signatures and fields.

Core JSON-RPC LSP runtime that spawns/manages language server processes, handles message framing, request/response routing with timeouts, notification subscriptions, I/O handlers, and capability tracking. It exposes LanguageServer and related types, binary options, and an adapter-server capability bridge.

Renders markdown as a GPUI element with configurable styles, link handling, code block rendering (default or custom), selection/copy actions, and asynchronous parsing. It supports optional syntax highlighting via a language registry and efficient incremental updates for appended or replaced content.

Parses markdown into a structured representation using pulldown-cmark and HTML parsing for blocks, producing elements with source ranges, tables/lists, and code blocks annotated with languages. It builds a tree of parsed elements to drive a separate renderer.

Framework for migrating keymaps and settings using ordered tree-sitter query patterns and JSON transforms, computing non-overlapping edits and applying them safely. It centralizes versioned migrations and ensures idempotent, incremental upgrades of user configurations.

Implements a MultiBuffer that composes excerpts from one or more Buffers into a single view with diff overlays, row/range mapping, and event emission for edits and language changes. It maintains history/transactions, supports clipping and boundary queries, and integrates BufferDiff snapshots for VCS features.

Unit tests for MultiBuffer behavior, validating text composition from excerpts, diff statuses, boundary detection, clipping, and reactions to underlying buffer edits and excerpt mutations. They also exercise event emission and subscription handling.

Provides the Outline Panel UI that lists symbols and filesystem entries, supports searching/filtering, indentation guides, expansion/collapse, and integrates with editor buffers and themes for highlighting. It manages async fetching of outlines per excerpt and persists UI state.

Manages project buffers across local and remote modes, including loading/opening, syncing operations, sharing across peers, saving, and emitting lifecycle events. It coordinates with LSP handles, worktree store, and RPC to construct buffers from serialized state and stream operations.

Implements project-wide Git integration, tracking repositories, statuses, diffs (unstaged/uncommitted), conflicts, and coordinating background jobs for fetching, resets, and index writes. It bridges buffers with BufferDiffs, handles downstream updates, and exposes repository events for UI and tools.

Defines a Workspace Item that renders a remote peer’s screen via RemoteVideoTrackView, with event subscriptions to close when the track unsubscribes or the view requests it. Integrates with tab UI (icon, tooltip, content text), navigation history, focus handling, and supports cloning on split.

Implements a status bar that manages left/right StatusItemView widgets, rendering and updating them based on the active pane’s item. Handles insertion/removal, type-based lookup, and adapts styling for client window decorations.

Adds task scheduling to Workspace, resolving tasks to terminal spawns with remote-connection guards, inventory updates, debugger hooks, and error toasts. Provides helpers for starting debug sessions and direct terminal task spawning with async result handling.

Registers a dev action to open a ThemePreview Item that showcases theme colors, typography, and UI components for visual validation. Implements tab labeling, focus, and clone-on-split for the preview window.

Manages transient toast notifications with optional actions, auto-dismiss timers (pause/resume on hover), focus tracking, and overlay rendering animations. Exposes APIs to show/toggle/hide toasts and integrates with a RunAction to trigger toast actions.

Provides a composable toolbar framework where ToolbarItemView components choose their location (left/right/secondary/hidden) based on the active pane item and focus state. Renders primary and secondary sections and propagates pane activation and focus changes to items.

Defines WorkspaceSettings and TabBarSettings mapping to persisted settings and importing equivalents from VS Code, covering panes, docks, autosave, windows, and UI behaviors. Includes ActivePanelModifiers for pane appearance and accessors used across the workspace.

Models the serialized workspace (location, docks, panes) and provides deserialization to reconstruct pane trees, active items, and dock state, with DB (sqlez) bindings for DockStructure/DockData. Handles remote connection metadata and item restoration via SerializableItemRegistry.

Implements a layered IgnoreStack of Gitignore matchers (global and per-path) with repo-root awareness to determine file/dir exclusion, including special-casing .git. Traverses the stack to resolve matches, supporting hierarchical overrides and fallbacks.

Represents WorktreeSettings for file scanning (inclusions/exclusions) and privacy, offering path tests and VS Code import. Parses and normalizes glob path matchers to support performant ancestor-based checks.

Defines x.ai Model variants with IDs, display names, token limits, and capability flags (images, tools, parallel tool calls). Provides mapping from string IDs, defaults, and utility methods used by higher-level AI features.

Initializes diagnostics telemetry including uploading previous minidumps and, on macOS dev channels, monitoring main-thread hangs via a SIGUSR2 backtrace handler to report hang events. Integrates with remote projects to upload crash files and respects telemetry settings.

Builds the application menus (Zed, File, Edit, Selection, View, Go) wiring items to actions across settings, panels, layout, and system functions. Provides platform-specific entries and consolidated command palette and navigation items.

Registers a serializable ComponentPreview Item that lists and filters UI components, supports sectioning, navigation, and persistence of active page via a small DB. Integrates with Workspace to open the preview and ties into Item/tab UI behaviors.

Coordinates assignment of edit prediction providers (None, Copilot, Supermaven, Zed/Zeta2) to editors based on settings and user state, reacting to settings/user updates and editor lifecycle. Provides backward-compatible action aliases and registers buffers with providers.

Ensures single-instance behavior on macOS by binding a per-user, per-channel localhost TCP port and exchanging a handshake string. Falls back gracefully if binding fails and spawns a listener thread to respond to subsequent instances.

Implements a toolbar MigrationBanner that detects deprecated keymap/settings files, displays a dismissible notification with backup-and-update action, and listens for global migration events. Reads/writes settings/keymaps via Fs and migrator helpers.

Parses and routes open requests from URLs/CLI (including ssh, wsl, zed:// links, and dock actions), manages IPC with the CLI, and produces workspace openings with caret positioning and diffs. Exposes a global OpenListener channel and OS-specific listeners.

Renders a context-sensitive QuickActionBar for the active editor, surfacing search, code actions, assistant, diagnostics, inlay hints, minimap, and other toggles, with popover menus and tooltips. Reacts to settings, editor capabilities, and selection state.

Adds a QuickActionBar preview button that detects Markdown/SVG editors and dispatches open-preview or open-to-side actions, with tooltip hints and Alt-click behavior. Integrates with Workspace to resolve the active previewable item.

Implements a REPL menu in the QuickActionBar using Jupyter integration, showing kernel status, run/interrupt/clear actions, and kernel management. Adapts availability based on project locality, selection state, and session support.

Defines a broad set of application-wide actions (settings, UI, git, command palette, assistant, toast, etc.) with serde/schemars metadata and namespaces. Serves as the central action registry to enable loose coupling across crates and UI components.
Provides helpers for environment variables including a ZED_STATELESS flag and macros to define lazy EnvVar and boolean env flags. Normalizes empty values to None for consistent checks.

Custom UI element that renders an edit prediction diff with highlighted insertions/deletions and an active-line background, drawing a cursor indicator. Computes inline highlights from edits against an excerpt and paints within the editor theme.

Registers Zeta-related actions (rate completions, reset onboarding, open onboarding) and gates their discoverability via feature flags and AI disablement settings. Hooks into Workspace to toggle modals and updates command palette filtering dynamically.

Generates a compact prompt excerpt around the cursor by expanding to the largest syntax scope within token limits and falling back to line-based expansion, inserting start/cursor/end markers. Provides deterministic construction from a BufferSnapshot with tests.

Defines a modal introducing Edit Predictions, allowing users to choose Zed or Copilot providers and persisting the choice, with dismissal tracking. Integrates with Workspace modal lifecycle and focuses management.

Modal UI for reviewing and rating edit predictions, navigating the suggestion history, previewing diffs, and submitting feedback text. Wires actions for thumbs up/down, selection movement, and confirmation while syncing with Zeta state.

Represents an edit prediction tied to a buffer/snapshot, converting cloud responses into anchor-based edits and building EditPreviews; includes robust interpolation logic to reconcile model edits with user edits since the snapshot. Provides diff-based edit extraction and grouping helpers with tests.

Implements the Zeta2 EditPredictionProvider integrating with editors to request, throttle, and present suggestions, grouping nearby edits and handling accept/discard cycles. Tracks pending requests, respects user/account state, and computes nearest edits by cursor proximity.

Core Zeta2 service managing projects, buffer registration, syntax indexing, options, token refresh, and current predictions, with event tracking and debug info streaming. Coordinates prediction replacement logic and initialization/waiting for indexing.

Provides a developer inspector Item for Zeta2 to visualize context, prompts, timings, and adjust options live, replaying predictions for quick iteration. Hooks into Workspace to open a split view and listens for debug events from Zeta2.

Initializes a headless app environment for the Zeta CLI, setting up settings, HTTP client, project, user store, languages, and node runtime. Prepares extension infrastructure and language services for command-line operations.

Implements the Zeta CLI with subcommands to print context, build Zeta2 prompts/requests, run predictions, and collect retrieval stats, parsing cursor/paths and optionally using language servers. Manages project/worktree setup, buffer opening, and formatting output modes.
Parses environment logging filters (global level and per-directive levels) into a structured EnvFilter, with validation and tests. Supports both max-level specification and module/scope directives.

Runtime log filtering that merges settings, environment, and defaults into a scope-aware map, caching the maximum enabled level and answering enablement checks per scope/module. Supports dynamic refresh and hierarchical scope matching.

Outputs logs to stdout/stderr or a rotating file with ANSI level coloring and timestamped formatting, tracking file size for rotation. Provides flushing and structured formatting including scope/module display.

Sets up the global logger, processes env config, and provides logging macros (trace/debug/info/warn/error), scoped loggers, and a Timer utility. Bridges to the sink and filter layers to implement scope-aware, dynamic logging across crates.

Defines the LspCommand trait and helpers to translate high-level project requests into LSP parameters and proto messages, gate them by server capabilities, and map responses back to project data. It also declares concrete command types (rename, definitions, references, hover, completions, code actions, diagnostics) and formatting/URI utilities. This is the core abstraction bridging the editor’s model with language servers and collaboration.

Implements the unified LSP store architecture, with a LocalLspStore that manages language server lifecycles, capabilities, watchers, diagnostics, formatting, and per-buffer snapshots, and a façade for local/remote interaction. It orchestrates server selection per worktree, tracks opened buffers across servers, and aggregates workspace edits and diagnostics.

The Project entity coordinates worktrees, buffers, language servers, tasks, terminals, debug sessions, and remote collaboration modes, exposing events and operations that drive the workspace. It integrates with LspStore and other stores, manages client state (local/shared/remote), and routes ordered messages affecting buffers and language servers.

Integration tests validate project behaviors including blocking, symlink handling, .editorconfig overriding .zed settings, git provider settings propagation, and project-specific settings management. They exercise the end-to-end interactions between filesystem, language registry, and project stores.

Tracks and aggregates tasks and debug scenarios from multiple sources (user input, worktree .zed files, global files, language/LSP providers), and provides context-aware listings and scheduling history. It builds task contexts from active buffers/worktrees and exposes functions to render and retrieve scenarios per source.

Defines traits to encapsulate DAP requests and proto translation, including cacheability and capability checks, and implements step-related commands (Next, StepIn, StepOut) with conversions to/from proto messages. This abstraction simplifies sending DAP requests and handling responses consistently.

Manages a debugger session lifecycle, client creation and child connections, message multiplexing, breakpoints synchronization, and thread/stack state tracking. It coordinates DAP commands, handles events (stopped/output), and updates breakpoint verification and UI-facing session state.

Implements the project panel’s file tree UI, including selection, expansion, auto-folding, drag-and-drop, diagnostics highlighting, context menus, and actions like opening, renaming, deleting, and splitting panes. It maintains per-worktree visible entries, state persistence, and integrates with workspace operations.

Visual and interaction tests for the project panel verify visible entries, opening files, exclusion filters, and auto-collapse behavior under various worktree structures and settings. These ensure panel rendering and actions behave correctly.

Provides UI flows to connect to remote servers (SSH/WSL), pick projects, edit nicknames, and persist selections in settings, then open workspaces with existing connections. It watches SSH config, manages prompts, and interacts with RemoteClient and Workspace.

Implements a RemoteClient that establishes and maintains SSH/WSL connections with heartbeat monitoring, reconnect strategies, and multiplexed RPC channels. It encapsulates state transitions, delegates for password and binary download, and uniquely identifies connections for session reuse.

Tests exercise remote editing workflows including buffer opening/saving, file system changes propagation, renames, diffs, project search, and settings synchronization between client and server. They validate headless server tracking of shared buffers and precedence of server settings.

High-performance rope implementation backed by a sum-tree of fixed-capacity chunks, with operations for append, replace, slicing, pushing large text, and robust UTF-8 char-boundary handling. It optimizes chunk merging/splitting, supports parallel extension, and exposes row/point conversions.

Implements the Rules Library window and picker for managing prompts/rules, including actions (new, delete, duplicate, toggle default), token counting, saving, and integration with inline assist. It handles opening/activating a dedicated window and renders categorized search results.

Implements a buffer search bar with replace, selection-aware searching, and toggles for case, whole word, and regex, synchronizing matches with active searchable items. It manages history, UI rendering with toolbars, error feedback, and focuses between query/replacement inputs.

Provides project-wide search view and toolbar, managing queries, replacements, filters (include/exclude patterns, ignored files), and results aggregation across buffers via a MultiBuffer. It registers workspace actions, persists settings per project, and supports navigation and copy operations.

Parses and loads keymap JSON sections with context predicates and bindings, supports partial failure with accumulated errors, and integrates custom validators via inventory. It generates JSON schemas for actions, maps keystrokes to actions, and loads built-in keymaps with metadata.

Provides algorithms to update or replace JSON values in text while preserving formatting and comments using tree-sitter queries and range-based edits. It supports nested object diffs, key replacement, array handling, and whitespace/comma-aware removal, producing pretty-printed replacements.

Central settings store that merges defaults, user, server, extension, and local project settings with editorconfig, registers typed settings, and provides global and path-scoped retrieval/override. It tracks changes, updates values asynchronously, and exposes APIs to import VSCode equivalents.

Implements the settings UI window and dynamic field renderer, mapping setting fields by type to UI components and selecting the file scope to edit. It renders pages of settings, integrates with SettingsStore, and supports editing and persisting changes.

Wraps alacritty_terminal to implement the terminal model, actions, event loop integration, scroll behavior, selection, vi mode, hyperlink detection, and rendering parameters. It defines bounds, error reporting, and a builder for display-only terminals, with extensive input/output handling.

Detects URLs and path-like targets in terminal content using regex-based searches across the visible grid, including special Python tracebacks, and sanitizes trailing punctuation/parentheses. It computes match bounds and trims decorations to yield openable targets.

GPUI element that lays out and paints terminal content, batching adjacent cells into text runs and merging background regions to minimize rectangles. It tracks layout state (cursor, highlights, hyperlink tooltips) and renders with per-cell metrics for performance.

Implements the terminal panel managing panes, split controls, zoom, tab bar buttons (including assistant), and serialization of layout. It wires workspace actions to open/new terminals and toggles focus, applying UI menus per pane.

TerminalView integrates the terminal with the workspace, handling focus, blinking cursor, breadcrumbs, embedded/scrollable modes, context menus, and search events. It registers actions to deploy terminals, handles hover tooltips for paths/URLs, scrolling, and serialization via persistence.

Implements the Buffer with rope-backed visible/deleted text, edit history, transactions, grouping, undo/redo stacks, and operation queues for collaborative edits. It manages versions, subscriptions, insertion slices, and provides APIs for transactional editing and history merging.

Defines default light and dark theme color palettes for UI elements, editor, and terminal, using color scales and system colors. It provides version-control status colors and various component-specific hues derived from neutral and accent scales.

Adapter that exposes an MCP context server tool as an assistant_tool::Tool, adapting input schemas for model formats and invoking CallTool via the context server client. It aggregates text outputs, warns on non-text content, enforces confirmation, and runs asynchronously through gpui tasks.

Manages the active set of agent context handles (files, directories, symbols, threads, rules, URLs, images), assigning IDs, preventing duplicates, and emitting updates. Integrates with Project to open buffers/images and respects directory inclusion, supporting creation/removal and conversion from threads.

Tracks and presents recently opened entries (threads and saved contexts), sorting by last update and persisting a small deque to disk with debounce and legacy format handling. Exposes convenience views for UI and supports list maintenance (push, replace, remove).

Core thread orchestration that wires Project, ToolWorkingSet, and PromptStore to manage threads, system prompts, and MCP context server tools. Subscribes to project/prompt updates, reloads shared system prompts per worktree and default user rules, and tracks serialized thread metadata and tool IDs.

Tracks tool use lifecycle per assistant message, reconstructing from serialized messages and maintaining pending, completed, and errored tool states with UI labels and icons. Supports cancellation, card deserialization, and derives needs_confirmation/status based on tools and results.

Represents a runtime agent profile tied to a ToolWorkingSet and computes enabled tools based on AgentSettings (including context server presets and global flags). Provides profile creation, listing, and test coverage for MCP tool enablement behavior.

Initializes an embedded MCP server exposing placeholder tools for listing history, memory operations, and indirect context tool calls, and writes its socket path to a file for external access. Tool implementations are schema-annotated and currently return informative stub responses.

Defines Agent v2 thread persistence format with upgrader from Agent v1, converting segments and tool uses/results while preserving token usage and metadata. Provides a shared, async-initialized ThreadsDatabase wrapper with typed DataType binding for storage.

Aggregates history across ACP threads and local text threads, producing sorted entries with mention URIs and a recently-opened list persisted via a key-value store. Supports reloading from the database and operations to open/delete text threads and delete ACP threads.
Embeds and renders Handlebars templates (notably the system prompt) with strict mode and a custom contains helper. Produces prompts from a ProjectContext and available tool list.

Generates JSON Schemas for tool inputs tailored to the model’s required format, converting Option and oneOf constructs to a simpler OpenAPI-like subset. Provides a transform to inline subschemas and normalize type fields.

Implements an AgentServer for the native Zed Agent that creates a NativeAgent connection using project, history, templates, and prompt store. Integrates with the agent server infrastructure and provides tests via common e2e harness.
Exports all built-in agent tools and enumerates their names to avoid collisions with MCP tools. Serves as the central registry module for tool imports in agent2.

Maintains a registry of running context servers and dynamically loads their tools, wrapping each as an AnyAgentTool with schema adaptation and remote execution via CallTool. Reacts to server status changes to refresh or remove tool sets.

Tool to copy files or directories within the project, resolving project paths, executing via Project API, and returning a confirmation message. Runs asynchronously and validates source and destination are within the project.
Tool to create a directory (recursively) at a project-relative path, validating scope and returning a confirmation. Uses Project APIs and runs as an async task.

Tool to delete a file or directory recursively, streaming traversal, opening buffers for ActionLog deletion tracking, and performing the deletion via Project. Validates project scope and reports progress/errors.

Tool to summarize project diagnostics or list errors/warnings for a specific file, opening buffers as needed and formatting severity and line information. Falls back to project-wide summaries when no path is provided.
Tool to fetch a URL and return content as Markdown, converting HTML (with special Wikipedia handlers), JSON, or plaintext, and enforcing authorization. Handles HTTP errors and content-type detection.

Tool to glob-search project paths across worktrees with pagination, path-style awareness, and include-pattern matching, emitting resource links via event stream. Returns both structured output and LLM-friendly text.

Regex-based content search tool over project files with include/exclude matchers, privacy/exclusion checks, pagination, and context-aware snippets using parse and syntax ranges. Streams results and composes readable markdown summaries.
Tool to list directory contents within the project, respecting global/worktree exclusion and privacy settings and handling common degenerate inputs. Outputs separate folder and file sections.
Tool to move or rename files/directories inside the project, selecting rename vs move labeling based on paths and returning a confirmation. Validates scope and executes via Project APIs.
Simple utility tool returning the current datetime in UTC or local time in RFC 3339 format. Intended for explicit user requests to know the current time.
Tool to open a file or URL with the OS default application after authorization, resolving project-relative paths to absolute when possible. Reports success and handles failures gracefully.

Tool to read file contents (or images) from the project with optional line ranges, enforcing global/worktree privacy/exclusion policies and emitting location metadata. Falls back to an outline for large files, logs reads in ActionLog, and updates agent location.

Tool to execute a shell one-liner in a project worktree via a ThreadEnvironment, requiring authorization and returning combined output with truncation and exit status handling. Validates working directory context and streams terminal linkage to the UI.
Non-executing tool to capture and display free-form planning or reasoning content as part of a turn. Updates tool call content and returns a simple completion message.

Tool that performs web search via the active provider (Zed Cloud only), streaming result links and metadata into the UI and serializing the response for LLM consumption. Handles unavailable providers and error titling.

Defines the input schema for an indirect call_context_tool that routes to specific context-compaction tools (list_history or memory) with optional raw arguments. Enables a single exported MCP tool to target vetted internal tools.

Implements an ExternalAgentToolExecutor that deserializes arguments and runs internal compaction tools (list_history, memory, or call_context_tool) against a Thread, returning ToolResponse values. Bridges the context_server adapter to internal tools without introducing cyclic deps.

Tool that lists conversation messages by index with character-capped previews, a JSON summary block, and optional full message markdown, clamping limits for safety. Reads from the current Thread and formats as a table for compact navigation.

Defines a memory management tool API (store/load/list/restore/prune) for conversation compaction, currently returning placeholder text indicating pending integration. Establishes input schema and titles for future implementation.

Manages lifecycle of external agent processes over ACP: spawning with IO pipes, initializing client connection, session management (including MCP servers per project), auth handling, and mode control. Streams stderr, kills child on drop, and integrates with registry and fore/back executors.

Defines the AgentServer trait and delegate plumbing to connect agents for a project, including default mode management and environment proxy injection. Provides downcasting and shared helpers used by concrete server implementations.

AgentServer implementation for Claude Code that resolves commands via the store, injects proxy settings, applies default mode, and connects using ACP, persisting mode changes to settings. Uses standard server delegation and optional login task.
AgentServer implementation for Codex that fetches its external command, sets proxy env, applies default mode, and connects via ACP. Includes common e2e tests integration.

Generic AgentServer for user-defined external agents that looks up configuration by name, persists default mode, and connects via ACP with proxy and status/new version wiring. Provides a terminal icon and simple identity.

Shared end-to-end test harnesses for AgentServer implementations covering basic message flow, path mentions, tool calls with permission flow, and cancellation. Spins up temp projects and asserts key behaviors via AcpThread entries.

AgentServer for the Gemini CLI that injects SURFACE and API key env, loads proxy settings, and connects via ACP with default mode support. Includes local command helper for tests and common e2e tests.

Settings-side AgentProfile and AgentProfileSettings with tool enables and context server presets, helpers to create profiles and list available ones, and serialization to SettingsContent. Provides builtin profile IDs and simple enable checks.

Defines global AgentSettings (models, profiles, UI, behavior flags, completion mode) and integrates with the Settings system, including VS Code import and model temperature lookup. Exposes default IDs and serialization helpers used across the agent.

Implements a UI data table with support for uniform list rendering, focus/scroll management, and column resizing via draggable handles and double-click reset. Manages column width fractions and visible widths through TableColumnWidths.

Provides cross-platform path utilities including home-directory compaction, hidden-file/extension detection, UNIX/WINDOWS byte-to-path conversion, and local-to-WSL path translation. Includes a SanitizedPath wrapper and PathStyle helpers for joining/splitting remote-style paths.

Defines Vim command actions and option parsing (e.g., :set), wiring them to editor/workspace behaviors like soft wrap, line numbers, and search case sensitivity. Wraps actions with ranges/counts and integrates palette and shell command invocations.

Declares the Motion enum and related actions, encapsulating cursor and selection navigation across lines, words/subwords, sentences, brackets, windows, and find/sneak operations. Establishes motion kinds and parameters (e.g., smartcase) forming the core navigation algorithms.

Registers and implements normal-mode editing commands including insert/delete/yank/change/join/undo/redo and Helix variants. Coordinates counts, forced motions, and selection transformations against the editor.

Implements Vim text objects and selection algorithms, finding quotes/brackets and syntax ranges relative to the caret using buffer/display snapshots. Provides actions to select various objects and utilities to locate enclosing or nearest delimiters.

Defines Vim modes, operators, registers, marks, and global state, including recording/replaying actions and mark persistence via the database. Tracks counts, last-find, focused Vim, and integrates with workspace/project buffer events.

Adds, deletes, and changes surrounding delimiters based on motions/objects or current selection, handling whitespace and visual modes. Performs editor transactions to insert/remove bracket pairs and updates selections accordingly.

GPUI-based integration tests covering Vim mode toggling, motions, search, indentation, selections, command palette interactions, and Neovim-backed flows. Validates edge cases and platform-specific behaviors.

Top-level Vim integration defining actions, counts, registers, mode switching, and workspace-level handlers; wires initialization into the App and workspace. Coordinates menu interactions, pane actions, and toggling Vim mode.

Implements visual-mode actions (toggle visual/line/block, yank/delete) and selection operations like select-next/previous and syntax node navigation. Handles motion updates for visual selections and restoration of previous visual states.
Defines the Item trait and tab UI behavior, item/settings models, and lifecycle events (save/close/reload). Establishes how items render content, tooltips, persistence, and interact within panes.

Manages pane state and tab bar behavior, supporting item activation, splitting/joining, pinning/preview, navigation, and search deployment via a rich set of actions/events. Bridges UI interactions with workspace settings and item handling.

Implements workspace persistence using a SQLite-based domain, serializing window bounds, pane groups, items, and breakpoints with custom bind/column types. Defines schema migrations and provides a WorkspaceDb for reading/writing state.

Central workspace orchestrator handling windows, panes, docks, actions (open/save/move/split), notifications, and integration with remote connections and persistence. Coordinates UI themes, sessions, and item workflows.

Represents local/remote worktrees, performing filesystem scanning, symlink handling, git repository discovery, and ignore processing while maintaining snapshots of entries. Supports external directories, incremental refresh, and event streaming.
Tests worktree traversal, circular symlink handling, external symlink expansion, and case-only renames using fake/real filesystems. Verifies entry lists and emitted path change events.

Application entry point that parses CLI arguments, initializes paths/logging/crash handling, enforces single-instance behavior, and launches GPUI windows or prompts on failure. Bootstraps services, sessions, and environment before running.

Defines app-level actions/menus and window options, opening settings/tasks/logs and bundled files, and orchestrates workspace creation and common UI flows. Includes development-only crash/panic hooks and title bar behavior.

Implements Zeta's edit prediction feature: tracking events, assembling input excerpts, sending requests, receiving edits, and interpolating predictions with user edits. Manages LLM token refresh, upsell state, and per-project history/notifications.
Links to the project's Code of Conduct hosted at zed.dev/code-of-conduct.
Provides the default pull request template detailing issue linkage and release notes.
Bash script that generates a CSV of cargo licenses using cargo-about and a Handlebars template, producing a sorted output in assets.
Contains the ISC license text for Lucide icons used in assets.
Documents pending breaking changes to the extension API to batch in a future release, e.g., renaming SlashCommand fields.
Static header text for auto-generated notifications indicating files changed since last read.
Guidance for generating a detailed conversation summary with structured headings and bullet points.
Instruction to generate a concise 3–7 word title for a conversation without preamble.
Explains a tool that copies files or directories recursively within the project, preferring efficiency over manual read/write.
Describes a tool to create directories (including parents) in the project similar to mkdir -p.
Documents a tool that deletes files or directories recursively and returns confirmation.
Explains a tool for retrieving diagnostics for a file or the project, with examples and usage guidelines.
Describes a tool for creating or editing files, advising prior reading and directory verification before use.
Documents a tool that fetches a URL and returns its content as Markdown.
Explains a glob-based path search tool with pagination and guidance on when to use it over grep.
Documents a regex-based content search tool with pagination and best-practice guidance; not for path searches.
Describes a tool for listing directory contents, recommending grep or path search for codebase queries.
Explains a tool to move or rename files/directories within the project without altering contents.
Describes a tool that opens files or URLs using the OS default application, to be used only on explicit user request.
Explains a tool that reports files modified since last agent access, serving as notifications without requiring immediate action.
Static header text used for notifications listing files changed since last read.
Describes a tool to read file contents and cautions against reading paths not previously mentioned.
Documents a tool that runs a shell one-liner and returns combined output, with guidance on cwd, long-running commands, and statelessness.
Describes a tool for thinking/planning or brainstorming without executing actions or making changes.
Explains how the Project manages breakpoint lifecycle and serialization, and how breakpoint data is sent to debug adapters.
Prompt instructing how to write clear, stylistically correct Git commit messages following best practices.
Example Zero-Clause BSD license text used for license detection and testing.
Example Apache-2.0 license snippet for reference in license detection.
Example ISC license text used in license detection tests.
Example zlib license text used for detection and pattern matching.
Pattern file specifying match ranges and phrases to detect the Zero-Clause BSD license in text.
Pattern file for detecting references to the Apache-2.0 license including the canonical URL.
Pattern file defining phrases to identify ISC license text.
